events.name: BayAreaChess Open Rapid @ Milpitas (Feb 16, 2026)
events.sourceText:
BayAreaChess Open Rapid @ Milpitas (Feb 16, 2026)
Sonesta Silicon Valley Event Center
Monday, February 16, 2026
Event Overview
Jump into fast-paced action in the Open Rapid at the 2026 US Amateur Team West National Championship! This USCF-rated event blends speed and strategy, offering players of all levels a fun, competitive challenge alongside the main championship.
Register here
You must log in or sign up before you can register.
Online registration closes at 12:00 a.m. the day of the tournament.
Onsite registration is subject to availability ($14 additional fee incurred).
Late fees applied starting February 12 or when reaching capacity.
Schedule
Rounds: 5 rounds
Time Control: G/10 d2
Round Times: 6:55 p.m. to 9:25 p.m. (Rolling schedule)
( Mandatory check-in by 6:40 p.m.)
Sections
Players will be placed into groups of 6 based on their February 2026 Published Supplement Quick rating.
Prizes
For every group, 1st place winners earn $70, 2nd place winners earn $40.
A player who withdraws during the tournament is not eligible for prizes.
Fees
Entry fee: $33
Discount for BayAreaChess Membership Subscribers ( More Info )
Late fees, starting: Feb. 12: +$7
Onsite fee: +$14
BayAreaChess Membership discounts are NOT redeemable for late and onsite fees.
Withdrawals
Withdrawals are eligible for a partial refund, subject to the following deductions: until Feb. 11, 4% processing fee.
from Feb. 12 to Feb. 13, $7 withdrawal fee + 4% processing fee.
from Feb. 14 onward, NO REFUND will be issued.
Only withdrawals made before or on Feb. 13 are eligible for refund.
Change requests
After registration, changes can be requested at bayareachess.com/changeform and are subject to the following fees: until Feb. 12, $7 change fee.
on Feb. 13, $15 change fee.
Other requirements
USCF membership must be active.
More information available here .
Address: Sonesta Silicon Valley Event Center
1800 Barber Ln
Milpitas , CA 95035
United States
Sections:
Grand Prix Points:
Prize Fund: $110 per group
FIDE Rated: No
Handicap Accessible: Yes
Residency Restriction: No
Online Event: No

CCL President Day Scholastic
Northside Library Meeting Room
Monday, February 16, 2026
Event Overview
ROUND 1 STARTS AT 10 AM.
Chess sets and clocks are provided.
Registration https://cclchess.com/president-day-scholastic-registration/
Format: 4 Round Swiss, no elimination, 1 half-point bye allowed if declared before round 1. Games are USCF-rated for K-12 Open, K-12 U1200, K-12 U900, K-12 U600, K-6 U300 sections which require current US Chess membership. Games are not USCF rated in Nonrated sections which do not require US Chess membership.
Time Control: G45, d5 for K-12 Open & U1200 sections; G30, d5 for other sections. Round 1 starts at 10 am for ALL sections. Check out specific section's schedule on site.
Sections: K-12 Open, K-12 U1200, K-12 U900, K-12 U600, K-6 U300, K-3 Nonrated, 4-8 Nonrated
Awards: Individual trophies for anyone scoring 2.5 out of 4 in each section. Team trophies for top 2 overall best school teams across sections. Medals for all.
General Entry Fees: $40 by Feb 9, then $50 until Feb 16. Discounted entry fees applied to CCL active students.
Acceptable Payments: major credit cards, Zelle ( [email protected] ), Venmo (@Jeff-Shen-23) or cash.

HCC February Action Quads ($300, b/24; $50/quad winner)
Play More Chess Academy - Home of the Hamden Chess Club
Monday, February 16, 2026
Event Overview
HCC February Action Quads ($300 in prizes, b24)
DATE & TIME: Monday, February 16, 2026; 6:30~9:00PM (Round 1 at 6:30PM, subsequent rounds ASAP. End time: Between 8:30-9:30PM depending on quad).
LOCATION: Play More Chess Academy, Home of the Hamden Chess Club, 1227 Whitney Ave., Hamden, CT 06517
TIME CONTROL: G/25, d5
EVENT FORMAT: Quads - Players placed in groups of four by their US Chess regular rating to ensure closer matchups. 3 Rounds.
ELIGIBILITY: A current USCF membership is required to register for this tournament (go to https://new.uschess.org/join-us-chess to join or renew). This quad tournament open to all adult players ages 13+ of any rating level, including Unrated. (Players who are under 13 who have a USCF rating of 700+ are also eligible for this tournament). This tournament provides an opportunity to play three regular rated games in one week day evening.
BYES: None available as this is a three-round Quads tournament. All participants are expected to play all three games.
WHEN: HCC Monthly Action Quads occur once a month, usually occur on the 3rd Monday of the month (with the other Monday evenings open for casual play). Note: Jan 2026 it will be held on the 4th Monday (and no casual play on 3rd Monday). Please check the Events Calendar to confirm dates of upcoming HCC tournaments.
ENTRY FEE: $20-$35 (Discounts for Early Entry and HCC members) Early entry - $20 HCC members (by 11:59PM Tuesday prior - non-HCC members, additional $10); Free early entry for titled players (GMs, IMs and NMs) with no entry fee deducted from any prize. Then $30, by 11:59PM Thursday prior; Thereafter, $35 until 6:00PM day of tournament.
PRIZES: $300, b/24; ($50 to the winner of each quad. A 2nd place prize of $25 added if a swiss section of 5-7 players is needed due to number of players not divisible by four).
SECTIONS: Participants grouped into Quads (groups of four) at close of registration based on USCF regular rating.
REGISTRATION AND CURRENT ENTRY LIST: https://caissachess.net/online-registration/index/8305
ENTRY DEADLINE: 6:00PM day of tournament
Join HCC today and Save - Member benefits include discounts on OTB tournaments, free weekly online tournaments with prizes, free casual play evenings each week.
Adults only $130/year; Scholastic (K-12) and Senior Citizens (65+) only $110/year.
PARKING AND TRANSPORTATION: Free parking is available on behind the Academy, including free street parking on Putnam/Lake Drive that goes behind Play More Chess Academy. ( See Parking Map ). CT Transit bus stop is adjacent to Academy at intersection of Putnam/Whitney Ave.
ADDITIONAL NOTES: All players must be current members of US Chess (go to USCHESS.org to join or renew your USCF membership/membership ID number). Must register for HCC tournaments in advance. Sets, boards, clocks, score sheets are provided - must use our equipment. Pens and scoresheets also available. Quad tournament players are not permitted to withdraw mid-event - participants must plan to play all three rounds. Space is limited to 36 players.
WITHDRAWALS/CONTACT: If you cannot make it to the tournament, and have to withdraw, email: Click here to show mail address . A request for a refund may be made no later than Sunday, 11:59PM (day before tournament). Refunds for this tournament must be requested by email and are subject to a $15 cancellation fee. For contact during the event please email: Click here to show mail address as PMCA phone will be silenced.
Address: 1227 Whitney Ave
Hamden , CT 06517
United States

Presidents' Day Online Open Action
lichess.org
Monday, February 16, 2026
Event Overview
Register here: https://caissachess.net/online-registration/index/8440
Monday (Presidents' Day), February 16th at 2 pm Eastern Time (1 pm CT, 12/noon MT, or 11 am PT)
This tournament will use Swiss pairings.
The time control will be game in 30 minutes with a 5-second increment . There will be four rounds. Rounds will be held at ( Eastern Time ): 2 pm, 3:20 pm, 4:40 pm, and 6 pm. The tournament will last for approximately 5 hours.
This event will be rated under the USCF online regular (slow) rating system . The tournament will be run on lichess.org .
This tournament is open to both children and adults of any age or rating.
Before signing up for the tournament, please register for a lichess.org account (it's free!) if you do not have an existing account. If you have any issues try watching this"> video we originally made for our scholastic tournaments about how to register an account on lichess: XTr_tAh7JeQ">
There will be two sections: Open and Under 1300 . These sections are determined by over-the-board USCF-regular rating. For example, a player with a rating of 1350 would belong in the Open section, a player rated 1200 would belong in the Under 1300 section, and so forth. Unrated players can play in any section. If you don't know which section you belong in, feel free to contact us.
All participants must be active members of the US Chess Federation.
Players can withdraw from the event at any time by pressing the "withdraw" button.
Prizes : Plaques for 1st, and trophies for 2nd and 3rd in both sections. All plaques and trophies will be inscribed with the winner's name. Tiebreaks are calculated based on the Sonneborn–Berger method, after which we use lichess performance ratings as a secondary tiebreak. 1st-place trophies are always awarded to players with a perfect score, even in the event of a tie. If you live outside of the contiguous United States, we might not be able to mail your trophy due to the increased shipping costs for international orders (or we may ask the foreign player to pay a shipping fee).
After you register, you will receive an email from us with instructions on how to join the tournament online. If you don't receive the email, please check your spam folder by typing the word instructions into your spam or junk folder.
We encourage players to complete the registration process and join the tournament online before 1:45 pm ET. If you're late to the tournament you could end up missing round 1!
Players will not be required to join a Zoom call during the tournament, but we will monitor the games very closely to ensure fair play. Lichess has an excellent algorithm for detecting cheating, and we will also do a post-tournament fair-play inspection. If a participant's account is flagged for cheating by lichess, we have the prerogative to submit the player's games as losses for USCF-rating purposes, or (in rare cases) annul the games.
The entry fee is $20 by 11:59pm ET on Sunday 2/15/2026 and $25 on Monday 2/16/2026
Online computer analysis of all games will be possible immediately after the tournament! See our video about how to analyze your games on lichess: Tv1Kx0yEM10">
If you have any questions, don't hesitate to reach out to DMV Chess at 703-415-6600 or Click here to show mail address

events.name: Charlotte Chess Center Tuesday Night Action
events.sourceText:
Charlotte Chess Center Tuesday Night Action
Charlotte Chess Center (Main/South)
weekly on Tuesday, starting from Tuesday, March 11, 2014, forever
Event Overview
OVERVIEW
Tuesday Night Action is one US Chess-rated game every Tuesday night, completely free for CCC members. This is a great way for players to get weekly rated practice. The Top and U1600 Sections are also FIDE-rated - offering the only free weekly FIDE-rated game in the whole country. In addition, there is a free lecture before the games begin.
HOW IT WORKS
CCC opens Tuesdays at 5:45pm
Lecture with FM Peter Giannatos prior to rated games starting at 6:00 pm
Players must register weekly and in advance using the online registration system
Each Tuesday evening will be limited to the first 62 players to register
TNA registration will close at 6:30pm if not already full
Once spots are filled, players may email events Click here to show mail address to be placed on the waitlist.
​REQUIREMENTS
Players must be members of the CCC
Players must have a USChess membership
Open to all players in grades 9-12 and adults
Students in grades K-8 must be rated over 900
K-8 players rated under 900 - See Monday Action Quads , Wednesday Action Quads , Friday Action Quads , and Sunday Action Quads
​START TIME
Lecture: 6:00pm
Game: 7:00pm
GAMES
1 round weekly, rated at the end of the month
​ SECTIONS
TOP (1600+)
Under 1600
Under 1300
​ PRIZES
2.5/3.0 score required for TNA tournaments with 3 weeks or 4.0/5.0 score required for TNA tournaments with 5 weeks.
Free entries must be used for Monday Action Quads , Wednesday Action Quads , Friday Action Quads , and Sunday Action Quads within 1 month.
Not transferrable to other events or players.
Section winners will receive a voucher for CCC merch.
TIME CONTROL
Top Section: G/80, inc/10 - FIDE and US Chess Rated
U1600 Section: G/60, inc/10 - FIDE and US Chess Rated
U1300 Section: G/60, inc/10 - US Chess Rated
ENTRY FEE
Free, must be a CCC Member ​ - CCC membership only $50/year - join today !​
OTHER NOTES​​
Top and U1600 Sections are FIDE-rated - FIDE rules apply, except for US Chess penalties for cell phone infractions.
Tournament Directors will accelerate pairings to pair players close in rating when possible
Most recent "live" US Chess regular ratings used for all sections to ensure close matchups
Open to high schoolers and adults of any rating, including unrated
All players must use CCC equipment - wooden sets and digital clocks are provided
PRIZES
The top adult (18 or older) in each section will win a $25 gift card to USCF Sales .
The top junior (under 18) in each section will win a $25 gift card to USCF Sales .
All perfect scores (with perfect attendance) will receive a 3-month CCC membership extension.
See special notes on site for tiebreak rules.
The Charlotte Chess Center’s Main/South Location is conveniently located off of I-485 and Pineville-Matthews Road. CCC’s Main/South Branch serves both North Carolina and South Carolina. Regulars join in from Ballantyne, Pineville, SouthPark, Matthews, Mint Hill, Waxhaw, Weddington, Steele Creek, Fort Mill, Tega Cay, Rock Hill, Lake Wylie and South Charlotte.
Address: 10700 Kettering Drive
Unit E
Charlotte , NC 28226
United States

events.sourceText:
Climb The Rating Ladder Online Courses (Rated Games & Analysis)
Online
weekly on Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday, starting from Friday, May 1, 2020, forever
Event Overview
Climb the Rating Ladder Online Courses
By DMV Chess since May 2020!
OVERVIEW
Register here: https://www.dmvchess.com/courses-register
Students play one USCF-online-regular-rated game per week, after which a professional chess coach will help students analyze their games together as a group. When time permits, the coach will also give the class puzzles and lectures on tactics and strategy. Coaches are all experienced chess players who have a passion for teaching.
Time control: game in 25 minutes with a 5-second increment
Games submitted to the USCF for rating at the end of every month
Open to scholastic players from any geographical location
Wednesday class exclusively for adults
Active USCF membership required
Class participation strongly encouraged
Groups meet online on different days for two hours .
Schedule (Eastern Time):
Monday class from 6:30 pm to 8:30 pm- (designed for 400 to 1000 USCF)
Tuesday class from 6 pm to 8 pm- (designed for 400 to 1000 USCF)
Wednesday (Adults) class from 8 pm to 10 pm- (Open)
Friday class from 6 pm to 8 pm- (designed for 400 to 1000 USCF)
Friday (Advanced) class from 7 pm to 9 pm- (designed for 1100 to 1600 USCF)
Sunday class from 6 pm to 8 pm- (designed for 250 to 850 USCF)
Coaches:
Mondays: National Master Justin Burgess
Tuesdays: National Master Dennis Norman
Wednesdays: National Master Sam Martin
Fridays: Chess Author & USCF Expert Kevin Stokker
Fridays (Advanced): International Master Joshua Posthuma
Sundays: USCF Expert Epiphany Peters
Registration & Billing
The cost of enrollment is $150/month for every course except the Friday advanced class. The cost of enrollment for the Friday Advanced course is $200/month. Fees are assessed regardless of attendance. After registering online, you will be set up for automatic monthly payments. These payments can be cancelled prior to the start of the upcoming month.
To register for this course , kindly visit our website: https://www.dmvchess.com/courses-register
Note: If you would like to join a class mid-month, we can send you a pro-rated invoice for the first month. By default, students who register online will be enrolled on the first of the upcoming month. After registering on the website, please email Click here to show mail address if you would like to be enrolled immediately in the middle of a month.

weekly on Tuesday, starting from Tuesday, December 2, 2025, forever
Event Overview
DECEMBER TUESDAY NIGHT SWISS
USCF RATED - YOU MUST BE A USCF MEMBER TO PARTICIPATE
WHEN: Every Tuesday in December: 2nd, 9th, 16th, 23rd, 30th. Rounds at 7pm each Tuesday Night
WHERE: Houston Chess Studio, 250 Patton St. Suite H, Houston TX 77009
FORMAT: 5 Round Swiss G/90, d5. Rounds at 7pm each Tuesday Night
SECTIONS: one section
ENTRY FEE: Poison Pawn members $45 anytime. Non-members $55 through Sunday November 2nd then $65.
PRIZES: Percentage of entries, varies based on number of entries, approx. 40%. All prizes paid via PayPal. Draws before 30 moves disqualifies both players from any prize. * NON-MEMBERS OF POISON PAWNS CHESS CLUB ARE ONLY ELIGIBLE FOR 75% OF THE CASH PRIZES! (So isn't it time you joined!)
CANCELLATION: You may cancel up to 24 hours before the beginning of round 1 and get a refund of what you paid minus $15, or you may apply the entire amount towards a future entry fee.
BYES: One ½ point bye available for any round except the last round. The bye must be declared before the beginning of round 2. No last round byes except for zero point byes.
HOTEL INFO: Holiday Inn Express , 3401 N. Main St., is less than a mile from The Studio. Phone 832-834-6197 and ask for The Houston Chess Studio discount, or if booking online use code ALDR9. Also within a mile is the Heights House Hotel , an America’s Best Value , and a Luxury Inn . Google them for info.
THE HOUSTON CHESS STUDIO: Houston’s only ‘brick and mortar’ chess venue is dedicated to providing a quality chess playing experience for players of all levels. Centrally and conveniently located at 250 Patton St., Suite H, Houston TX 77009. Just inside North Loop 610 and just 2 blocks off North I-45. There are 3 restaurants in the same strip center as The Studio: The Red Hot Noodle (Asian), Subway, and Patron Pizza. Several others are within walking distance. Plenty of FREE parking.
SCANNING: All players are subject to being electronically scanned (“wanded”) in order to help prevent cheating.

Mardi Quads
Presidio Junction la Madeleine French Bakery and Café
Tuesday, February 17, 2026
Event Overview
Join the Alliance Chess Club for our monthly Quick rated quads tournament!
Entry Fee:
$5 cash entry/$3 cash entry for Seniors 60+/Veterans/Additional family member; $5.29/$3.23 (2.6% + 15¢) for debit/credit card payments. One free entry for new or renewal of US Chess membership if purchased through our club. Cash preferred ; exact change is appreciated. For PayPal entry, please send $5.69/$3.58 (2.99% + 49¢) to [email protected] .
Prizes:
First place winner from each quad/small Swiss receives a la Madeleine gift card. Standard US Chess tiebreaks and/or a blitz playoff will be used to determine winners (if applicable).
Format:
3 Round Quads, G/10;+5 (affects Quick rating only).
Round Times:
7:00 PM
7:40 PM
8:20 PM
Entries To:
Please email Click here to show mail address with your intent to play. Please include your name and US Chess ID number.
Onsite Registration:
6:30 PM — 6:50 PM. Due to the nature of the quad format, entries not accepted after 6:50 PM.
Equipment:
Sets provided; please bring clocks . Clocks not capable of delay or increment are allowed to alternatively use G/15 d/0.
Restrictions:
A valid US Chess membership is required. Purchase or renew your US Chess membership through our club, and receive a one free paid entry into this tournament!
More Information:

Newark JFK Chess Club
John F. Kennedy Recreation & Aquatic Center.
weekly on Tuesday and Friday, starting from Tuesday, September 24, 2024, forever
Event Overview
Unlock Your Chess Potential at Newark JFK Recreation!
Are you ready to dive into the exciting world of chess? Newark JFK Recreation is thrilled to announce our comprehensive chess program, catering to players from beginners to advanced levels! Join us every Tuesday and Friday from 4:30 PM to 6 PM for engaging lessons and strategic gameplay that will elevate your skills.
What We Offer:
Beginner to Advanced Classes : Whether you’re just starting out or looking to sharpen your tactics, our skilled instructors will guide you through the intricacies of the game. You'll learn essential techniques, openings, and strategies to outsmart your opponents.
Introduction to Tournament Play : Immediately following our classes, we will introduce you to the thrilling world of tournament play. Discover what it takes to compete, and gain valuable insights into the competitive chess landscape.
Opportunity to Represent Our Club : We’re excited to announce that the chess club will be selecting players to represent us in upcoming team tournaments! This is your chance to showcase your skills, gain experience, and be part of a passionate community of chess enthusiasts.
Why Join Us?
Chess is more than just a game; it’s a fantastic way to develop critical thinking, problem-solving skills, and patience. Plus, it’s a great way to make new friends and become part of a supportive community. Whether you’re playing for fun or aspiring to compete, there’s a place for you here.
How to Get Involved:
Don’t miss out on this fantastic opportunity to enhance your chess skills and join our vibrant chess community! Simply come to Newark JFK Recreation on Tuesdays or Fridays at 4:30 PM, and we’ll take care of the rest. Bring your enthusiasm and willingness to learn, and let’s make some moves together!
We look forward to seeing you on the board! Let’s checkmate those challenges and have fun along the way. For more information, feel free to reach out to us or visit our website. Happy playing! ♟️

events.name: TUESDAY CHESS NIGHT (3ss, 25+5) by Indy Chess
events.sourceText:
TUESDAY CHESS NIGHT (3ss, 25+5) by Indy Chess
Latvian Community Center
weekly on Tuesday, starting from Tuesday, January 6, 2026, forever
Event Overview
All are welcome to join us for Indy's largest weekly chess night at the Latvian Community Center!
Register ahead of time at indychess.org/events!
There are three areas in which you can play chess:
1) USCF-RATED TOURNAMENT ROOM
There's a 3-round, Swiss system, G/25+5 USCF-rated tournament (typically two or three sections determined by rating) in a separate room from about 6:30pm to 9:30pm.
Arrive by 6:15pm if you want to be paired in round one (if you are a regular and you pre-register online, just text Mike if you can't arrive by 6:15pm so we know to pair you and start the clock).
Games affect both USCF regular and quick ratings.
Must be a member of USCF to play rated chess (new.uschess.org/join-us-chess). Make sure to provide your USCF ID# to [email protected] prior to the event, or arrive by 6:15pm to be paired in round one.
First visit = free (but arrive by 6:15p)! Other visits are $5 members/$10 non-members (club membership is $50/yr).
2) KIDS' WORKSHOP AND QUADS
There will be a kids' game review workshop from 6:30-7:00, followed by kids casual play from 7:00-8:00pm.
Kids can earn medals, and eventually cash in medals for trophies.
Kids typically play in "quads" after the lesson, meaning we place them in groups of four according to their level and they play each kid in the quad one time! First Tuesday of each month we play "Bughouse" (two-on-two chess).
Participation in the kids' area costs $5 (members) / $10 (non-members), but the first visit is free (just show up).
Pay at the door by 6:30p, or save time and register in advance at indychess.org/events.
Parents are requested to stay the first visit, but future visits can leave and return by 7:50pm.
3) ADULT CASUAL
Adult casual play (13+ years old) will also be available 6:30-9:30pm, so come make some friends and meet new opponents.
Adults pair themselves for pick-up games.
Sets and clocks are provided (you can bring your own as well), and any time control is allowed as you desire.
Adult Casual section is always free; just show up and play pick-up games!
The rooms are wheelchair accessible.
All chess equipment is provided (though feel free to bring your own).
There is a cash-only drinks vending machine, but many players bring a water bottle as the water fountain is broken.
Register for chess night at indychess.org/events!
Questions? Email Mike at [email protected] . Hope to see you there!

Western Illinois University QC Campus
monthly on Tuesday, but only the first and the third instance of this set, starting from Tuesday, February 3, 2026, forever
Event Overview
Western Illinois Chess Club USCF Rated, 4-Round Rapid Play Tuesday Chess Tournament
Open to all ages. USCF membership required.
♟️♟️♟️
When: The 1st Tuesday and the 3rd Tuesday of every month, 5:30pm - 8:30pm
Type: 4 Round Swiss USCF Quick Rapid Rated G/15; d2
Where: Western Illinois University - Quad Cities Campus, Riverfront Building, rooms 103/104, 3300 River Drive Moline, Illinois, 61265
Registration: 5:30pm - 5:55pm
♟️♟️♟️
Rounds:
1st round: 06:00pm
2nd round: 06:35pm
3rd round: 07:10pm
4th round: 07:45pm
♟️♟️♟️
Entry Fee: $4 cash in person
♟️♟️♟️
Sections: Open Section & Under 1200 Section
Open Section Prize: $25 Gift Card
Youth Section Prize: $10 Gift Card
♟️♟️♟️
Additional info:
-US Chess Federation (USCF) membership required. On Site Registration Available. We have some vouchers for free USCF membership for those 17 and under. $3 off for adults.
-Parents/Guardians of young chess players are responsible for their children. Parents/Guardians must be present at all times of the tournament and may enjoy some light snacks or drinks in waiting area while games are in progress.
-Boards and clocks will be provided.
-By registering for this event, you also agree to have your photo taken to be used on our facebook page for promo purposes. Sometimes the local news stations show up as well.
♟️♟️♟️
For questions: Contact Luis Peralta or Mariela Treviño at [email protected] or (309) 737-2890
♟️♟️♟️
Tournament Director: Mariela Trevino
♟️♟️♟️
♟️♟️♟️
Key Rules, Procedures, Cheating & Etiquette:
Contacting the TD: Stop the clock and immediately call the Tournament Director for any rule violation, illegal move, or dispute.
Touch-Move Rule: If you touch one of your pieces, you must move it if it has a legal move. If you touch an opponent's piece, you must capture it if possible.
One-Hand Rule: Use only one hand to move a piece and press the clock.
Clock use: Make your move then press the clock to stop your time until it is your turn again. You will have 15 minutes plus a 2 second delay in each turn. Running out of time before checkmate means you lose the game automatically.
Illegal Moves: If you make one, your opponent stops the clock, shows the TD the illegal move, and you get a time penalty (2 minutes extra time will be added to your opponent).
Castling: Touch the King first, then the Rook, using one hand.
"J'adoube" (I adjust): Say this before touching a piece to adjust it, not to move it.
Pawn Promotion: The pawn is considered "touched" when it reaches the promotion square and must be promoted immediately to the piece you place on that square.
No Outside Help: No computers, phones (strict penalties), books, or talking to others about the game during play.
Communication: Only talk to your opponent or the TD. Be courteous. Be curteous of the players and their ongoing games around you. Whisper if talking must happen.
Cell Phones: Keep them off and away; penalties are severe.
Disputes: Handle calmly; argue with the TD, not your opponent.
Where to Find More rules: The full rules are in the US Chess Federation's website under Official Rules of Chess section.

Charlotte Chess Center Wednesday Action Quads
Charlotte Chess Center (Main/South)
weekly on Wednesday, starting from Wednesday, September 14, 2022, forever
Event Overview
OVERVIEW
A 3 round "quad" US Chess-rated tournament open to all adult players and youth. Quads, which group players by their skill level, are a great way to ensure closer matchups for a more fun and competitive challenge. Opportunity to play 3 regular rated games in one night!
Top Quads are FIDE rapid rated!
​
WHEN
Every Wednesday Night!
​
WHERE
Charlotte Chess Center - Main/South Campus
10700 Kettering Drive, Unit E
Charlotte, NC 28226
​
CCC HOURS
6:00pm - 10:00pm
REQUIREMENTS
Participants must be members of the US Chess Federation
​
ROUND TIMES
Round 1: 7:00pm
Round 2: ASAP
Round 3: ASAP
End Time: Between 8:30pm-10:00pm depending on quad.
HOW IT WORKS
Players must register weekly and in advance
Quads - players placed into groups of 4 by their most recent US Chess rating*
3 US Chess rated games every Wednesday night Top 6 quads also FIDE rapid rated
Each evening will be limited to the first 60 players to register
Entries are first registered, first served​
*Minor roster shifts to avoid family member pairings may be possible
​​
PRIZES
$40 to the winner(s) of each quad; $45 for perfect 3-0 score
TIME CONTROL
G/20; Increment 10
Each player receives 20 minutes plus a 10 second bonus each move to complete each game
ENTRY FEE
CCC Members Rated 2000+: Free Entry ( $20 deducted from any prize )
CCC Members: $20.00

​
Join the CCC and Save - Only $50 a Year - Save on Camps, Classes, Tournaments and More!

ChessPalace Wednesday Knights
ChessPalace
weekly on Wednesday, starting from Wednesday, June 18, 2025, forever
Event Overview
Wednesday Knights is a month-long tournament with one US Chess-rated game every Wednesday. The tournament is an excellent opportunity for players of all ages and skill levels to participate in weekly rated practice. With classical time controls, players can take their time to think more thoroughly about their moves and strengthen their calculation skills.
Details:
Schedule : Rounds start weekly at 7 pm;
Format: 1 round per week. Games are submitted for rating at the end of the month; 4 rounds/month (5 rounds in some months)
Time Control: 30moves/90minutes + sudden death 30minutes, both time controls have 5-second delay starting move one
Sections: one open section
Players must have an active US Chess membership. Player can also sign up or renew their US Chess membership onsite
Players must know how to use the clock and record the moves with chess notation
Entry Fee:
$30 per month​ (Free for ChessPalace club members/$35 for first-time club players)
CLICK HERE TO REGISTER
For schedules of other regular ChessPalace tournaments (i.e. Scholastic tournaments, Blitz Tournament, and Saturday Tournaments) and special events such as Grandmaster lectures and simul exhibitions, please check out our calendar page or subscribe to the blog at https://www.chesspalace.com

Community Chess Club of Rochester Wednesday Night chess!
Rochester Chess Center
weekly on Wednesday, starting from Wednesday, January 4, 2023, forever
Event Overview
1 USCF-Rated Game, G/80 d5. New players welcome. *EF: $6 for visiting players; CCCR members $4. Register on-site: 6:30-7:15 pm. Rd.: 7:30pm.
*US Chess Membership is required and can be done on-site during registration. Cost varies by age group: 20 (Youth), $27 Young Adult, $45 Adult, $40 Senior. Details for eligibility for each age group is available from the US Chess site and during registration at the Chess Center.
Snack bar on-site at the Chess Center.
Many special events take place throughout the year including our annual club championship.
Club Membership is optional. Club membership is $30 for individual members and $40 for family members in same household.
Chess game pairing is generally arranged by closest chess rating available. New players generally play the lower-rated players.
Our Club's Web Site: www.rochesterchessclub.org
Rochester Chess Center store on-site for all your chess needs, including sets, boards, clocks, books and more.
You may schedule Chess Lessons and Sign-up for Chess Camps run by the Rochester Chess Center.
History: Our chess club has been hosting chess players for over 60 years. During this time, thousands of USCF-rated chess games have been played, and countless unrated chess games have been played (e.g. Blitz, Simultaneous exhibitions, etc.). Weekly club meetings are held at the Rochester Chess Center located at 221 Norris Drive, Rochester, NY 14610; Phone: (585) 442-2430. We welcome all chess players & curious visitors. Currently, we have chess players of all ages with USCF ratings from beginner to Master strength. All are welcome.
Club Organization: Club President: Ken McBride (Local TD), Vice President: Jamshed Ahmed (Club TD), Treasurer/Organizer: Mike Lionti (Senior TD), Club Secretary: Mike Runnells, Club Officers: Mike Runnells and David Worl. Several other TDs and volunteers also assist us.

The Santa Paula Oddfellows Lodge # 314

THE CHESS RUN WEDNESDAYS is a month-long tournament with one US Chess-rated game every Wednesday. events.sourceText:
Under 800 Wednesdays
Charlotte Chess Center (North)
weekly on Wednesday, starting from Wednesday, April 2, 2025, forever
Event Overview
OVERVIEW
Under 800 Wednesdays is a free, 1 round per week, US Chess rated tournament for K-8 children, held every Sunday at the CCC's North Charlotte location.
WHEN
Every Wednesday, 6:30 - 8:00pm
REGISTRATION REQUIREMENTS
Open to K-8 participants (ages 13 and under)
Players must be rated under 800
Unrated players who wish to establish a rating are welcome to play.
Participants must be members of US Chess Need a US Chess Membership? Purchase through the CCC and save !
Participants must be members of the CCC .
Limited to first 42 players to register.
Online registration only.
Registration closes 30 minutes prior to round 1 if not already full.
HOW IT WORKS
Parents strongly encouraged to drop off.
Students play one rated game per week.
Each registration is only for the next round.
The event is submitted for rating monthly on the final Wednesday of the month.
Students may choose to get their game analyzed by a CCC coach.
SECTIONS
Under 800
Under 400/Unrated
TIME CONTROL
G/35, inc/10
Each player receives 35 minutes plus a 10 second increment to complete the game.
PRIZES
The top player in each section will receive a trophy!
See special notes below for tiebreak information.
This is a CCC Grand Prix event!
ENTRY FEE
FREE, must be a CCC Member ​ ​
CONTACT
Click here to show mail address
For contact during the event email (above) or call 980-265-1156
WITHDRAWAL
Use this link to withdraw (cancel). Withdrawals close 30 minutes prior to each game.

events.name: CHESS CARDINALS THURSDAY GRAND PRIX TOURNAMENT
events.sourceText:
CHESS CARDINALS THURSDAY GRAND PRIX TOURNAMENT
Four Seasons Shopping Center, Chesterfield
weekly on Thursday, starting from Thursday, October 16, 2025, forever
Event Overview
“Chess Cardinals” is a nonprofit 501c3 approved USCF Affiliate and is hosting USCF-rated SWISS format OPEN chess games at Four Seasons Shopping Center, Missouri, every Thursday between 6:00-8:45 pm (on-site registration between 5:30-5: 55 pm). Adults, kids and all levels of players are welcome. SPACE IS LIMITED TO THE FIRST 60 REGISTRANTS. PLEASE REGISTER BEFORE 5:45 PM. NO LATE REGISTRATION IS ALLOWED.
Time control: G/25; d5 (3 Rounds; USCF dual-rated)
Sections: The tournament has four sections:
Advanced Section: USCF rating >=1400 USCF
Championship Section: USCF rating 1000-1399 USCF
Reserve section: USCF 600-999 USCF.
Beginner section: USCF Under 600 USCF.
TD reserves the right to revise section breaks or provide wild cards. Byes are allowed in any round as long as you let us know by at least 1 round in advance.
Entry fees: $5 per tournament. We accept online payment or credit card on-site. No Cash Transactions. Online registration is highly preferred. WWW.TOURNAMENTSIGNUP.COM . Please enter your complete name and USCF ID when you register. PLEASE REGISTER BEFORE 5:45 PM. NO LATE REGISTRATION IS ALLOWED.
Mandatory requirement: Please bring a valid USCF membership ID number for registration. Additional details at http://chesscardinals.com on how to apply online for USCF membership. Our team can help you get a membership on-site too.
Optional requirement: Notation is optional. Notation books are available for purchase on-site.
Grand Prix Prizes: Based on all the “Thursday tournaments” in a month, we will tally up points and give trophies to reward improvement in chess skill and encourage participation. For each night’s attendance, you get 3 points for showing up, and for each Win 1 point, each Draw or 1/2-Byes 0.5 point (we will use the USCF cross-table for the event). Regardless of which sections you played, prizes include Top Prize 1st (Champions Trophy). Additional prizes may be awarded depending on the available funds.
Past Tournaments: US Chess MSA - Affiliate Details (Tournament History)
Mandatory requirement: Please bring a valid USCF membership ID number for registration. Additional details at http://chesscardinals.com on how to apply online for USCF membership. Our team can help you get a membership on-site too. New Female Chess Players can get up to 50% discount on their membership.
Directions:
Parking: Recommended in front of the UPS STORE or SEOUL TACO.
Entrance: Ground floor through main big glass doors.
SIGNS: Look for the Chess Cardinals banner.
Restrooms: Ground floor near emergency EXIT. Separate for MEN/WOMEN. You would need keys. Please RESTROOM KEYS sign on the wall to locate these keys.
Photo/video Consent Agreement . By registering to the Chess Cardinals tournaments, participants, caregivers & parents grant full permission to Chess Cardinals to use photographs, video- and/or audio-recordings of them, and/or their children, taken during Chess Cardinals events in publications, news releases, online, and in other communications related to the mission of Chess Cardinals. To ensure the privacy of individuals and children, images will not be identified using personal identifying information without written approval from the photographed subject, parent or legal guardian. A person attending Chess Cardinals event who does not wish to have their image recorded for distribution should make their wishes known to the organizer in writing of his/her intentions and include a photograph. Chess Cardinals will use the photo for identification purposes and will hold it in confidence. No registrants and/or participants are entitled to compensation for their appearance in such materials. By registering, you also grant Chess Cardinals and US Chess Federation the right to lawfully use the photos on its website, social media sites, e-newsletters, and other public media which such use shall be considered commercial use for promotion and advertising. You also release Chess Cardinals and US Chess Federation from any claims related to the use of the photos, recordings, or interviews, including claims of libel or invasion of privacy. You understand that Chess Cardinals retains ownership of the materials and may use them now or in the future for the purposes mentioned above. All registrants and participants release and discharge Chess Cardinals from all liability, losses, and damages for libel, slander, invasion of privacy or any other claim arising out of or relating to the use of videotapes, recordings and/or photograph.

Thinking Thursdays
The Cork and Board
weekly on Thursday, starting from Thursday, November 20, 2025, forever
Event Overview
When: Meets most Thursdays at 6:30PM
Where: The Cork and Board, Jefferson City's premiere board game pub!
Cost: Free! Donations accepted but not expected!
USCF Tournament Director(s): Joshua Wood
USCF Membership Required: Sold Onsite*
Equipment: Several sets, boards, and chess clocks provided; players are encouraged to bring their own!
Registration: Onsite at 6:15PM. Round 1 Begins at 6:30PM (or as close as possible)
Prizes: Bragging rights!
We play for the love of chess!
Join us most Thursday nights for blitz chess! Graciously hosted by The Cork and Board, stop by for an ice cold beer or a crisp cocktail, some delicious entrees, and some rated chess! The default is rated G/10;d0, though if the participants want to play something else, they make it known! (Including Hand & Brain, Bughouse, and G/0:01;d5, among other terrible influences!) Please note, while very family friendly, there is alcohol served at this establishment. The chess is played in a relaxed atmosphere - arriving late and leaving early are ok.
*If you don't have a USCF membership, it can be purchased on site (or I can walk you through doing it yourself as well). While required to play rated chess, effort is made if not a member to provide opponents, but preference is given to the tournament players. When playing anything not rated (e.g. Hand & Brain, Bughouse, etc), a membership is obviously not required!
Check out The Board Fools Chess Club on Facebook for details regarding individual dates!

events.sourceText:
2026 Charlotte February Open
Grand Prix
Hilton Garden Inn - Southpark
Friday, February 20, 2026
- Sunday, February 22, 2026
Event Overview
https://www.charlottechesscenter.org/events/febopen
OVERVIEW
The Charlotte February Open is a classical event with a $6,000 guaranteed total prize fund - $5,500 in the main event plus a free $500 Saturday evening blitz tournament.
All sections are US Chess and FIDE rated. There is a minimum rating of 1200 and registration cap of 140 players.
WHEN
February 20-22, 2026
3-day and 2-day schedules available
​
WHERE
Beautiful Venue in the Heart of Southpark! Walk to Starbucks, Whole Foods and more!
Hilton Garden Inn - Southpark
4808 Sharon Road
Charlotte, NC 28210
(704) 362-5080
Free internet, free parking
​
​ HOTEL BOOKING
Both hotel options attached to the playing venue.
Hilton Garden Inn - Southpark
$134/night for King or $149 for 2 Queens
Booking Link - Reserve ASAP
Homewood Suites - Southpark
$152/night for King suite with sofa bed
Booking Link - Reserve ASAP
ELIGIBILITY
There is a strict minimum rating of 1200 to enter, based on February US Chess ratings or a peak rating achieved between January 1 - February 20.
See events schedule for other options this weekend.
Registration Cap: 140 players. The organizer may continue to accept registration past 140 players based on specific space constraints.
REGISTRATION
Online registration only - no on-site registration.
All registration closes 90 minutes before round 1 start time.
On-site check-in is not necessary .
TIME CONTROLS
3-Day Schedule: G/110; inc/10
Rounds 1-2 of 2-day: G/30, inc/10
PRIZES & SECTIONS
$5,500 Guaranteed Prize Fund in 3 Sections .
Championship Section - FIDE Rated
$1000 – $700 – $400
Top U2200: $400
40 US Chess Grand Prix Points
​
Under 2000 Section - FIDE Rated
$700 – $400 – $200
Top U1800: $300
Under 1600 Section - FIDE Rated
$600 – $300 – $200
Top U1400: $300
Minimum rating of 1200.
100-point Rule applies for "playing up" - see Special Notes below.
Plaques to first place in all sections.
SCHEDULE
3-Day Schedule - 5 Rounds
Friday: 6:30pm
Saturday: 10:30am & 4:00pm
Sunday: 10:00am & 3:00pm

September 2023 Dragon Knight Chess Grand Prix Tournaments

events.name: Charlotte Chess Center Friday Action Quads - North
events.sourceText:
Charlotte Chess Center Friday Action Quads - North
Charlotte Chess Center (North)
weekly on Friday, starting from Friday, May 3, 2024, forever
Event Overview
Friday Action Quads - North
A three round US Chess-rated tournament open to all scholastic (K-12) players. Quads, which group students in sections of 4 by their rating level, are a great way for students to get closer matchups for a more fun and competitive challenge.
During the Fall and Spring seasons, this event does count for eligibility towards the Tournament of Champions .
​ CHECK OUT ALL OF OUR EVENTS!
WHEN
Every Friday Night!
Can't make Friday evenings? Great alternatives are:
Sunday Action Quads ( CCC Main/South )
Monday Action Quads ( CCC North )
Friday Action Quads is also offered at our South Location - Info Here
REGISTRATION
Limited to first 42 to register. Registration must be completed online ahead of the event.
REQUIREMENTS
Ages 17 and under
Participants must be members of the US Chess Federation
US Chess is the governing body of chess in the US and conducts all of the rating calculations for players. Need a US Chess Membership? Purchase through the CCC and save !
​​ ROUND TIMES
Round 1: 7:00pm
Round 2: ASAP
Round 3: ASAP
Approximate End Time: 9:00pm
HOW IT WORKS
Players must register weekly and in advance
3 US Chess regular and quick rated games every Friday night
Quad format - students placed into groups of 4 by their most current "live" US Chess regular rating to ensure closer matchups.
Each evening will be limited to the first 42 players to register
Entries are first registered, first served
Quads are for students (K-12) only​
PRIZES
Medal to winner of each quad
​​ TIME CONTROL
G/20; Increment 10
Each player receives 20 minutes plus a 10 second bonus each move to complete each game
​ ENTRY FEE
Players currently rated 1500+: FREE Entry (see special notes for details)
CCC Members: $17.50
Non-Members: $22.50
​
Join the CCC and Save - Only $50 a Year - Save on Camps, Classes, Tournaments and more!
The Charlotte Chess Center’s North Branch is conveniently located off of I-485 and Benfield Road. Opened in September of 2023, the CCC’s North Branch serves North Charlotte, University City, Concord, Kannapolis, Harrisburg, Huntersville, Cornelius, Davidson, Lake Norman, and Mooresville. Regulars visit from both North Carolina and South Carolina.
Address: 10211 Prosperity Park Drive
Ste 230 (floor 2)
Charlotte , NC 28269
United States

events.name: G90+30 Friday Night Chess #13
events.sourceText:
G90+30 Friday Night Chess #13
Memphis Chess Club
weekly on Friday, starting from Friday, February 6, 2026, 4 times
Event Overview
4ss, G90+30, one game per Friday
Registration ends each Friday night 7:30pm. Games start at 8pm, but if both opponents want to start sooner when pairings are ready (hopefully by 7:30pm) that's okay too!
Entry Fees
Prize Pool
(For folks who want to win prize money; byes must be declared on first played round, one half point bye ok)
$80 for Social and Non Members
$60 for Full and Family Members
No-Prize
(For folks who want to play stronger players but don't mind not being able to win prizes; half point byes are available any round)
$30 for Social and Non Members
$25 for Full and Family Members
Per-game, No-Prize
(This is for folks with uncertain schedules, visiting players, etc., all rounds un-played are half point byes for pairing purposes.)
$15 per game for Social and Non Members
$10 per game for Full and Family Members
Prizes(80%!!):
Prizes are determined by the total number of entries, prize players and non-prize players. Prizes are a percentage of ALL collected entries, both prize players and non-prize players.
There are never more prizes than prize players(all 80% goes to prize players)
1-4 players:
1st, 80%
5-6 players:
1st, 48%
2nd, 32%
7+ players:
1st, 40%
2nd, 25%
3rd, 15%

February Open – Day Knight Chess Free USCF-Rated Tournament
Welcome to the Day & Knight Chess February Open! This free community event is designed to help players of all levels gain experience in a competitive tournament environment.
https://www.kingregistration.com/event/Feb26

events.name: 2026 Greater Austin Scholastic Championships
events.sourceText:
2026 Greater Austin Scholastic Championships
NYOS Charter School
Saturday, February 21, 2026
Event Overview
Would you like to be an Austin area scholastic chess champion? Here’s your chance!
Scholastic chess tournament in multiple sections to be held on February 21, 2026. G/25, +5 inc. Trophies and medals awarded.
Full pairings and standings can be found at the registration link below (click on the blue “Live” text to get to them).
Register HERE ! When you click the link, scroll to the bottom for registration.
See Preregistration List HERE
Basics
USCF rated chess tournament in multiple RATED scholastic sections: K-3 U400, K-3 U700, K-5 U600, K-5 U1000, 6-12 U600, 6-12 U1000, and K-12 Elite (for players rated 950-1399). Please note: all scholastic players rated 1400 and over must play in the Open section . Please note, at the event pairings will be posted only online .
This is a Swiss-system tournament, so everyone plays all day—there is no “elimination.” Players must know how to play the game of chess! We follow US Chess rules including: touch-move, mandatory clocks if available, and notation. K-3 and younger sections are excused from taking notation. Please review the Parent/Coach Responsibilities before registering.
Location
NYOS Charter School
12333 N Lamar Blvd
Austin, TX 78753
Eligibility
This is a rated tournament. You must have a USCF ID and your membership can be purchased/renewed online with US Chess in advance of registration. You can verify your US Chess membership ID and expiration by visiting the US Chess Member Services Area . Anyone can become a USCF member. Players new to tournament chess are welcome to play. Your US Chess membership cannot expire before February 28, 2026. (New players in 3rd grade and below may request a non-member ID as a part of USCF’s Junior Tournament Player program during registration. JTPs ok in K-3 sections only .)
“Under” sections are only for students meeting the rating criteria. All players who are new to tournaments are eligible for their age appropriate ‘under’ section. ( Look up your player’s rating here . Please email the registrar or ask your chess coach for placement information.
If your 6th grader attends an Elementary School, please contact the registrar for options. With enough registrations, any section may be divided into two sections so we can offer more prizes. Sections with fewer than 20 entries may be merged into a similar section to provide optimal pairings and competition.
Please note: February 2026 ‘Regular’ OTB ratings will be used for pairing purposes. If no regular rating is available, then other USCF ratings (quick, blitz, online) can and will be considered for section placement. Requests to play down will not be honored. FYI: Any event that is rated after January 21st will not affect your February supplement rating, as those events takes place after February ratings are calculated.
All players in this event must be in 12th grade or lower.
Schedule
No check-in necessary for preregistrations. We will make every attempt to contact you in advance if we see a problem with your registration. Verify your entry online!
8:00 a.m. Chess Control opens for onsite registration. Onsite registrations before 9:30am accepted, but must start play in round 2.
8:30 a.m Announcements begin in all scholastic playing rooms.
Players and coaches should be present.
9:00 a.m. Rd 1 begins. Scholastic sections have 5 rds, G/25, +5.
9:00 a.m. Open section (different event allowing adults) begins. Open has 4 rounds, all rounds are are G/45, +5.
9:15 a.m. – 5:00 p.m. Chess control open for event issues. No changes for round 1 (bye or section) allowed after online registration closes. Requests for byes, withdrawals, and player or school information edits go in effect immediately if made via email before the close of online registration. Changes requested onsite go into effect as of round 2.
Approximate Round Times
Scholastic Sections:
round 1 – 9:00am, rd 2 – 11:00am, rd 3 – 12:45 pm, rd 4 – 2:30 pm, rd 5 – 4:00 pm
Awards in the cafeteria as each section finishes.
Notes
There will be some down time between rounds since many games will finish early. We will provide an area (outside the tournament room) for casual “skittles” chess and/or other indoor activities. Parents and/or coaches, please provide age-appropriate activities during the time between rounds. The organizers cannot baby-sit. No child should be left unattended!
Concessions details coming soon. Only water bottles allowed at the chess board.
Awards
Trophies & Medals to Top Contenders! Ribbons to all participants!
Trophies to the top individuals in each scholastic section. Trophies to the top teams in all sections. Number of individual and team trophies will depend on number of entries. Chess medals will go to all players (excluding Open section) that finish the tournament with a positive score (3.0 & 3.5 points). Trophies to players scoring 4.0 and above. No teams in Open section, but special trophies will be awarded to the highest scoring Family & Child teams (Uncles, Aunts, Adult siblings, Parents, Grandparents, or coach paired with at least one scholastic aged player.)
Registration Information
*$35 thru Saturday, 1/31/2026.
*$45 thru Saturday, 2/14/2026.
*Late entry $50 begins Sunday, 2/15/2026 and ENDS at midnight on Wednesday, 2/18/2026, at which time online entry closes.
*$60 Onsite entry receives 1/2pt bye in round 1, and begins play in round 2.
Withdrawals requested via email before online registration closes ( midnight on Wednesday 2/18/26) are eligible for a refund (minus a $10 service fee). No exceptions. No refunds for USCF memberships after purchased from the USCF. NO email/phone entries.
Please request byes by adding a note when you register. First bye receives 1/2-point. Further byes receive 0-points. Email the registrar to make changes to your requested byes. Deadline to add or remove a 1st round requested bye is 9am Friday 2/20/2026. All 1/2-point byes must be requested/removed before the end of round 2.
Email Click here to show mail address with other questions. No phone calls, please. Emails will be returned promptly.

events.sourceText:
2nd Annual B-Town Blizzard Scholastic & Open!
Faith Lutheran Church
Saturday, February 21, 2026
Event Overview
2nd Annual B-Town Blizzard Scholastic & Open!
$1,000 projected prize fund! Part of weekend festivities w/special guest! Free pizza & cocoa!
Saturday, February 21, 2026
Faith Lutheran Church, 2200 S High St, Bloomington, IN
Onlineregistration.cc registration:
https://onlineregistration.cc
Sections and prizes: Scholastic sections: 3rd Grade/Under Scholastic - trophy prizes
8th Grade/Under Scholastic - trophy prizes
12th Grade/Under Scholastic - gift card prizes
Open sections: Master/Expert Open (2000+) - $350 prizes
Upper Open (1500-1999) - $300 prizes
Lower Open (1000-1499) - $200 prizes
Novice Open (<999) - $150 prizes
Note: We may combine sections due to turnout if necessary
Scholastic round times, arrival times, and time control: Round times: 9:30AM, (lunch break), 12:00PM, last two rounds will start as soon as the last game finishes
Arrival time: Arrive between 8:00-9:15AM (inc. on-site registration)
Time control: G45;d5 (each side has 45 minutes to make moves with a five-second delay before the clock ticks down each move)
Open round times, arrival times, and time control: Round times: 9:00AM, (lunch break), 12:30PM, 3:30PM, 6:30PM
Arrival time: Arrive between 8:00-8:45AM (inc. on-site registration)
Time control: G60+5 (each side has 60 minutes to make moves with a five-second increment after each move)
NOTE: Open sections begin 30 minutes BEFORE the scholastic sections! Plan accordingly!
Equipment: Open section players, please bring boards, pieces, and clocks!
Byes: Up to 2 half-point byes can be requested. Let us know ASAP. We do not want to forfeit you!
Entry fee for all sections: $5 until December 31, $20 till January 31, $40 after/on-site. Free entry upon proof of public assistance. Full refunds available between January 1 and February 18.
Perks: Cozy concessions and free pizza available!
Scholastic players earn 400 HCA points and join/climb up our participation leaderboard! Visit our website to learn more
This tournament is just one of many exciting chess activities all weekend, Saturday and Sunday! Stick around to meet a special guest…
Awards: Scholastic players will receive trophies at each section’s awards ceremony once all fourth-round games finish. Let us know if you need to skip the ceremony, and we can ship trophies to your address.
Open section players who need to leave before cash prizes are handed out will receive their payouts electronically via PayPal, Venmo, or check.
Contact: Click here to show mail address , 812-318-2875
Full tournament policies and procedures: Visit our website to read

CKQ Saturday Piscataway Rapids
Kings & Queens Chess Academy
Saturday, February 21, 2026
Event Overview
Start time: Players should arrive no later than 4:15 p.m. The first game begins promptly at 4:30. Latecomers risk their clock running when they arrive.
End time: The Under 600 section typically ends by 8:30 p.m., the Under 1200 section more like 9:00. The tournament could go a bit longer if players use all their time.
Players: Most players at this event will be children (ages 6-16), but adults are welcome to play. Beginners are welcome, but at a minimum players should know how to legally move chess pieces, recognize when they’re in check, and how to perform basic checkmates (ex; king and queen vs. king).
Structure / time controls: 4-SS, G30 +5. (Each player will play four games. Each player receives 30 minutes per game, plus another five seconds per move.)
Sections: Under 600 and Under 1200 rating sections. The Under 1200 section requires at least 500 rating to enter. Lower-rated and unrated players may enter with the tournament director's permission.
Requirements: A USCF membership is required to play in the tournament. Contact the tournament director if you need assistance creating or renewing a membership.

Each Saturday at 1:30pm
A 3-6 round "quad" US Chess rated tournament open to all scholastic (K-12) players. Quads group players by their skill level. This is a chance to play 3-6 rated (regular and quick) games each Saturday afternoon!

Free Entry Policy:
Free entry is offered to scholastic (K-12) players who have a current "live Over The Board (OTB)" US Chess rating of 1200+. No exceptions.
To get free entry, players must register online mid-day before the event (Noon Friday).
If you register for free but must cancel, email [email protected]
or text (919) 422-2535 by 12:30pm (one hour before Round 1 of the quad).
Players receiving free entry are not permitted to withdraw mid-quad, without permission from all other players in their quad. Free entry players who withdraw mid-quad (without permission) will not be eligible for free entry in future Dragon Knight Chess quads.
US Chess membership required; Dragon Knight Chess will use vouchers to create new scholastic memberships. US Chess is the governing body of chess in the United States. US Chess conducts all rating calculations for players.

Above USCF 800 sections G/40; delay 5 (3 games): Each player receives 40 minutes (plus a 5 second delay each move) to complete each game.

Players must register weekly.

3-6 rated games each Saturday afternoon

1804 Mindehall Drive, Farmers Branch Texas 75234

Inquiries : [email protected]
Lunch\Drinks : Not available at Location - Participants may bring sack lunches. Please plan accordingly
Tournament Policy :
Refunds: A player can receive Tournament credits if notified in an email by 11:00pm the day before the event. Players that no-show do not receive a refund. No exceptions.
Photography: Photos will be taken of the tournament
Note :
Parents/Guardians of Minors
We welcome children to play in our tournament, but please be aware of the following:
Your child will play against adults, will be treated like an adult, and will be expected to interact like an adult. Your child will not be supervised by us. If a child is under 16 years old, a parent/guardian must remain in the building.
Rule Variations in Effect at the Tournament
1H1. Director as witness only. In an event in which most games are not watched by directors, a director may refrain from correcting all illegal moves he or she may notice but simply serve as a witness should one of the players point out the illegal move before any moves have been made.
15A. Paper scoresheet variation. The player using a paper scoresheet may first make the move, and then write it on the scoresheet, or vice versa.

Event Overview

DATE & TIME: Saturday, February 21, 2026; 1:00PM~6:00PM (Round 1 at 1:00PM, subsequent rounds ASAP) .
LOCATION: Play More Chess Academy, Home of the Hamden Chess Club, 1227 Whitney Ave., Hamden, CT 06517

This tournament is open to all adult players ages 13+ of any rating, including Unrated. (Players who are under age 13, but have a USCF rating of 700+ are also eligible for this tournament).

Early entry (by 11:59PM Thursday prior): All players $50, then
Regular entry (by 11:00AM day of tournament): All players $60
PRIZES: $600, based on 24 paid entries (70% Gtd); (Open Section: $150-100, Top Female $50; U1600 Section: $125-75, Top Female $50; Biggest Upset in tournament $50. Prizes adjusted on pro rata basis based on actual entries. Players with tie score within section share prizes equally.
PRIZE LIMITS: Unrated player: $100 limit. Unrated player not eligible for Biggest upset prize and place prize is limited to $100 for unrated player.
PLAY UP LIMIT: 200 POINTS. i.e. player with rating 1400-1599 may choose to play in either section.

CT Transit bus stop is adjacent to Academy at intersection of Putnam/Whitney Ave.

events.name: Jenks K-12 Open
events.sourceText:
Jenks K-12 Open
Jenks Middle School
Saturday, February 21, 2026
Event Overview
Schedule
8:30 Doors open. There is no check-in; all registered players will be paired.
9:30 Round One for all sections will begin following announcements in the playing hall.
​Subsequent rounds are paired back to back with a break for lunch. Awards ceremonies take place for each section after that section's final round is complete.
​For late arrivals or last-minute cancellations, send a text to 918-978-1899. This helps us start on time and avoid pairing players with no-shows.
​
​Sections & Prizes
1: Grades K–3 rated under 600
Five rounds, G/30
🏆 Trophies for first, second, and third-place individuals. Outstanding Performance trophies for players scoring 4.0+ who did not place in the top three. Trophies for first, second, and third-place school teams and for first-place club team.
🏅Medals for players with scores of 3.0–3.5​​.
​ 2: Grades 4–6 rated under 600
Five rounds, G/30
🏆 Trophies for first, second, and third-place individuals. Outstanding Performance trophies for players scoring 4.0+ who did not place in the top three. Trophies for first, second, and third-place school teams and for first-place club team.
🏅Medals for players with scores of 3.0–3.5​​. ​
​ 3: All grades rated under 900
K-6th graders rated under 600 may play in either section 1 or 2 according to their grade.
Five rounds, G/30
🏆 Trophies for first, second, and third-place individuals and Outstanding Performance trophies for players with 4.0 or higher who did not place in the top three. Trophies for first, second, and third-place school teams and for first-place club team.
🏅Medals for players with scores of 3.0–3.5​​
4: All grades rated under 1300
Four rounds, G/40;d5
Clocks required
Notation strongly encouraged
🏆 Trophies for first, second, and third-place individuals. Trophies for first-place school team and club team.
🏅Medals for players with scores of 2.5 or higher.
5 (Premier): All grades rated 1300+*
Four rounds, G/40;d5
Clocks and notation required
🏆 Trophies for first, second, and third-place individuals. Trophy for top U1600. Trophies for first-place school team and club team.
🏅Medals for players with scores of 2.5 or higher.
​*Players with a rating of 1200+ may play up to Premier. ​
​
Equipment
Sets are provided for tournament games, but players are encouraged to bring their own for skittles (waiting area).
​Scoresheets and pencils are provided.
Clocks are provided for sections 4 & 5 only. Players in other sections may bring their own. A good selection of tournament-suitable clocks can be found here .​
Membership
A current US Chess membership is required for all players. OSCO offers discounted memberships to all registered players, including non-Oklahoma residents. If your player has never had a US Chess membership, or if their membership will have expired by the date of the tournament, visit the appropriate link below after you register.
This is NOT an automatic process. Our volunteers will use the information you provide in the forms below to get a US Chess ID for you child or renew their membership.
New players: Grades K–3 rated under 600
​ Oklahoma residents: First-time membership, Section 2 or higher
All players: Renew an expired membership
​ Other states: First-time membership, Section 2 or higher
​Not sure if your player's membership is still current? Please check before you register: US Chess Player Search (Link opens in a new window.)
Read before you register
When you register, you will be asked to agree to OSCO's terms & conditions. You will also be asked to affirm that you will make sure your player understands our tournament rules and code of conduct. Please take a moment to read them now. (Each link opens in a new window, so you won't lose your place.)
Terms & conditions
Tournament rules
Code of Conduct ​
​If you or your player have a question about OSCO's rules, please contact us at Click here to show mail address so we can answer it before the tournament.
​Registration
Registration is on our website HERE and ends February 19. No registrations will be accepted after the deadline.
Entry is $25/player. Parents registering three or more siblings at the same time: $20/player.
​​Questions?
For general tournament or registration questions, requests to change section or team affiliation, or cancellations before the registration deadline, send an email to Click here to show mail address .
For payment questions or refund requests made before the registration deadline, send an email to Click here to show mail address . Refunds do not include online processing fees.

Tulsa , OK 74137
United States

Event Overview
Scholastic Chess Tournament designed for beginners and players with a short experience.
ONLY FOR K-12 PLAYERS RATED UNDER 1000.
4 Rounds Swiss Game in 25/5d.
Entry Fee: $25 by Wednesday, $30 by Friday, $35 Same Day. Full refund if canceling up to 1 hour before the event. No refund after that.
Sections: Open, K-12 Under 600, K-3 Under 500, and K-3 Under 200. Highest rating will be used for sections and prizes. Half point Byes available in all 4 rounds (Max 2) and must be requested before round 2.
Schedule: First round starts at 2:00 PM. Rounds 2, 3, and 4 will start as soon as the previous round is over. Ceremony will follow right after the 4th round is over.

Loudoun Chess Tournament 2/21/26
Executive Conference and Training Center
Saturday, February 21, 2026
Event Overview
Register at chessacademy.com/tournaments !
This tournament is for scholastic players in grades K-12 with and without prior tournament experience. We recommend that players in their first tournament choose the Unrated option, where they will be grouped by age and play 3 or 4 games.
Players who've previously done well in an Unrated section or have previous rated tournament experience should choose the Rated option, where they'll be placed in a group of 4 players according to their age and rating. Each participant then plays one game against each of the other three players in their group. At the end of the third game, the winner of each group receives a trophy.
This event should typically finish in 1-2 hours, but can potentially take as long as 3 hours for the most advanced players (although that is rare).
Everyone will use a clock! We'll go over how to use clocks on-site, and you can watch this short video to see how they work. Unrated section players will play a game in 10 minutes with a 5 second delay, and Rated games are 25 minutes with a 5 second delay for each player.
Players can play in the morning at 10am, the afternoon at 1pm, or both!
All sections are non-elimination, and all players participate in all rounds
If you're playing in the Rated sections and have a US Chess ID# and membership, please include it. If you don't have one, we will purchase it for you ($24 value!). If you're not sure what your ID# is you can look it up here
Please arrive 15 minutes before games start. Players who arrive after that may not be placed in quads.
Prices increase by $10 at noon the Tuesday before the tournament.
Questions? Please let us know at Click here to show mail address !

events.name: Mohar February Chess Tournament
events.sourceText:
Mohar February Chess Tournament
Holiday Inn
Saturday, February 21, 2026
Event Overview
Team Trophies!
Three players in the rated sections attending the same school (as of the spring 2026 semester). Teams have no upper limit;
the more players on a team, the higher the chances for a good result, but only the top 3 players’
results count for the team total. The team gains points by winning or drawing rated games. Points are
weighted, with results in higher sections worth more.
-------------------------------------------------
Mohar February Chess Tournament – Scholastic and Open Chess Tournament
February 21, 2026
Holiday Inn, 909 Holcomb Bridge Rd Roswell, GA 30076
4SS, G/25;d5
5 sections – An Open section for adults and advanced scholastic players, 3 Rated Scholastic-only
sections for K-12 players and a Nonrated Scholastic practice section for new and young players.
ROUND TIMES: First round is at 10:00AM, rounds 2-4 will start ASAP after the preceding rounds finish
with a slightly longer break for lunch between rounds 2 and 3. We are usually done around 4 – 4:30
PM.
NONRATED SECTION: The Nonrated section is for new/unrated players and players rated below 300
who need practice. While the rules of chess still apply, this is a more relaxed game designed to let new
and young players experience chess without worrying about ratings. New players may choose to play
in the Under 400 section if they want to become rated.
3 SCHOLASTIC-ONLY RATED SECTIONS: Under 400, Under 800 and Under 1200: These sections require
an active US Chess Federation membership (https://new.uschess.org/join-us-chess). New players
wanting a rating play in the Under 400.
OPEN SECTION: This Section is available to both adults and scholastic players. Scholastic players rated
over 1199 must play in this section; however, any scholastic player rated 1000+ may choose to play in
either the Open or kids-only Under 1200 section.
Players will be placed in the section that matches their rating unless granted an exemption by the
Tournament Director. Rated sections may be combined at TD discretion.
ENTRY FEE: Early entry received through 10th February is $35. Registration is $40 from February 11 - 19.
Late registration begins February 20th and is $45.
Same day, onsite registration is $50 and must be completed by 9:00AM to be paired for Round 1. Late
sign ups may receive a ½ point round one bye.
REGISTRATION: CLICK HERE , fill out the form, and pay via Zelle to [email protected]
BYES: If you have a scheduling conflict and plan to skip one or two rounds, 1/2 Point Byes are available
and should be requested at the time of registration.
INDIVIDUAL PRIZES: Trophies for 1st, 2nd, 3rd place in each SCHOLASTIC section and cash or gift cards
for the Open section.
TEAM PRIZES: Team Trophies to top 3 schools based on weighted points of 4 players. Must have a
minimum of 3 players from the same school playing in the USCF Rated Sections to qualify for Team
Prizes.
FOOD – We plan to have food vendors to supply snacks and lunch.
Sets, boards and notation sheets supplied. Please bring chess clocks if possible.
CONTACT: [email protected] or 7708158221 FOR QUESTIONS
Address: 909 Holcomb Bridge
Rosewell , GA 30076
United States

events.name: Open Section at 2026 Greater Austin Scholastic Championships
events.sourceText:
Open Section at 2026 Greater Austin Scholastic Championships
NYOS Charter School
Saturday, February 21, 2026
Event Overview
USCF rated chess tournament on February 21, 2026 for adults and more advanced scholastic players. 4 round Swiss at G/45 +5.
Full pairings and standings can be found at the registration link below (click on the blue “Live” text to get to them).
Register HERE ! When you click the link, scroll to the bottom for registration.
See Preregistration List HERE
Basics
This is a Swiss-system tournament, so everyone plays all day—there is no “elimination.” Players must know how to play the game of chess! We follow USCF rules including: touch-move, mandatory clocks (bring your own if at all possible), and mandatory notation. If registrations exceed 32, we reserve the right to split into two sections.
Location
NYOS Charter School
12333 N Lamar Blvd
Austin, TX 78753
Eligibility
All adults
Any youth who have reached at least 1300 by the February 2026 USCF supplement.
Ineligible entries will be moved to the appropriate scholastic section of the 2026 Greater Austin Scholastic Championships .
This is a rated tournament. You must have a USCF ID and your membership (can be purchased/renewed at check out or online with the USCF in advance of registration) . You can verify your USCF membership ID and expiration by visiting the USCF’s Member Services Area . Anyone can become a USCF member. Players new to tournament chess are welcome to play. Your USCF membership cannot expire before February 28, 2026.
Schedule
No check-in necessary for preregistrations. We will make every attempt to contact you in advance if we see a problem with your registration. Verify your entry ONLINE!
9:00 a.m. Open section begins. Open has 4 rounds, all rounds are are G/45, +5.
No changes for round 1 (bye or section) allowed after online registration closes. Requests for byes, withdrawals, player info edits be made onsite with your chief TD and go into effect as of round 2.
Approximate Round Times
Open Section:
rd 1 – 9:00am, rd2 – 11:00am, rd3 – 1:30pm, rd4 – 3:30pm
Notes
There will be some down time between rounds since many games will finish early. We will provide an area (outside the tournament room) for casual “skittles” chess and/or other indoor activities.
Concessions TBA. Only water bottles allowed at the chess board.
Awards
Cash prizes (to winners in both sections, in the case of multiple sections), based on number of entries. Special trophies will be awarded to the highest scoring Family & Child teams (Uncles, Aunts, Adult siblings, Parents, or Grandparents paired with at least one scholastic aged player.).
Registration Information
Entry fee pricing is staggered and based on date of entry/payment.
*youth – $35/adult – $25 through Saturday, 1/31/2026.
*youth – $45/adult – $35 through Saturday, 2/14/2026.
*Late entry youth-$50 / adult – $40 begins Sunday, 2/15/2026 and ENDS at midnight on Wednesday 2/18/26, at which time online entry closes.
*If space permits, onsite registration on Saturday, 2/21/26 will be permitted, $50 regardless of age. Cash or venmo only. First round play requires registration and payment before 8:45am.
Withdrawals requested via email before midnight on Wednesday 2/18/26 are eligible for a refund (minus a $10 service fee). No exceptions. NO email/phone entries.
If you need byes, request them by adding a note when you register. First bye receives 1/2-point. Further byes receive 0-points. Email the registrar to make changes to your requested byes. Deadline to add or remove a 1st round requested bye is 9am Friday 2/20/2026. All 1/2-point byes must be requested/removed before the end of round 2.
Email Sarah Brauner ( Click here to show mail address ) with other questions. No phone calls, please. Emails will be returned promptly.
Organized by Rocks & Rooks

Austin , TX 78753
United States

Rising Star February Grand Prix
Mesa DoubleTree by Hilton
Saturday, February 21, 2026
Event Overview
Rising Star February Grand Prix
Saturday, Feb 21st, 2026
Location:
Mesa DoubleTree by Hilton
1011 West Holmes Ave
Mesa, AZ 85210
Format: 4-round Swiss tournament
Time Control : G/45;+10
Six Sections:
Open (2000 and up)
Class A (1800-1999)
Class B (1600-1799)
Class C (1400-1599)
Class D (1200-1399)
U1200 (1199 and Under)
Players within 100 points of rating floor of a higher section may play up for an additional $5.
Important:
• All sections USCF dual-rated.
• USCF membership required (may join or renew here: USCF join or renew or on site).
• The official published February 2026 USCF Regular ratings will be used for section eligibility, pairings, and
prize eligibility. Higher unofficial USCF ratings might be used for playing up, or for other purposes.
• A maximum of two half-point byes are available. Half-point byes must be requested no later than
30 minutes before the round starts for rounds 1-2. Half-point byes for rounds 3-4 must be requested
before the start of round 2 and may not be revoked after round 2 starts.
• Boards, sets, clocks AND pens will be provided for all sections.
Prizes: $1000 Prize Fund (based on 80 paid paid entries):
Open: 1st -- $120, 2nd -- $90, 3rd -- $60, 1st U2200: $30
Class A: 1st -- $90, 2nd -- $60, 3rd -- $45
Class B: 1st -- $60, 2nd -- $45, 3rd -- $30
Class C: 1st -- $60, 2nd -- $45, 3rd -- $30
Class D: 1st -- $60, 2nd -- $45, 3rd -- $30
U1200: 1st -- $40, 2nd -- $30, 3rd -- $15, 1st U800: $15
All players earn Rising Star Grand Prix points. See Rising Star Grand Prix Policy for details.

$30 deducted from FIDE-titled players' prize winnings if entered after Fri, Feb 13, 2026

Re-entry fees: $5 after round 1, $10 after round 2.

Online registration is available until 11:59 pm MST Fri, Feb 20th
On-site registration is available until 8:30 am on Sat, Feb 21 before round 1.
After round 1 starts, late on-site registration is available with half-point byes for any previous rounds.

Refunds: Refunds may be requested until one hour before the start of round 1. No refunds will be given after that time. All refunds will incur a 5% processing fee.
