events.name: SCHOLASTIC SUNDAY by Indy Chess
events.sourceText:
SCHOLASTIC SUNDAY by Indy Chess
St. Monica Catholic School Gym (Door 15)
Sunday, March 1, 2026
Event Overview
REGISTER FOR THIS TOURNAMENT HERE: https://www.indychess.org/events
Kids who have learned how the pieces move and some basic strategy are welcome to enter the world of rated chess tournaments! All school-aged kids from kindergarten to 12th grade are welcome. Walk-ins are discouraged, as we would appreciate all registering online in advance. The chess playing room is a silent atmosphere to enable maximum concentration.
For the "rated" tournament, all players MUST be members of the US Chess Federation ($24/year). Before registering for the rated event, become a member of USCF here (you will need to write down your child's USCF ID#). However, being a member of Indy Chess--our local club--at $50/year/student or $75/year/family is optional. If interested, you can do that here to get a $5 discount on this event and every other one you attend this year with us, including Weekly Tuesdays, and support the growth of chess in Indy!
[If a beginner and wanting to play in the "casual" tournament (unrated, does not require USCF membership), that is explained far below.]
Here are the details:
Check-in on site: 1:45-2:00pm, entering the door up a few exterior stairs/ramp (not the street-level door). Games start right after a player meeting at 2:15pm.
4ss: Four rounds in a "Swiss" system. A Swiss tournament--the most common chess form--means every player plays every round, with future rounds pairing those who won and those who lost. Up to two 1/2-point byes can be requested by emailing [email protected] or telling the tournament director at the event which rounds you would like byes. Note: Premiere section is 3 rounds.
G/25+5: Games are 25 minutes on each players clock, plus 5 seconds added to a player's time when they hit the clock every move.
USCF-rated: All players must be members of the US Chess Federation and provide a member ID# in online registration. This will give each child a "rating" in chess that will follow them with each tournament they play. Ratings are in blitz, quick, and regular play, and the 25+5 time control affects their regular and their quick rating.
Entry fee is $20/kid, or $15 for members of Indy Chess.
Kids rated under 1000 are divided into three sections so kids play only those in their age group (e.g., 3rd Grade & Under, 6th Grade & Under, and 12th Grade & Under). Want your child to "play up?" Just email Mike at [email protected] . Notation is optional but encouraged in these sections.
There is one "Premiere" section for kids rated 1000 or above (published rating from the 1st of the month). Notation is required in the premiere sections. The Premiere section is three rounds, and may be split by rating at TD discretion to achieve less than eight players per section.
Casual Tournament:
Alongside the rated tournament, kids can instead register for a casual tournament (i.e., unrated) which will begin at the same time. The games will be optionally clocked, notation is not required, and the tournament director will determine section splits based on turnout. It will be a Swiss tournament (i.e., all players play all rounds, unless someone gets a bye due to an odd number). There will be four rounds. There are trophies for the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd place winners!
Other details:
Children under 12 years old must have an adult present and responsible for them, unless the parent/guardian has the permission of the tournament director.
Concessions are typically available for sale by St. Monica, including hot food (less likely in summer months).
An outside playground is available.
Parents may watch chess silently from the bleachers in the gym, or sit at tables in the cafeteria. There is a guest WiFi network with password August27.
The site is wheelchair accessible.
Parking is free in the school lot (Door 15 is located near the southeast side of the building), but is sometimes full right at 1:45p due to a church function. Parking on a nearby street for overflow is available.
Chess sets, clocks, and notation sheets are provided for up to 60 kids. If the child has played in a tournament or two prior, it is helpful if they bring a regulation set and/or clock to ensure there are enough.
Trophies are provided to the top five finishers in each of the three lower sections. In the premiere section, a $50 Amazon gift card goes to the winner (decided by 5+0 blitz playoff if need be, Black/White randomly chosen). Biggest upset earns a medal (unrated does not qualify).
Players who notate at least one game get to pick a prize from the bin at the end of the tournament! Learn how to notate chess moves here (YouTube link).
Questions? Email Mike at [email protected] . We hope to see you there!

TCA Region V Scholastic 2026 (Elementary)
The Houston Chess Studio
Sunday, March 1, 2026
Event Overview
TCA Region V Scholastic 2026 (Elementary)
Date & Location
Date: March 1, 2026
Location: The Houston Chess Studio 250 Patton St. Suite I Houston, TX 77079
Contact Info
Organizer: Edgar Acosta
Email: [email protected]
Phone: (281) 844 4139
Pricing
Early Registration: $32, ends on January 31, 2026
Regular Registration: $37, between February 1 - 15, 2026
Late Registration: $40, between February 16 - 27, 2026
Active USCF membership is required by February 16, 2026. Visit new.uschess.org/join-us-chess starting at $24 to join USCF or renew your membership!
Visit chess.jliptrap.us/hgroup.htm for $13 discount Scholastic memberships and renewals!
TCA Tournament membership is included in the tournament entry fee. Visit texaschess.org/memberships to join TCA or renew your membership!
Pricing is included in the registration form automatically.
Eligibility
Participants must live or attend school in one of these counties:
Austin, Brazoria, Brazos, Chambers, Fort Bend, Galveston, Grimes
Hardin, Harris, Houston, Jasper, Leon, Liberty, Madison
Matagorda, Montgomery, Newton, Orange, Polk, Robertson
San Jacinto, Trinity, Tyler, Walker, Waller, Wharton
The max number of registrations for this tournament is 74. Text Edgar Acosta to join a waiting list
Sections
Elementary Open : Any Elementary student may enter this section.
Elementary U700 : Only Elementary students rated 700 or below may enter this section.
Note: Sections may be combined in case of low registrations.
Definitions:
High School - Grades 9-12; in some districts 10-12, if Junior High is 7-9.
Middle School - Grades 6 to 8 or 9 depending on how the school district divides them.
Elementary - K-6 if 6th grade is in the Elementary building, K-5 if 6 is in Middle School. A 5th-6th campus has been ruled Elementary, a 6th-only campus as Middle School.
Primary - K-3. Note that a first grader could enter K-1 or K-3 or K-5.
K-8 and K-12 schools and Home School Associations are divided K-5, 6-8, and 9-12.
Students not assigned a grade in school will be assigned a grade at the tournament based on their age as of September 1 of that school year as follows: six years old is assigned first grade, seven years old is assigned second grade, and so on through grade twelve.
Note: Sections are based on USCF January 2026 ratings. "Current" ratings may be used to pair unrated players but will not determine section placement. Accelerate Pairings will be used at the discretion of the TD the day of the tournament.
Tournament Format
Rounds: Swiss 5 Rounds, Game in 25 with a 5-second delay (G/25 d/5).
Membership: USCF and TCA memberships required.
Rules: USCF rules apply.
Open sections require notation and clocks (if available). Players who opt to not take notation will have their time start at 20 minutes instead of 25.
Reserved sections are strongly encouraged to use notation and clocks.
Touch-move / Touch-take: Applies to all sections. Younger players, especially in Kinder-1st Open, will be encouraged to keep these rules with gentle reminders as needed.
Equipment: Plan on bringing your own chess set and clock if you have one, money for lunch, and a good attitude! Every player needs to bring their clocks!
Please make sure your clocks are labeled with the player's name and USCF ID.
Chess sets for the whole tournament will be provided!
Schedule
No At-Site Registration. All registrations must be submitted online at before 11:59pm on February 27, 2026.
Please arrive between 8:15 and 8:45 to check in and get ready to play.
Round 1: Starts at 9:00 AM SHARP; subsequent rounds will start ASAP. No elimination.
Players may request a single 1/2 point Bye missed, 0 point Bye for any subsequent Byes. Any Byes need to be requested by Friday February 27th, 2026 at 7pm.
Lunch break after Round 3, estimating 12pm-1pm.
Teams
Teams consist of two or more (2+) players in the same section from the same school/association.
Team members must attend the same school campus full-time or belong to the same Home School Association .
Sections are not combined for teams.
Team scores will be calculated by summing the top four (4) individual scores from each team.
Awards
Trophies: Top 5 individuals in each section and Top 4 teams in each section.
1st Place Finishers qualify for a spot in the State Regional Invitational April 18-19th .
Alternate awards (likely medals) to players who score 3 or more points but do not win a trophy.
Tie Breaks: Solkoff (sum of opponents' scores), Modified Median (dropping the lowest opponent's score), Cumulative of Opposition, then Cumulative (USCF Standard)
We look forward to seeing you at The Houston Chess Studio on February 27, 2026 for a day of competitive and fun scholastic chess!

Growth Chess Center
Wednesday, March 4, 2026
- Wednesday, March 25, 2026
Event Overview
1. Dates & Location
Four Wednesdays March 4th, 11th, 18th, 25th
Location: Growth Chess Center 4506 Regent St Madison, WI
2. Tournament Format:
Tournament Format: Individual Swiss
Two Sections: Open & Reserve (U1500), if there are less than 6 players in either sections will be combined. Prizes will still be separate.
Total Rounds: 4 (1 round each Wednesday night)
Round Times: Wednesdays at 6:30PM
Time Control Open: G/60+30 (Game in 60 minutes with 30 second increment on each move)
3. Byes
Byes are available for players in any rounds in case they can't participate that evening, but would like to stay in the tournament.
A maximum of one half-point byes can be requested in this tournament.
Round 1-3 byes must be requested prior to the pairing of the round. Pairings usually are posted shortly after noon on Tuesday, the day before the round.
Round 4 byes must be requested before start of Round 3. Round 4 bye is irrevocable to prevent possible prize-fund manipulations.
Late registrations will receive a half-point bye for any missed round, up to a total one round.
4. Prizes -- $600 based on 20 paid entries. Prizes will increase proportionally after 40 entries. Single Game Entries are not counted towards the based on prizes.
1st place $160

3rd place $80

Unrated players may enter any section for which they are otherwise eligible.

The Houston Chess Studio
Friday, March 6, 2026
- Sunday, March 8, 2026
Event Overview
$2,500 MARCH CHAMPIONSHIP 2026
Open to Poison Pawn members AND non-members*
US CHESS RATED - MUST BE A US CHESS MEMBER TO PARTICIPATE
WHEN: MARCH 6-8 or MARCH 7-8 Three-day or two-day schedule, take your pick.
WHERE: Houston Chess Studio, 250 Patton St. Suite H, Houston TX 77009
FORMAT: 5 round Swiss, G/90, +30. (round 1 of 2 day schedule is G/60,d5)
3 day schedule : Round 1 at 6:30pm Friday night . Round 2 at 1pm Saturday and Round 3 at 6pm. Round 4 at 9:30 am Sunday and Round 5 at 2:00 pm.
2 day schedule : Round 1 is at 9:30am Saturday morning and is G/60, d5. Then merges with the 3 day schedule for rounds 2-5.
ENTRY FEE: Non-members $105 thru Friday FEB 20TH; then $125 thru Wednesday MAR 4TH; $135 thereafter. Poison Pawns club members $80 anytime! For membership info contact Edgar at : Click here to show mail address GMs and IMs may enter free, their entry fee will be deducted from winnings.
2 SECTIONS: Championship (1900 and up); Challengers (U1900).
PLAYING UP: If you are rated U1900 but are at least 1700 you may play up into the Championship section for $35.
PRIZE FUND $2,500 - 1st place in each section is guaranteed . 2nd place and 3rd place 25% OF ENTRY FEES B/50. 15% BONUS FOR CLUB MEMBERS in all sections combined. Championship 1st $800 ; Challengers 1st $550 . Un-rated may play in any section but are limited to winning $150 except in the top section where they are eligible for all prizes. DRAWS PRIOR TO 30 MOVES AND BOTH PLAYERS ARE INELIGIBLE FOR ANY PRIZE MONEY!
ONLY MEMBERS OF POISON PAWNS CHESS CLUB ARE ONLY ELIGIBLE FOR 100% OF THE CASH PRIZES ! (So isn't it time you joined!)

CANCELLATION: You may cancel up to 72 hours before the beginning of Round 1 and get a refund of what you paid minus $25, or you may apply the entire amount towards a future entry fee IF USED WITHIN 30-DAYS OF ORIGINAL EVENT .
BYES: One ½ point bye available, must be declared before the beginning of round 2. No last round byes except for zero point byes.
RE-ENTRY: If you are in the 3-day schedule, after round 1, you may re-enter immediately for $35 and be given a choice of a ½ point bye for round 1 OR you may choose to play in round 1 of the 2-day schedule. If you are in the 2-day schedule you may re-enter immediately after round 1 and take a ½ point bye for round 1.

There are 3 restaurants in the same strip center as The Studio: The Red Hot Noodle (Asian), Subway , and Patron Pizza . Several others are within walking distance. Plenty of FREE parking.

events.sourceText:
2026 Virginia Scholastic & College Chess Championships
Heritage Event, State Championship Event
Thomas Jefferson High School for S&T
Friday, March 6, 2026
- Sunday, March 8, 2026
Event Overview
PRE-TOURNAMENT ANNOUNCEMENT
2026 Virginia Scholastic & College
Chess Championships
hosted by
Thomas Jefferson High School
for Science and Technology
Saturday-Sunday, March 7-8, 2026
6560 Braddock Rd., Alexandria VA
WHAT : The Virginia Chess Federation (VCF) is partnering with Thomas Jefferson High School for Science and Technology for the 2026 Virginia Scholastic & College Chess Championships.
WHEN : Saturday and Sunday, March 7-8, 2026, with a Blitz Tournament on Friday night, March 6th.
REGISTRATION : We will open Registration at www.vachess.org by December 1st, 2025. Specific entry fees have not yet been determined; they are pending final logistical arrangements with the venue. Please do not contact TJ High School , they are relying on the VA Chess Federation to answer all questions about the tournament and event logistics.
HOTEL ARRANGEMENTS : TBD. We will seek agreements with hotels close to the High School. Details will be posted on the VCF website, www.vachess.org .
EVENT FORMAT : The tournament has nine (9) sections:
College: One section, with all games on Saturday.
K-12 Championship and K-12 Under 1400
K-8 Championship and K-8 Under 1200
K-5 Championship and K-5 Under 1000
K-3 Championship and K-3 Under 600
TOURNAMENT SCHEDULE :
Friday, March 6th: On-site Registration for the Main Event and Blitz. Round 1 of BLITZ is at 6:30 PM.
Saturday, March 7th: Rounds 1-3 at 9 am, 12:30 pm, and 4:30 pm. College Section games are at 9, noon, 3 pm, and 6 pm. Parents & Friends tournament starts at 12:45.
Sunday, March 8th: Rounds 4-5 at 9:30 am and 1:30 pm. Awards Ceremonies held by section as soon as possible after the last game finishes in a section.
TEAMS : Teams must be comprised of players who attend the same school. A school is not required to have a “chess club” or “official school team” to form a team for this tournament. Two or more players who go to the same school and play in the same section of the tournament are automatically considered a team for the purposes of this tournament. More details will be available when we open registration.
PLAYER ELIGIBILITY :
All players in the Scholastic sections (K-12, K-8, K-5, K-3) must be Virginia residents .
In the College section, players must be attending college in VA or be a VA resident attending college out of state. All college players must be high school graduates.
U.S. Chess Federation membership is required for all players. Players can join US Chess or renew their membership through the VCF at www.vachess.org and select the “Join US Chess” tab on the left side of the webpage. We offer all Virginians a small discount on US Chess Federation membership. If you prefer, you also can join/renew your US Chess membership directly with US Chess, go to www.uschess.org .
IMPORTANT : The VCF uses the results of this tournament to identify and nominate representatives to attend the US national tournaments of State Champions. These tournaments (see list below) will be held in early August in conjunction with the U.S. Open in Grand Rapids, Michigan. The VCF provides stipends to assist the Viriginia players selected to represent The Commonwealth at these tournaments.
Denker Tournament of High School State Champions (Grades 9-12)
Barber Tournament of Middle School State Champions (Grades 6-8)
Rockefeller Tournament of Elementary School State Champions (Grades 4-5)
NEW for 2026 : Maurice Ashley Tournament of Primary School State Champions (Grades K-3)
Haring Tournament of Girls State Champions
FUN SIDE EVENTS :
BLITZ on Friday evening March 6th (Round 1 at 6:30 pm). 4 double-rounds (2 games per round for 8 total games).
4-round “Parents & Friends” tournament open to adults. Scholastic or college players are NOT eligible to play in this event.
“Challenge the Master” Simultaneous Exhibition.
TEAM ROOMS : We are working with the TJ High School administration to obtain a number of classrooms that can be used by teams with 10 or more players as well as by parents who wish to form a group in order to get a team room. Please do not contact the school for any information about this, the school relies on the VA Chess Federation to collect and consolidate all Team Room requests.
PRE-EVENT ZOOM INFO MEETINGS : The VCF will organize several options for players and parents to attend a pre-event Zoom Meeting in mid-to-late February 2026.

Alexandria , VA 22312

Side Events : Parents & Friends Tournament (starts 15 minutes after Round 2 in the Scholastic Sections ... e.g., 12:45 PM on Saturday)
“Play the Master” simultaneous Exhibition on Saturday afternoon beginning about 2 PM.
TOURNAMENT SCHEDULE :
Friday, March 6th : On-site Registration for the Main Event and Blitz. Round 1 of BLITZ is at 6:30 PM . Blitz is an optional event. Blitz is usually finished about 8:30 or 8:45 PM.
Saturday, March 7th : Round 1 at 9 AM . Rounds 2-3 at 12:30 pm and 4:30 pm. College Section games are at 9, noon, 3 pm, and 6 pm. Parents & Friends tournament starts at 12:45.
Sunday, March 8th : Rounds 4-5 at 9:30 am and 1:30 pm. Awards Ceremonies held section-by-section as soon as possible after the last game finishes in a section. NOTE: We remind everyone that Daylight Savings Time begins Sunday, March 8th .
TEAMS : Scholastic and College Teams must be comprised of players who attend the same school. A school is not required to have a “chess club” or an “official school team” to play as a team for this tournament. Two or more players who go to the same school and play in the same section of the tournament are automatically considered a team for this tournament. You can find detailed team eligibility information on the VA Chess website at this helpful link .
PLAYER ELIGIBILITY :
Scholastic Sections : All players in the Scholastic sections (K-12, K-8, K-5, K-3) must be attending school in Virginia or be a VA resident attending school out-of-state. Players attending an out-of-state school cannot compete as a team-- all teams must be Virginia-based schools . Players from neighboring states who attend school in VA are eligible to compete. Please check with us if you have questions!
College Section : Players must be attending college in VA or be a VA resident attending college out of state. All college players must be high school graduates. High school students who are attending college cannot compete on a College team.
U.S. Chess Federation membership is required for all players. Players can join US Chess or renew their membership through the VCF at www.vachess.org and select the “Join/Renew US Chess” tab on the left side of our webpage. We offer a small discount on US Chess Federation membership. If you prefer, you also can join/renew your US Chess membership directly with US Chess, go to www.uschess.org and hover your cursor over the “Join” option near the top of your screen.
AWARDS : Tons of trophies! See www.vachess.org
IMPORTANT : The VCF uses the results of this tournament to select representatives to attend the US national tournaments of State Champions. These tournaments (see list below) will be held in early August as part of the U.S. Open in Grand Rapids, Michigan. The VCF provides healthy stipends to assist the 5 Virginia players who earn the right to represent The Commonwealth at these tournaments.
Denker Tournament of High School State Champions (Top Player in Grades 9-12 from the K-12 Section)
Barber Tournament of Middle School State Champions (Top Player in Grades 6-8, from the K-8 Section)
Rockefeller Tournament of Elementary School State Champions (Top Player in Grades 4-5, from K-5)
NEW for 2026 : Maurice Ashley Tournament of Primary School State Champions (Top Player in K-3)
Haring Tournament of Girls State Champions (Top finishing Girl from Virginia’s K-12 Section)
FUN SIDE EVENTS :
BLITZ on Friday evening March 6th (Round 1 at 6:30 pm). 4 double-rounds (2 games per round for 8 total games). Includes a Parents & Friends section.
4-round “Parents & Friends” tournament open to adults. Scholastic or college players are NOT eligible to play in this event.
“Challenge the Master” Simultaneous Exhibition.
TEAM ROOMS : See www.vachess.org . We are working with the TJ High School administration to obtain about 15 classrooms that can be used by teams with 10 or more players as well as by parents who wish to form a group in order to get a team room. Please do not contact the school for any information about this, the school relies on the VA Chess Federation to collect and consolidate all Team Room requests. The cost for a Team Room is $100 per room of which $25 is returned to you after the tournament and $75 is used to purchase a Gift Card for the teachers whose rooms we use.
PRE-EVENT ZOOM INFO MEETINGS : The VCF will organize several options for players and parents to attend a pre-event Zoom Meeting in mid-to-late February 2026. These events will be announced on our website and emails sent to all registered players.
QUESTIONS : Contact Mike Hoffpauir, VA Chess Federation, Click here to show mail address or text to 757-846-4805.

The VCF is a 501c(3) non-profit organization

State Championship Event

Event Overview
Silver State Chess Association
presents
2026 Northern Nevada State Seniors Championship
March 6-8 2026
Mathewson Bridge Center
125 West Plumb Lane
Reno, NV 89509
Swiss 5 Rounds Game/90+30
Note: Players must be age 50+ prior to Aug 3, 2026.
Players must reside in Nevada in one of the following counties and have their eligible address on file with USCF: Washoe, Humbolt, Elko, Pershing, Storey, Churchill, Lander, Eureka, White Pine, Lyon, Douglas, Mineral and the independent city of Carson City.
Southern Nevada residents should register for the Southern Nevada State Seniors Championship in a separate tournament.
Schedule : (all rounds G/90+30)
Round 1: Friday March 6 @ 6:00 pm
Round 2: Saturday March 7 @ 12:00 pm
Round 3: Saturday March 7 @ 5:00 pm
Round 4: Sunday March 8 @ 12:00 pm
Round 5: Sunday March 8 @ 5:00 pm
Top three winners advance to the State Championship to compete against top three winners from Southern NV in a proctored online tournament to be held at the Mathewson Bridge Center on April 24-26.
Please bring boards, sets, and clocks as none are provided.
Prizes
$1000.00 with 20 paid players:
Top Prize: $500 + Trophy
Second: $350 + Trophy
Third: $150 + Trophy
Top U1900: Trophy
Top U1600: Trophy
Above cash prizes adjusted proportionally for more or fewer players.
Note: Cash prizes will be awarded following the completion of the Nevada State Seniors Championship on April 26. To receive a cash prize in the Northern NV Championship, players must play in the Nevada State Seniors Championship. If a player is unable or unwilling to play in the online Nevada State Seniors Championship, entry and cash prize will be offered to the next highest scoring player.
The winner of the Nevada State Seniors Championship will represent Nevada in the John T. Irwin Tournament of Senior State Champions on August 3-6 (TBD) in Grand Rapids, MI. Silver State Chess will provide a travel stipend of $650 upon completion of the Irwin with no forfeited games.
Maximum number of entries: 40. Registration not confirmed until payment received.
Waitlist will start if/when max entries received.
Entry fee : $99 by March 5, $115 later.
Refunds : may be requested prior to start of Round 1. $15 withheld for processing fees
Entrants may register in person and pay with cash or check at the Reno Chess Club on Thursday evenings 6-9pm before March 6 @ 8:00pm.
Maximum two half-point byes available and must be requested before Round 3 and are irrevocable
US Chess Membership is required.
Please join or renew the player’s membership at www.uschess.org before registering for the tournament.

events.name: Parents & Friends Tournament at the 2026 VA Scholastic Championships
events.sourceText:
Parents & Friends Tournament at the 2026 VA Scholastic Championships
Thomas Jefferson High School for Science and Technology
Friday, March 6, 2026
- Sunday, March 8, 2026
Event Overview
Parents & Friends Tournament
at the 2026 VA Scholastic Championships
Saturday and Sunday, March 7-8, 2026 – with Blitz on Friday March 6th
At the Thomas Jefferson High School for Science & Technology in Alexandria, VA What : Parents & Friends (P&F) Tournament at the VA Scholastic Championships. There’s also a Blitz Tournament on Friday night for Parents & Friends.
New for 2026 : This year in the P&F BLITZ tournament there will be awards for the “Top Parent-Child” Team! A Parent-Child team is defined as a parent playing in the P&F tournament who has at least one child playing in the K-6, 7-12, or College Blitz Tournaments. The award recognizes the top 3 Parent-Child Teams by adding the parent’s blitz score to the blitz score of their highest-finishing child in the scholastic or the college sections.
When : Saturday and Sunday, March 7-8, 2026, with Round 1 on Saturday at 12:45 PM (this is 15 minutes after the start of Round 2 in the Scholastic sections). Blitz is on Friday evening at 6:30 PM.
Where : Thomas Jefferson HS for Science & Tech, 6560 Braddock Rd., Alexandria, VA. Please DO NOT call the school for information about the chess tournament .
Hotels : The Virginia Chess Federation is developing lodging options with several hotels near the school. The properties represent a range of selections and costs. See www.vachess.org for the options available. All hotel deals will have a “cut off”; reservations made after the cut-off date may no longer be eligible to get the “Chess Rate” for lodging.
Event Format : 4 Rounds using the Swiss System. This is NOT an elimination tournament! The Blitz Tournament will have 3 or 4 rounds of play (2 games per round), depending on the number of entries in the Blitz event.
Entry Fees and Registration : Select the “Register Now” button below to register for Parents & Friends!
P&F Main Event Entry Fees: $30 through February 28th ; increases to $35 on March 1st and onsite. Entry onsite permitted on Friday March 7th and Saturday March 8th until 12 noon. Players who register after 12 noon on Saturday might not be paired until Round 2.
P&F Blitz Entry Fees: $20 through February 28th ; increases to $30 on March 1st and onsite.
Registration: On-line at this link or www.vachess.org .
One half-point Bye is available in any of the 4 rounds of the main P&F tournament. No Byes allowed in Blitz.
Sections of Play : All players compete in one section in both the main and blitz P&F tournaments.
Event Schedule for the P&F Events :
Registration Onsite: 4-9 pm on Friday and 9 am to noon on Saturday. Blitz players must be registered by 6 PM to play in Round 1 at 6:30.
Main P&F Tournament Round Times: Saturday : Rounds 1 and 2 at 12:45 pm and 4:45 pm.
Sunday : Rounds 3 and 4 at 9:45 am and 1:45 pm.
Blitz Tournament Round Times : Round 1 at 6:30 PM
Time Controls : All players’ clocks will be set each round using the time controls listed here.
Main P&F Tournament: Round 1: Game-45 + 5 seconds of time increment. This means each player has a total of 45 minutes to complete all moves in each game, plus each player gets an additional 5 seconds after completing each move.
Rounds 2-4: Game-60 + 5 seconds of time increment.
Blitz P&F Tournament: All games use a time control of Game-5, delay 0. You play two games each round. We will play 3 or 4 rounds, depending on the number of entries.
Ratings Used : Players will be paired using the higher of their US Chess over-the-board and online regular ratings found in the US Chess Rating Supplement for March 2026 (to be published by the US Chess Federation on or after Feb 21, 2025). Established ratings have priority over provisional ratings. Ratings from other systems such as FIDE or from another country will be considered, especially when a player has no US Chess rating. Ratings from platforms such as Chess.com, Chesskid.com, Lichess.com, and ICC are not used. The Chief TD makes the final decisions about all players’ ratings used in the tournament.
Awards : All awards are gift certificates to the onsite Chess Book & Equipment Store. There are no cash awards. Gift certificates must be redeemed onsite and cannot be exchanged for cash. Trophies/Plaques to Top 3 Parent-Child Teams.
Player Eligibility :
The Parents & Friends event is not open to players eligible to compete in the College or Scholastic sections of the main tournament. You do not need to have a child playing in the main tournament to participate in our P&F events!
A current US Chess Federation membership is required for all participants. Renew your US Chess membership or become a new US Chess member through the VA Chess Federation at www.vachess.org and select the “Join/Renew US Chess” tab on the left side of the screen. Joining the US Chess Federation through the VA Chess Federation saves you a little money.

2026 Texas Scholastic “Super State” Championship
State Championship Event
DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel Austin
Saturday, March 7, 2026
- Sunday, March 8, 2026
Event Overview
2026 Texas Scholastic “Super State” Championship
March 7, 2026 to March 8, 2026
DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel Austin
6505 N Interstate 35, Austin, TX, 78752
Registration is limited to the first 800 players.
Sections
K-1 Championship
Primary K-3 JV (U700)
Primary K-3 Championship
Elementary School K-5/6 JV* (U800)
Elementary School K-5/6 Championship*
Middle School 6-8 JV (U900)

Eligibility
The event is open only to Texas residents with a valid US Chess (valid through March 2026) and TCA membership. All sections are US Chess rated, and the March 2026 US Chess rating supplement will be used for pairings and prizes.
Winners of the Championship sections will earn official Texas State Champion titles. The top finishers in key sections will also qualify for the 2026 Texas Junior Invitational , and team results determine qualification for the 2026 Lone Star Cup .
Entry Fees
$65 by February 7, $75 by February 21, $85 by March 6 by 9pm, Onsite $95 with 1st round bye.

6505 N Interstate 35, Austin, TX, 78752

Players who fail to appear within 30 minutes of round start forfeit the game unless the Chief TD otherwise provides for good cause.

Texas Scholastic Puzzles Championship: TBD. The entry fee is $20.
TCA Junior Chess Meeting: This is a business meeting where members will hear reports from officers and vote on important business affecting the Association. All TCA members who are Texas residents and at least 16 years of age are voting members. Everyone is welcome to attend. An agenda will be posted on the TCA website at least two weeks in advance.
Other Rules and Information
Chess sets provided; bring your own clock
Notation required except for K-1 and Primary JV. Time deduction will be ⅓ of your time for no notation. Must use tournament provided notation.
Food and drinks are not allowed in the playing hall. Water is the only exception.

Only players whose game is in progress, tournament directors and staff, TCA officers, and press are allowed in the hall during rounds.
Refunds available until March 4th, subject to a $20 fee.

58th annual New York State Scholastic Championships, OPEN TO GRADES K-8 ONLY
Heritage Event, American Classic, Junior Grand Prix, State Championship Event
Saratoga Hilton Hotel and 3 other nearby locations
Saturday, March 7, 2026
- Sunday, March 8, 2026
Event Overview
An American Classic!
A Heritage Event!
US Chess Junior Grand Prix!
A State Championship Event!
MAR 7-8, 2026. NEW YORK.
58th annual New York State Scholastic Championships (out of state players allowed but with prize restrictions)-- OPEN TO GRADES K-8 ONLY. See separate TLA, 2/28-3/1, for NY State High School Championship , for grades 9-12 (grades 6-8 also permitted on 2/28-3/1, but with some prize restrictions). 6-SS, G/60, d10, top NYS player and team in each Championship section are NY State Champions. In 12 separate sections: 1). Middle School (K-8) Championship (top NYS grade 6-8 born after 9/1/10 qualifies for Barber National Tournament of State K-8 Champions), 2). K-8 Under 1700 Section, 3). K-8 Under 1300, 4). K-8 Under 900; 5). Elementary (K-5) Championship (top NYS player born after 9/1/13 qualifies for Rockefeller National Tournament of State K-5 Champions), 6). K-5 Under 1400, 7). K-5 Under 1000 , 8). K-5 Under 600; 9). Primary (K-3) Championship (top NYS grade K-3 born after 9/1/15 qualifies for Ashley National Tournament of State K-3 Champions), 10). K-3 Under 800; 11). K-1 Championship, 12). K-1 Under 400 Section. In four separate playing locations: Saratoga Hilton Hotel (K-3 Under 800, K-1 Championship, K-1 Under 400 sections), 534 Broadway, I-87 Exit 13-N, 4 miles north on US 9 (Hilton Chess parking rate: $6 daytime, $12 overnight); Saratoga Springs City Center (K-8 Under 900, K-5 Under 1400, K-5 Under 1000, K-5 Under 600, K-3 Championship), adjacent to Saratoga Hilton Hotel (connected by indoor walkway), 522 Broadway; Saratoga Music Hall (K-5 Championship Section), 2½ blocks south of Convention Center at 474 Broadway; Courtyard By Marriott Hotel (K-8 Championship, K-8 Under 1700, K-8 Under 1300), 11 Excelsior Ave., 2/5 mile north of Saratoga Hilton; Saratoga Springs, NY 12866. Some K-5 Under 1400 Section games might also be played at Saratoga Music Hall. Sections at Hilton/City Center may be limited to a total of 1200 players, sections at Marriott may be limited 340 players, section(s) at Music Hall may be limited to 220 players. Team prizes based on top 4 scores from same school, teams of 2 or 3 allowed, but are at a disadvantage. Players are subject to the specific rating and grade requirements for each section (Championship sections open to all players meeting grade requirements); the four Middle School (K-8) sections are open to players in grades 8 and below; the four Elementary (K-5) sections are open to players in grades 5 and below; the two Primary (K-3) sections are open to players in grades 3 and below; the two K-1 sections are open to players grades 1/below; unrated players meeting grade requirements allowed in any section. Online entry fee at chessaction.com, all sections (space permitting) : $120 per player by 2/7/26, $160 by 2/23. REGISTRATION MAY CLOSE PRIOR TO THESE DATES DUE TO SPACE LIMITATIONS. Entries may be subject to wait list. If registration is still open, entry fee after 2/23 until advance registration closes is $200. On-site entries: $250 and may not be available this year. USCF Membership Required. Special 1-year USCF dues if paid online with entry: see chessaction.com. Trophies, plaques or medals to top 10 players & top 5 teams each section, top 2 unrated in U900, U800, U600 & U400, top 2 each U1800, U1600, U1400 (K-8 Championship), U1500, (K-8 U1700), U1100 (K-8 U1300), U700, U500, U300 (K-8 U900), U1700, U1500 (K-5 Championship), U1200, U1000 (K-5 U1400), U800, U700 (K-5 U1000), U500, U400, U300 (K-5 U600), U1400, U1200, U1000 (K-3 Championship), U600, U500, U400, U300 (K-3 U800), U800, U600, U400 (K-1), U300, U200 (K-1 U400). Speed playoff if 6-0 tie. Free/reduced entry fee prizes to all CCA OTB tournaments (only for players residing in NY and/or attending NY schools) : Championship sections: 8 months 1st, 6 months 2nd, 4 months 3rd & 4th. Other sections: 6 months 1st, 4 months 2nd, 3 months 3rd & 4th. 2 months bonus entries to NY players with 6-0 scores. Some CCA events also have minimum rating requirements and/or additional surcharges, based on rating, to play in the top sections; the free/reduced entry fee prizes do not cover any such additional surcharges for playing in the top sections. Schedule: Rounds begin Sat 11, 2, 5; Sun 9, 12, 3. Awards: about 5:30 pm Sun. Recipients responsible for arranging delivery and/or replacement of awards not claimed at site. Half point byes OK all, limit 2, must commit before round 2. HR:see chessevents.us for rates, minimum stay and other details (hotel reservations links at chessevents.us should be open by mid-November or sooner). Hotels may sell out very quickly but could have availability much later due to late cancellations. For backup hotels see chessevents.us. Special car rentals: Avis, 800-331-1600, use AWD #D657633. $15 per player service charge for refunds. Section switches subject to $20 extra charge after 2/23 (all substitutions from advance list subject to space limitations and charged late fee), no section switching or substitutions after 5 pm 3/5. Questions: chesstour.com, [email protected] . Bring digital clock if possible- none supplied. March official ratings used (except unofficial USCF ratings or USCF Online Regular ratings usually used if otherwise unrated). Players with USCF Online Regular ratings over 100 points over their OTB ratings may be assigned higher tournament rating and may be required to play in higher section (TD may use USCF Scholastic Regulations for eligibility guidance). TD reserves right to assign estimated rating to players with non-USCF ratings. Electronic devices rules: Electronic scorekeeping devices not allowed. See also www.devicerules.com; players may not possess cellphones during play but may store them in bag under table. Entry: www.chessaction.com . No mail entries. Blitz tournament: 8 pm Sat, enter at site Sat by 7:40 pm.

G/45;d5 - Quad Format - No Prizes - All ratings welcome. $10 entry - cash only - Adults and Kids Welcome No Late Entries - No Byes - No Withdrawals ONSITE REGISTRATION ONLY US Chess Membership Required, will affect quick and regular rating.

What is Quad Format? Players are grouped in order of rating. The top four are grouped, then the next four are grouped, and so on. The groups (quads) of four play each other in a three-round round-robin. No late entries, no withdrawals . Quads are round robins. Please do not play if you can't stay for all three games. Leaving in the middle of a quad is rude and provides an extreme inconvenience to the other three players in your quad.

CKQ Saturday Piscataway Rapids
Chess Kings & Queens Academy
Saturday, March 7, 2026
Event Overview
CKQ Saturday Piscataway Rapids
Start time: Players should arrive no later than 4:15 p.m. The first game begins promptly at 4:30. Latecomers risk their clock running when they arrive.
End time: The Under 600 section typically ends by 8:30 p.m., the Under 1200 section more like 9:00. The tournament could go a bit longer if players use all their time.
Players: Most players at this event will be children (ages 6-16), but adults are welcome to play. Beginners are welcome, but at a minimum players should know how to legally move chess pieces, recognize when they’re in check, and how to perform basic checkmates (ex; king and queen vs. king).
Structure / time controls: 4-SS, G30 +5. (Each player will play four games. Each player receives 30 minutes per game, plus another five seconds per move.)
Sections: Under 600 and Under 1200 rating sections. The Under 1200 section requires at least 500 rating to enter. Lower-rated and unrated players may enter with the tournament director's permission.
Requirements: A USCF membership is required to play in the tournament. Contact the tournament director if you need assistance creating or renewing a membership.
Equipment: Players do not need to bring any equipment. Players are recommended to eat before arriving, or at least bring a snack.
Registration: The registration fee is $25. Online registration closes at 5pm on the day of the event.
Byes: If you can’t attend the entire tournament, a half-point bye (limit one) is available for any round. Byes must be requested before the tournaments starts. If you are going to take first-round bye please contact the tournament director at least one hour before the tournament starts.
Prizes: Top three winners in each section receive a trophy or a medal.
For more information: Contact tournament director Stephen Lorimor ( [email protected] , phone/text: 908-286-0720).

Event Overview
FIRST SATURDAY ONLINE GRAND PRIX
Join our monthly online tournament series - designed for all K-12 chess players who love to compete, learn and grow!
Overview
The First Saturday Online Grand Prix is a seven-tournament scholastic series open to all K-12 students nationwide.
Each monthly event offers its own prize and also counts toward the overall Grand Prix leaderboard. Players may join any number of tournaments.
Schedule
Platform : lichess.org
Time control : G/15; +5 seconds increment
Start Time : 10 AM EST
Format : 4 rounds Swiss
Dates : November 1, 2025; December 6, 2025; January 3, 2026; February 7, 2026; March 7, 2026; April 4, 2026; May 2 2026.
Entry fee : $20
Prizes
1st place winner of each tournament: One free private online lesson with WFM Bahar Hallayeva (An exclusive opportunity to learn directly from a titled chess master!)
Grand Prix Points and Series Awards
Players earn Grand Prix points in each tournament. Cumulative points across all seven events determine the Overall Grand Prix Winners:
1st place: Trophy + 3 months of Chess for Everyone weekly online classes ($300 value)
2nd place: Trophy + 2 months of Chess for Everyone weekly online classes ($200 value)
3rd place: Trophy + 1 month of Chess for Everyone weekly online classes ($100 value)

Mississippi Scholastic Chess Association – 2025 Team Tournament Regulations
INTRODUCTION To foster consistency between state and national-level scholastic events, the US Chess Federation encourages state scholastic organizations to adopt the National Scholastic Chess Tournament Regulations for all state scholastic championships. However, the national tournament regulations deal with a great many details and situations that are not likely to be relevant at any of our state team tournaments, so what follows is a summary of the national regulations that will be applied.
The Mississippi Scholastic Chess Association (MSCA) Team Tournament Regulations are intended to fulfill the needs and expectations of players, coaches and parents at our scholastic team chess events.
ELIGIBILITY Age and Grade Eligibility. The following ages are as of September 1 of the school year in which the competition takes place. These age requirements are considered upper bounds for each grade . Our events are grade-based and require all players to play in a section that allows for their current grade.
Kindergarten: 6 years old
1st Grade: 7 years old
7th Grade: 13 years old
2nd Grade: 8 years old
8th Grade: 14 years old
3rd Grade: 9 years old
9th Grade: 15 years old
4th Grade: 10 years old
10th Grade: 16 years old
5th Grade: 11 years old
11th Grade: 17 years old
6th Grade: 12 years old
12th Grade 18 years old
There shall only be one year of eligibility per grade level unless one of the following situations applies: Pre-schoolers may play as Kindergarteners in any event section. Kindergartners and Pre-schoolers may continue to play as Kindergartners in subsequent years until they start the first grade.
Players who repeat a grade in school may have a second year of eligibility in that grade as long as they are age-eligible for that grade.
TEAM REQUIREMENTS
MSCA team tournaments are individual tournaments with team scoring. A student who does not qualify to represent a team can compete only as an individual.
A team is comprised of students who attend the same school. ( Students may “play up” for a school team in the same feeder pattern. i.e. an elementary student can play on a middle school team if that middle school is the school they will be attending in the future according to the feeder pattern ) A school is defined as an institution which has one name, is located in one building or connected adjacent buildings, and is under one on-site administrator and which provides core curricular instruction in English, math, science, and social studies.
A student will be considered to attend a school if and only if he or she physically attends classes at that school building and receives more than 50% of his or her core curricular instruction during those classes.
Each school may enter only one team per section .
Teams may also be comprised of home schooled or virtual school students. A home schooled student is defined as a student who receives at least 50% of his or her core curricular instruction at home. Virtual school students are students who receive more than 50% of their core curricular instruction on-line, but not in a school building.
A home schooled or virtual school student has the following two options for participating on a scholastic chess team:
The student may join with other home schooled or virtual school students who reside within the boundary of the same local public school as defined in 3.2.
The student may join with other home schooled students who physically attend the same instructional program.
There may be more than one home school or virtual school team per recognized public school district.
A scholastic team must contain a minimum of two players to be eligible for team prizes.
There is no maximum number of players who may compete on a team, but only the top four(4) scores in any section count for team score.
The coach, an adult team representative, or the ‘Team Captain’ is responsible for assuring that all of the team’s players are properly registered and eligible to participate as members of the team.
TOURNAMENT FORMAT Mississippi scholastic team tournaments are individual tournaments with team scoring . Accordingly, they are paired as individual Swiss System tournaments , with individual scores added to create team scores. Whenever a rated section has more than 2N players, where “N” is the number of rounds, the TD will consider using accelerated pairings.
The combined total of the top four scoring players from the same school determines that team’s score.
Players from the same team will not be paired together unless no other reasonable natural pairing can be made.
When conflicts occur between individual pairings and team considerations – and where the top awards are at stake – individual pairings shall have higher priority.
Points from unrated games shall compile toward team score as such: 1 win = 1 point, 1 draw = 0.5 point
Points from RATED games shall compile toward team score as such: 1 win = 2 points, 1 draw = 1 point
Therefore, RATED play will count MORE toward your team score!
RATING SUPPLEMENT
For events starting before the 10th of the month , the previous month’s Rating Supplement will be used. For events starting on or after the 10th of the month , the current month’s Rating Supplement will be used.
CHESS NOTATION The use of approved electronic notation devices is permitted.
Chess notation is not currently required in any unrated sections but it is required for the rated sections (until one player has under 5 minutes, then notation for both can stop)
TIE-BREAKS Computer programs are used to determine pairings, standings and tie-breaks for all sections.
All players tied for first place are considered co-winners, but trophies will be awarded based on tie-breaks.
Tie-breaks are used only to award trophies. Players or teams with like scores are equal and may change the plate on their trophy to reflect this (at their own cost).
When individual or team scores are equal, the following order of tie-break systems will be used to designate awards:
Modified Median
Solkoff
Cumulative Score
Opposition Cumulative Score
Head-to-Head
Coin Flip

Mar. '26 Palmetto Scholastic Chess League
Columbia Chess Club
Saturday, March 7, 2026
Event Overview
WWW.COLUMBIACHESS.ORG
A Premier Monthly Scholastic Tournament Series
The Columbia Chess Club organizes the Palmetto Scholastic Chess League (PSCL) as a regular monthly tournament series to encourage the organization of scholastic chess clubs and to promote scholastic chess throughout the state! Separate sections for High School, Middle School, and Elementary School provides balanced competition and encourages players to form teams representing their school to win awards. See past winners of the PSCL .
Conveniently Scheduled, Easy to Enter
PSCL events occur once a month on a Saturday. Games start at 10:00 a.m. and finish before lunch . The games are officially rated by US Chess , meaning that all players will be nationally ranked after playing ( for example, see scholastic player Charlie Jordan's US Chess profile ). If you are already a US Chess member, it's only $20 to enter.
First Timers Get a US Chess Membership!
For those playing their first US Chess tournament, registration is $25, which includes a US Chess membership that the Columbia Chess Club will create for you! (A youth membership itself costs $24 from US Chess as of January 1, 2025).
Register Online Now
First-Class Facilities
The Columbia Chess Club is located at 6169 St Andrews Road, Columbia, SC and is the vision of passionate chess players who wanted to create the perfect atmosphere to play chess. Wood pieces, specially-designed chess tables, a well-appointed spectator lounge with concessions, and state-of-the-art technology displaying real-time results and video of the top boards make the Columbia Chess Club the place to play chess.
Tournament Details:
Online Registration
Online registration only. Standard Registration is $20 for players with US Chess memberships. First-time tournament players $25, which includes a US Chess membership that the club will create for you using the email you provide at registration. Registration limited to first 74 players. If you need to renew your existing US Chess membership, please visit https://new.uschess.org/join-us-chess.
Register Online Now
Format
4-Round Swiss.
Time Control: G/10;+5.
Sections: High School, Middle School, and Elementary School.
4-Round Swiss means that players play all 4 rounds and are not eliminated. Each player will play with a 10 minute starting time and will get an additional 5 seconds with each move. (G/10;+5). This will affect the player's US Chess "Quick" rating. All equipment provided. Tournament has three sections: High School (9-12), Middle School (6-8), Elementary School (K-5). Players must register with the section corresponding to their grade. We reserve the right to combine sections during play, but prizes will be awarded separately for each section.
Rules Modification: For this tournament, USCF Rule 14K(2) is modified such that a Tournament Director may declare a game drawn after 50 moves without a capture or pawn move, rather than 75. We reserve the right to use a player's live rating for pairing purposes. For blitz tiebreaks, Blitz Rule 7(d) is modified such that a player's first illegal move results in a 1-minute penalty, standard Blitz Rule 7(d) applying on any subsequent illegal move by that player (i.e. a second illegal move is a loss if opponent has sufficient mating material).
Schedule
Round 1: 10:00 a.m.
Round 2: 10:35 a.m.
Round 3: 11:10 a.m.
Round 4: 11:45 a.m.
Awards: 12:15 p.m.

The top five players from each of the High School, Middle School, and Elementary School sections receive individual trophies. In the event of a tie for first, a blitz playoff is played between the players tied to determine first place. US Chess tiebreaks are used otherwise.

Southern Nevada Scholastic Chess Championships
State Championship Event
Del Sol Academy of the Performing Arts
Saturday, March 7, 2026
Event Overview
Silver State Chess Association LLC
Presents
SOUTHERN NEVADA STATE SCHOLASTIC
INDIVIDUAL AND TEAM CHAMPIONSHIPS
and QUALIFIER to NEVADA STATE SCHOLASTIC CHESS CHAMPIONSHIPS
Date: Saturday, March 7th, 2026 @ 8:45am
IMPORTANT: Both the Southern portion of the state (defined below) and the Northern portion of the state will hold separate Over-The-Board tournaments to determine individuals and teams from each region who will then compete in the Nevada State Scholastic Chess Championship to be held on dates to be determined.
Individuals who reside in, or go to school in, the following Nevada counties will be eligible to participate in the Southern Nevada State Scholastic Chess Championship: Clark, Nye, Lincoln and Esmerelda.
This announcement is for the Southern Nevada State Scholastic Chess Championship. The Northern Nevada State Scholastic Chess Championship will be held on a different day and will be detailed in a separate announcement.
Location:
Del Sol Academy of the Performing Arts
3100 E Patrick Ln
Las Vegas, NV 89120
To register please visit www.kingregistration.com/event/2026SNVSCh
A US Chess Rated Tournament in 6 Sections open to Southern Nevada residents or Southern Nevada students in the counties listed above.
K-3 Championship (Open to all players in grades K – 3)
K-5 Championship ( Open to all players in grades K – 5)
6 rounds
Time Control Game/25 minutes +5 seconds
Middle School Championship (Open to all players in grades 6 – 8)
High School Championship (Open to all players in grades 9 – 12)
5 rounds
Time Control Game/30 minutes +10 seconds
K-5 Challengers (Open to all players in grades K – 5 rated Under 400 or unrated)
K-12 Challengers ( Open to all players in grades K – 12 rated Under 800 or unrated)
6 rounds
Time Control Game/25 minutes +5 seconds
Individual and Team Trophies will be Awarded!
All players will receive a participation medal. Trophies will also be awarded.
Qualifiers
The top three individual scorers in each of the six Sections in the Southern Nevada Scholastic Chess Championship will meet on a date to be determined to compete in the Nevada State Scholastic Chess Championship (individuals), an online tournament that includes the Southern Nevada individual qualifiers and the Northern Nevada individual qualifiers. We will provide digital tablets for that tournament. The winners of the four sections: High School, Middle School, K-5 Championship, and K-3 Championship from that tournament will represent the State of Nevada at national tournaments to be held on August 3-6 in Grand Rapids, Michigan. Nevada State representatives will each receive a travel stipend from Silver State Chess after completing all games in the national tournament without a forfeit loss.
The top two scoring teams in each Section in the Southern Nevada Scholastic Chess Championship will meet on a date to be determined to compete in the Nevada State Scholastic Chess Championship (teams), an online tournament that includes the Southern Nevada team qualifiers and the Northern Nevada team qualifiers. We will provide digital tablets for that tournament. The winning teams will not qualify for any national tournament because there is no national team tournament for which to qualify.
Additional Prizes
The top scoring player in each section will receive free entry to the International Youth Championship in Las Vegas June 13-14. Restricted to players born after June 14, 2011 and rated under 1800.
The second-place finishers in all six sections will receive an entry to a future one-day tournament of their choice at Southern Nevada Chess Club in Las Vegas. The high school second place finisher may choose the Thursday night series instead of a one-day tournament. The free entry offer expires 12/31/26. Visit https://snvchess.com for more information about tournaments at the Southern Nevada Chess Club.
Entry Fees:
$50 before Feb. 8
$65 by Feb. 22
$75 before March 6
$100 before 6 AM on March 7
$125 on-site on March 7 may receive a half point bye in round 1
Refunds:
Refunds must be requested via email to [email protected] prior to 11:59pm on March 6 and will have a processing fee of $12 withheld.
Byes
Maximum two half-point byes are available upon request. All half-point byes must be requested before 8:30am on March 7. Half-point byes for Rounds 4 or later are irrevocable after 12:30pm on March 7. If any player is unable to play any round for any reason, including withdrawals, please notify a tournament director or score keeper.
Teams
Two or more players from the same school in the same section automatically form a team.
US Chess Membership required: you may join or renew at https://new.uschess.org/join-us-chess
Lunch:
We are seeking a sponsor to donate a pizza lunch for all participants and staff. A 60-90 minute lunch break will be provided following the completion of Round 2. If we do not get a sponsor for a pizza lunch, we will invite one or more food trucks to provide food service in the parking lot.
Schedule: Welcome and announcements will begin at approximately 8:45am. All players should be seated for Round 1 start at 9:00am. Subsequent rounds start about 15 minutes after the previous round ends. There will be a lunch break for players to eat lunch. Players registering on site may not be paired for round 1.
Players should bring a Chess clock capable of using Increments and they should be familiar with how to set the clock.

events.name: Time Trouble March RAPID
events.sourceText:
Time Trouble March RAPID
Columbia Chess Club
Saturday, March 7, 2026
Event Overview
Time Trouble March Rapid
Time Trouble is a recurring tournament on scheduled Saturday afternoons from 2 p.m. to 5:30 p.m. Time Trouble is formatted on an alternating schedule as either a Rapid G/10+5, 5-Round Swiss or a Blitz G/3+2, 6-Round Double Swiss, depending on the scheduled Saturday. $400 Prize Pool b/30.
REGISTRATION
Standard registration is $20. Paid club members are $15. "Paid Club Member" rates are for players with Columbia Chess Club Memberships only. See our website if you are interested in becoming a member of the Columbia Chess Club .
Entry for titled players (National Master and above) is free, standard entry fee deducted from prizes. If you are a titled player, simply use the "Titled Player" option at checkout.
Register Online Now
K-12 Player? Consider playing in our Palmetto Scholastic Chess League during the morning before Time Trouble. More Details >>
SCHEDULE
RAPID SATURDAY SCHEDULE (G/10;+5, 5-Round Swiss):
Round 1: 2:00 p.m.
Round 2: 2:45 p.m.
Round 3: 3:30 p.m.
Round 4: 4:15 p.m.
Round 5: 5:00 p.m.
Estimated Completion 5:30 p.m.
FORMAT
Rapid Tournament : 5-Round Swiss. Time control is G/10+5 (10 minutes starting time with a 5-second increment), which will be USCF Quick rated.
All equipment provided. USCF Rules Apply, active USCF Membership required. If you need to renew or obtain a USCF membership, please visit https://new.uschess.org/join-us-chess.
Rules Note: Per USCF Rule 28T, the pairing system will avoid pairing players registered under the same team during the first-half of the event.
PRIZES
$400 b/30*
1st: $100 ; 2nd: $80 ; 3rd: $60 ; 4th: $40
Top Under 1800: $40
Top Under 1300: $40
Top Under 800: $40
Players that are unrated in the applicable USCF rating category (Blitz or Quick) are not eligible for rating-based prizes.
*Based on 30 players, meaning that 50% of all prizes are guaranteed and scale with participation to the amount shown.
BYES
A single half-point bye is available any round (1-point bye in double Swiss format), including the final round. The bye may be requested as a part of the advance entry or on site before the tournament starts. Thereafter the only bye available is a zero-point bye. The chief tournament director shall have the ability to grant a half-point bye for any round on unusual circumstances.
LIVE STREAMING
Time Trouble tournaments will be live-streamed to the club's Twitch channel , and thereafter archived at the club's YouTube channel .

monthly on Sunday, but only the second instance of this set, starting from Sunday, May 19, 2024, forever
Event Overview
**Novi's AccelerateKid Scholastic Tournament Overview**
**Presented by Implodians Chess School LLC**
Join us for an exciting day of competitive chess at the Novi's AccelerateKid Scholastic Tournament, sponsored by The Implodians Chess School LLC. This event is designed to provide young chess enthusiasts with a platform to showcase their skills, challenge themselves, and enjoy the spirit of competition.
**Date and Time:**
May 19th, starting at 10:00 AM EASTERN( this week only ,then back to every 2nd sunday)
**Venue:**
24404 Catherine Industrial Dr #316, Novi, MI 48377
**Tournament Format:**
- 5 Round Swiss
- USCF REGULAR Rated
- 3 Sections: Open, Under 900, Under 600
- Time Control: G/30; d5 (5-second delay)
**Entry Fee:**
$30 per participant. Ensure your spot by registering before the deadline on April 13th at 9:00 PM.
**Tournament Schedule:**
- Rounds begin at 10am, followed by 11:15am, 1:00pm, 2:15pm, and 3:30pm.
- Pairings for each round will be created as soon as possible after the previous round ends.
- The tournament is anticipated to conclude before 5pm.
**Awards:**
- Trophies for 1st, 2nd, and 3rd places in the Open and Under 900 sections.
- In the Under 600 section, trophies will be awarded to the top 5 finishers (1st through 5th).
- A special "Best Notation Award" will be given to the participant with the most legible and accurate score sheet.

Pdk NINE Quads Tournament in Mt Laurel
Pdk NINE Board Game Café
Sunday, March 8, 2026
Event Overview
Register Now!
Date: Sunday, March 8th.
Time: Doors open at 8:30. | Please arrive by 8:45 AM for check-in. | First round starts promptly at 9:00 AM.
Location: PDK NINE Board Game Cafe
Entry Fee: $25 (Pre-registered only)
Registration closes at midnight on Saturday, March 7th. No walk-ins will be accepted. Please call the store for assistance in registering if necessary: 856-206-9615.
Prizes:
1st Place in Each Section: $50
2nd Place in Each Section: Free Game Block (Store Game Library Pass)
Tournament Format:
Quads: Players will be grouped into 4-person sections based on rating.
Rounds: 3 total rounds per player.
Time Control: Game in 25 minutes with a 5-second delay (G/25; d5).
Sections and games will be US Chess-rated.
Important Notes:
The first round starts promptly at 9:00 AM.
The store will be closed to the public during the event, but coffee and pastries will still be available for players and spectators to purchase.
Please arrive by 8:45 AM to check in and be ready for pairings.
Pre-registration is required – no walk-ins will be accepted on the day of the event.
New to Chess Tournaments? No Problem!
This event is perfect for both experienced players and newcomers looking to try out a fun, structured chess tournament in a relaxed setting.
This is a US Chess-rated event, meaning your games will count toward an official chess rating and a paid membership is required.
If you’re not a US Chess member yet, signing up is quick and easy! Just visit www.uschess.org before the event.
A US Chess membership allows you to participate in rated tournaments nationwide.
Affordable options are available for adults, juniors, and first-time players. If you're unsure about the process, just ask—we’re happy to help!
All players must provide a US Chess ID number at check-in.
What to Bring?
Bringing your own chess set and clock is strongly encouraged.
A few chess sets and clocks will be made available by the store participants do not own their own.
Enjoy coffee and pastries before and between rounds!
Come test your skills, meet other chess enthusiasts, and enjoy a great day of games! Whether you're a tournament veteran or playing in your first rated event, we’d love to have you at the board.

events.sourceText:
Super Sunday FIDE Tournament
Chess Kings & Queens Academy
Sunday, March 8, 2026
Event Overview
Note: This is a dual USCF - FIDE section of a larger USCF tournament (Super Sunday). Please read the information carefully. For the other sections and more events, please check our other listing.
Structure
- 3 rounds Swiss-Style. G75 +15. Accelerated pairings at the director's discretion.
- One half-point bye is available for any round, but must be requested before tournament start. All other requested byes are zero points.
- Clocks, boards, and weighed plastic pieces are provided. Players may use their own equipment with the agreement of their opponent.
- FIDE notice: Rules for late arrival will match standard USCF 60 minute rule.
Schedule
- Round times: 10:00 am / 1:30pm / 5:00 pm
USCF
- A current USCF membership is required to play.
- Players MUST have at least 1) 1700 USCF rating (live or current published), or 2) 1600 FIDE rating
FIDE
- A valid FIDE ID is required to play. Most players with a valid USCF membership may request a USA-flagged FIDE ID at this URL. Note that it may take several days to process. https://tinyurl.com/3zcjwmex
- There is no minimum FIDE rating for this event. There is a maximum rating of 2399.
- FIDE norms are not available at this event.
Registration
- Registration fee: $45
- Online registration only. Registration closes at 9:00 a.m. on the day of the event. On-site registrations are discouraged but may be accepted at the TD's discretion.
- Registration link: https://chesskq.com/tournament
- Free entry for all players rated 2200 or higher. ($45 will be deducted from the player's prize winnings.) E-mail name, USCF ID, and FIDE ID to Stephen Lorimor at [email protected] to sign up.
- This event has no age restrictions.
- Players signing up for a section they are not eligible to join will be automatically shifted to the appropriate section.
- Players ineligible to participate in any section of this event, or withdrawing before 9:00 AM on the day of the tournament, will receive a credit for a future class or tournament.
Prizes
Prizes are paid out via Zelle or PayPal. Check-by-mail available for anyone without these options.
- 1st place: $200
- 2nd place: $100
- Top U1800 (FIDE): $60

@50 players - we add a Top Junior (under age 12) award to each section
@55 players - we add a Top Senior (age 55+) award to each section
@60 players - we increase 2nd place and "top under __ rating" prizes for all sections by $15
@65 players - we increase 1st place prizes for all sections by $20.
Additional information
- The tournament director for this event is Stephen Lorimor. Bye requests and other issues may be e-mailed to [email protected] , or by voice/text to 908-286-0720. Note that he may not notice or respond to e-mails, texts, or calls after 9:00 am the day of the event.
- The venue is located within walking distance of multiple restaurants and fast food businesses. No food is allowed at the playing tables, but a waiting room with tables is available.

Texas Grand Circuit ed.1 in Dallas
Champions Social Club Dallas
Thursday, March 12, 2026
- Monday, March 16, 2026
Event Overview
Texas Grand Circuit — Dallas (Edition 1) | March 12–16
If you’re chasing norms, crave world-class playing conditions, and want an event that treats players like VIPs without compromising integrity —this is the one.
Why this event is different
Norm conditions by design : a curated, norm-eligible field built for real title chances—not a “maybe the pairings work out” situation.
Player-first experience : punctual rounds, clear communication, professional staffing, and logistics that run like a machine.
Elite venue & comfort : a premium tournament hall that belongs in the conversation with the best venues in the U.S.
Treated like kings : hospitality touches that make you feel like a featured guest, not an entry fee.
Strict anti-cheating & game integrity : serious measures, consistent enforcement, and an environment where results matter.
Event Schedule & Sections
International Section (Norm Eligible)
March 12–16
9-round Swiss | Norm eligible
$10,000 prize fund (based on 48 players)
A focused, premium section built for norm attempts and high-quality pairings round after round.
Open Section (FIDE/USCF Rated)
March 13–16
7-round Swiss | FIDE/USCF rated
3-day / 4-day schedules available
$3,000 prize fund (based on 64 players)
A strong open with top-tier organization and conditions you can feel from round one.
Important details
Entry fee details : linked on the registration page
Total event cap : 112 players (both sections combined)
This venue is hands-down one of the best tournament halls in the United States—an experience you need to see in person. If you’ve ever wanted “St. Louis-level” conditions with a player-first feel, Dallas in March is your move.

events.sourceText:
2026 Indiana Chess Congress
Heritage Event, Grand Prix, State Championship Event
La Quinta Inn & Suites Indianapolis South
Friday, March 13, 2026
- Sunday, March 15, 2026
Event Overview
2026 Indiana Chess Congress
and 85th Indiana State Chess Championship
MARCH 13-15, 2026
$15,000 PRIZE FUND (B/O 150 PAID ENTRIES)
FIVE SECTIONS, 5-SS with 2- and 3-day options
La Quinta Inn & Suites Indianapolis South
Friday, March 13, 2026 - Sunday, March 15, 2026
FULL INFORMATION, REGISTRATION, & HOTEL RESERVATIONS
REGISTRATION:
Follow link above to register online.
Onsite registration for main sections before Friday @ 6:30 PM (3-day) & Saturday @ 9:30 AM (2-day) to ensure a first round pairing.
ENTRY FEES:
On or before February 1: $100 Early Special. Open to ISCA members only. Anyone, including out-of-state players, may join ISCA before registering.
February 2 to March 11: $155. ($15 discount off this entry fee for ISCA members. ISCA membership costs $15, so it is always worth joining.)
On or after March 12: $170 for all registrants
Re-Entry Fee: $50 before Saturday @ 9:30 AM
Cancellation of registration before event subject to $5 fee withheld from refund.
$3 convenience fee if paying by credit card, not charged to ISCA members.
Save on all ISCA tournaments by becoming a member at https://www.indianachess.org
Titled players: Feel free to contact the ISCA president ( [email protected] ) regarding possible conditions available. They are limited, so act soon.
SCHEDULES and TIME CONTROLS:
All championship sections are 5-round Swisses:
3-day schedule: Fri: 7:00 PM | Sat: 11:00 AM & 5:00 PM | Sun: 10:00 AM & 3:30 PM (all G/90 inc/30)
2-day schedule: Sat: 10:00 AM & 1:30 PM (G/60 inc/30), then merge with 3-day at 5:00 PM (G/90 inc/30)
Half-point byes allowed in rounds 1-4, limit 2, must be committed before round 2.
ISCA annual membership meeting Sunday @ 2:10 PM, after round 4 concludes
SECTIONS and PRIZES:
85th Annual Indiana State Chess Championship (1900+)*
Top Prizes
$1200 | $900 | $500 | $300
U2300 Prizes
$600 | $300
Top Indiana Resident Bonus:
$250 + Trophy | $175 | $125
Top Indiana Resident Seniors (must verify age before round 4)
$125 for age 60+ | $125 for age 50-59
Top Indiana K-12 Player (must verify grade before round 4)
$100
*Any IN resident may enter into this section; out-of-state players must be rated 1900 or above.
Indiana State Major Open Championship (U2100)
Players rated below 1800 in this section must either have had a peak non-provisional rating of 1800+ or have earned a USCF 1st Category norm and must give proof of eligibility in the comments at registration.
Top Prizes
$800 | $500 | $300 | $200
U1900 Prizes
$400 | $200
Indiana State Reserve Championship (U1801)
Players rated below 1500 in this section must either have had a peak non-provisional rating of 1500+ or have earned a USCF 2nd Category norm and must give proof of eligibility in the comments at registration.
Top Prizes*
$800 | $500 | $300 | $200
U1600 Prizes (no unrated)
$400 | $200
Top Indiana Resident Bonus:
$200 + Trophy | $100
*Unrated players limited to $300

Top Prizes*
$800 | $500 | $300 | $200
U1300 Prizes (no unrated)
$300 | $200 | $150
*Unrated players limited to $300

$700 | $400 | $300 | $200

$300 | $200 | $150
Unrated Player Prizes (if at least 3 unrated players registered)
$200 | $100

5120 Victory Drive
Indianapolis, IN 46203
+1 (317) 783-7751
Event room rates available
$114/night
Follow link above for hotel reservations.
Many guest rooms newly renovated since last Congress!
GENERAL INFORMATION:
All prizes paid electronically via PayPal or Venmo.
Bring board, set, and clock. Equipment is generally not provided.
Published March ratings will be used.
In the State Championship section, all players must turn in their original signed scoresheet in addition to reporting results.
In the State Championship section, players may be assigned to play on a broadcasted DGT board. They must play on that board if assigned to it. Games are broadcast on a time delay to deter cheating.
More Information available at https://www.indianachess.org .

Sunday, March 15, 2026 at 2:10 PM., after round 4
Annual meeting is for ISCA Members Only (join at indianachess.org)
If you cannot play a full Congress Championship schedule, there will be other chess events held concurrently at the site. events.name: 2026 ICEA Chess @ West LA
events.sourceText:
2026 ICEA Chess @ West LA
Nolte Community Center
monthly on Saturday, but only the second instance of this set, starting from Saturday, January 10, 2026, forever
Event Overview
ICEA Chess @ West LA hosts a Monthly OTB Chess Tournament on the second Saturday of each month. It typically features four sections (U1000, 1000+, 1600+ and 2000+) to accommodate different skill levels based on the monthly supplement USCF ratings.
The tournament is a one-day event with four rounds for the 1000+ / 1600+ / 2000+ sections, running from 9 AM to 6 PM, with a time control of G/45;+5 (45 minutes for each player, plus a 5-second increment per move).
The U1000 section is designed for players with ratings below 1000, making it an excellent starting point for new players who haven't established a USCF rating yet. This section has three double rounds from 9 AM to 4 PM, meaning players will play two games against the same opponent each round.
Schedule:
The Second Saturday Of Each Month
Format/Time Control:
Regular Month
1800+ Section: 4 Round SS, G/45;+5
1000+ Section: 4 Round SS, G/45;+5
U1000 Section: 3 Double Rounds SS, G/30;+5
Super Month (April, October)
2000+ Section: 4 Round SS, G/90;+20 (Cross Two Saturdays)
1600+ Section: 4 Round SS, G/45;+5
1000+ Section: 4 Round SS, G/45;+5
U1000 Section: 3 Double Rounds SS, G/30;+5

***This announcement is for the Southern Nevada State Girls Scholastic Chess Championship. The Northern Nevada State Girls Scholastic Chess Championship will be held on a different day and will be detailed in a separate announcement.

The winner of that tournament will represent the State of Nevada at the 14th Annual WIM Ruth Haring National Tournament of Girls State Champions in Grand Rapids, MI from August 3-6th. 3/14 - Quad chess tournament G40; d5
Saint Petersburg Chess Club
Saturday, March 14, 2026
Event Overview
There will be no “Byes” or withdrawals allowed. Please complete all your Quad games.
WHAT IS THE QUAD CHESS TOURNAMENT? After all the players have entered, they’re ordered from highest rating to lowest. Unrated players are placed at the low end. The top four players are placed into their own section (a “quad”), then the next four highest in another section, and so on down the list.If two family members are in the same quad, I can move one of them quad up or down.The players in each quad play a round robin, one game against each of the players in their section, for a total of three games each. If there is not an even multiple of four players, the lowest section (usually) will have the few extra players and play a three round Swiss tournament rather than a round robin. The quad format is popular in one day events, and results in players of the most similar playing strengths being paired together for all three rounds. Each group of four chess players is called a Quad.If two family members are at the same Quad,I can move one of them to another Quad.
ADVANTAGES OF QUAD TOURNAMENTS: The advantage of Quad Tournaments, and why players enjoy them so much, is that players of the same strength and experience are able to compete against each other. In addition, the less experienced players are able to win the same "First Place" prizes as their more experienced, stronger counterparts in Quad I and II. You have opportunity your rating to go up faster!!!
LOCATION: Saint Petersburg Chess Club 540 4th Avenue North Saint Petersburg, FL 33701 (it is located in between Mirror Lake and the Coliseum, next to the Sunshine Center.)

$30 afterward.

USCF membership is required. Please check your USCF ID and renew it if it has expired. If you need me to do it on site add $5 to your bill.
ROUNDS: Three Rounds, First starts at approx. 11:00 a.m.

Trophies for 1st to 3rd place for last section!

CKQ Saturday Piscataway Rapids
Chess Kings & Queens Academy
Saturday, March 14, 2026
Event Overview
CKQ Saturday Piscataway Rapids
Start time: Players should arrive no later than 4:15 p.m. The first game begins promptly at 4:30. Latecomers risk their clock running when they arrive.
End time: The Under 600 section typically ends by 8:30 p.m., the Under 1200 section more like 9:00. The tournament could go a bit longer if players use all their time.
Players: Most players at this event will be children (ages 6-16), but adults are welcome to play. Beginners are welcome, but at a minimum players should know how to legally move chess pieces, recognize when they’re in check, and how to perform basic checkmates (ex; king and queen vs. king).
Structure / time controls: 4-SS, G30 +5. (Each player will play four games. Each player receives 30 minutes per game, plus another five seconds per move.)
Sections: Under 600 and Under 1200 rating sections. The Under 1200 section requires at least 500 rating to enter. Lower-rated and unrated players may enter with the tournament director's permission.
Requirements: A USCF membership is required to play in the tournament. Contact the tournament director if you need assistance creating or renewing a membership.
Equipment: Players do not need to bring any equipment. Players are recommended to eat before arriving, or at least bring a snack.
Registration: The registration fee is $25. Online registration closes at 5pm on the day of the event.
Byes: If you can’t attend the entire tournament, a half-point bye (limit one) is available for any round. Byes must be requested before the tournaments starts. If you are going to take first-round bye please contact the tournament director at least one hour before the tournament starts.
Prizes: Top three winners in each section receive a trophy or a medal.
For more information: Contact tournament director Stephen Lorimor ( [email protected] , phone/text: 908-286-0720).
