Daniel Naroditsky Memorial
open to all chessplayers, ages 5 to 105, novice to master!
$12 entry fee, waived for K-12 students and SVCC chess club members
Hosted and co-sponsored by Salinas Valley Community Church. Organized and co-sponsored by Chess Monterey.
Your donations toward Chess Monterey community outreach are gratefully appreciated.
Saturday, March 14
Salinas Valley Community Church, 368 San Juan Grade Road, Salinas CA 93906
4 sections: USCF-rated Championship , Challengers , Contenders ,
and non-rated Candidates
Entrants to rated sections must be current members of USCF -- join or renew at uschess.org
Championship section is limited to the eight top-rated entrants (incl. qualifier from February 7 Challengers).
Challengers section is limited to the next group of eight entrants based on USCF ratings.
Contenders section is for the remaining entrants, including unrated players wanting to earn a USCF rating.
Candidates section is a non-rated introductory section for novice and youth players.

3 rounds: 10:30, 1:00, 3:30

events.name: El Dorado Afternoon Crazy Quads
events.sourceText:
El Dorado Afternoon Crazy Quads
El Dorado Train Depot, East Room
Saturday, March 14, 2026
Event Overview
Prologue:
I personally dislike waking up hours before I normally would to make the long drive to a chess tournament that starts early in the morning, playing for 6-8 hours, and drive back. And I sure as heck am not paying for pet boarding and a hotel on top of the entry fee. What an exhausting mess. If you can relate to that, then boy do I have the event for you!
Tournament:
Format: Quads. Up to four groups of four players in a round-robin. 3 rounds total.
Time Control: g/45; d5.
Registration: Register online before 11:59PM on 03/12. Venue opens at 11AM. Register at KingRegistration.com
Round timings: Round 1 pairings at 11:50AM Rounds: 12:01 - 1:45 - 3:30.
Registered players must arrive early or give director notice of late arrival. Failure to arrive on time or give notice of tardiness will result in automatic withdrawal.
No byes may be requested. Please come prepared to play all three rounds. If you aren't sure you can make it, please withdraw early to give someone else the chance for a seat.
Registration And Fees:
There are only 16 seats available due to space constraints. Registrations are first-come, first-serve. You are required to check in before first round pairings or you will lose your seat. There are only three rounds, so I'm not going to make someone sit at an empty board on the off-chance you do show up late.
All games will be rated by the United States Chess Federation. (Regular and Quick)
All players must be members of the United States Chess Federation.
KCA membership not required.
Entry Fee : $0. Donations welcome but not required.
Sections:
There will be 1 section available to register in, but players will be sorted into sections of four players the day of the event. Section 1 will have the top four rated players, then the second will have the next highest group of four, and so on.
If the registered players cannot form a multiple of four and the last section has 3 players available, the director will enter himself into the appropriate quad for his rating to ensure everyone gets a full quad.
If the registered players plus director cannot form a multiple of four, the bottom two quads will be merged and ran as a 3-round swiss. In that case, the director reserves rights to use accelerated pairings if deemed necessary for better pairings. Director may enter himself if necessary for better pairings.
Equipment:
Boards, pieces, and clocks will all be provided by the director. Do not bring your own.
Nearby Amenities:
Coffee: Great coffee shop (Dilly Deli) within a short walk
Food: Mexican restaurant within a short walk, Casey's, Taco Bell, Wendy's, and Arby's within a short drive. We have a refrigerator to keep food and drinks in, and a microwave to cook it.
Parking: Free, on-site.
Contact:
Feel free to reach out with any questions you might have.

4 round Swiss. Time control: Game in 40 minutes with 5 sec delay. Boards, sets, clocks and scoresheets will be provided.

Coppell Chess Club

TCA 2026 Region III Scholastic Girls Championship
USCF-Rated • 4-Round Swiss Tournament. Eligible players must be K–12 students who reside in or attend school within the Region III counties (Dallas, Collin, Ellis, etc.) to be eligible for regional titles. Any Texas resident may participate; however, championship title will be awarded to the player in that region only. Players must follow grade-level eligibility rules. Playing up a section is allowed; playing down is not permitted.
Where:
Coppell Chess Club
120 E Bethel School Rd,
Coppell, TX 75063
When:
Saturday, March 14, 2026
Round 1 starts approximately at 9:00 AM. Remaining rounds will start as soon as possible after the previous round.

G30; d5 (30 minutes with 5-second delay)
4-Round Swiss System (based on entries)
Sections:
MS/HS Championship (Grades 6–12)

$35 Early Bird (on or before February 21, 2026)
$45 Regular Entry

Awards:
Texas Region III Girls Championship Title for each section.
Trophies will be awarded to the Top 3 individuals in each section.
Tiebreaks will be used to determine final standings for trophy positions. If there is a tie for first place, a blitz playoff game (3 minutes with a 2-second delay) will be conducted among the tied players. If the blitz game also results in a tie, an Armageddon playoff will be used to determine the champion.
Byes:
Up to one ½-point bye is allowed for any round except the last round. The bye must be requested before the end of Round 2.
A zero-point bye/withdrawal must be requested before the section pairing is done.
Withdrawals/Refund:

More Details:
February/March US Chess ratings and rules will be used for pairings and awarding prizes.
Chess boards and pieces will be provided. Bring your own chess clock.
Unrated players will be placed at the Tournament Director’s discretion.
No spectators are allowed in the tournament area.
Players may not eat at the board. Only water or soft drinks are allowed.
All non-essential electronic devices must be completely powered off and remain in the player’s bag or face up on the table during play. Violations may result in penalties up to loss of game or removal from the tournament.

U1300, U800 and U600 sections : 4SS, G/30;d/5. Four rounds of US Chess rated chess in Swiss System format. Each player has 30 minutes to make their moves in a game with 5 second delay per move. Players should already be familiar with how to move and capture pieces, castle, how to check/checkmate an opponent, and play to the end of each game without being distracted. If unsure whether a player is ready, please email tournament director .
Beginner players in grades K-5 who do not yet have rated tournament experience are suggested to register for the U400 section, although parents are free to register players in the U800 section. Beginner players in grades 6-adult should register in the U600 section, although stronger players are encouraged to register for the U1300 section. All sections are rated, and a valid US Chess membership is required for all players.
When siblings are playing in the same section, a pairing exception will be added if possible.
If a section is full, seating will not be increased. If a player registration is cancelled before the tournament date, that seat will be available.

Prizes (All sections except U1300)
Gold medals for player(s) in top half of pool for each section, (for example, 1 point for each game won, 0.5 points for each game drawn), with no computer calculated tie-breaks. Silver medals for all other players.
Trophies are awarded to top player/players in each section. (See note at bottom for tie break rules if there are 2+ players with a tie).
Prizes (U1300 section)
$90 cash prize for section winner/winners, with $45 for the second place winner/winners.
Refunds/Cancellation/Inclement Weather Policy :
If unable to participate, registered players may withdraw by contacting the tournament director. If cancelling by Tuesday midnight before tournament, fee will be refunded but are subject to a $10 administrative fee. If cancelling after Tuesday, refund is subject to a $15 administrative fee.
If a player is feeling unwell (coughing, has fever, sore throat, etc) day of event, they should not compete in consideration of the health of other players.
If there is heavy snow day of event and road conditions are unsafe locally in Ridgefield, tournament will be rescheduled and players will be given the option to have their entry fee refunded with a $2 fee to cover platform and credit card costs.
Additional Details :
* This event takes place on Sunday afternoon, not Saturday afternoon.
* To register, go to link https://www.events4chess.com/events/?event_ID=2543&cat=1
* An active US Chess membership is required prior to registering for this tournament for all sections. - available at https://new.uschess.org/join-us-chess . The fee for one child under 19 is $24/year, and the membership fee for adults (under 65) is $54/year. Other membership options are available.
* Chess sets, clocks, pencils, erasers, and score sheets are provided, and players do not need to bring their own equipment. Players are welcome to use their own score sheets/score books.
* Supervision: Tournament director and tournament assistant(s) will be coordinating this event. Dropoff is possible, and parents can be contacted via cellphone as needed. Parents with players who require supervision should plan to attend the event for duration. For players without cellphone, parents may request at sign-in a text message to be sent to contact phone number at the start of round 4.
* Pizza will be delivered to venue at 3 PM, with water bottles and chips also available for purchase. Payment on-site via Venmo or Paypal.
* Safety: Masks are optional, and no food is allowed in the playing area. A water bottle for players is suggested.
* Parking: There are plenty of parking spaces in the venue parking lot.
* Social media: Photos/videos will be taken at the event and may be posted to the club website or social media accounts for outreach and marketing purposes. Inform the tournament director before the day of the event to opt-out if desired.
* See tournament handout for event rules and tournament etiquette. Taking notation is required for players in all sections except U400, although players may request an exemption with 5 minute penalty. Notation is not required for players in the U400 sections.
* For families visiting Ridgefield, Ridgefield's local library is open until 5 PM, and there are coffee shops ( Queen B , Tazza Cafe , an ice cream and candy shop (Deborah Ann's), and the local bookstore ( Books on the Common ) in downtown Ridgefield. Limited seating provided for parents and family members. Parents are welcome and encouraged to stay for the beginning and end of the tournament for the orientation and award ceremony.
* Tournament results and link to event photos will be posted to https://tournaments.wayoftheboard.org .
* Latest published ratings are used for tournament registration as opposed to official ratings. A player's official published rating will not be given to a player until 25+ games have been played and is updated 12 times a year. Tournament director may move a player to different section on day of event if rating has changed from time of registration (for example, if rating was initially 399 but on day of event is 401 player may be moved to the U800 section).
* An Events4Chess account is not necessary to register a player for a tournament, only the player's US Chess account ID. It is only needed to auto-populate fields when registering, or to be notified when a new event is live.
* Payment: Paypal/credit card/debit card accepted for payment. To use a payment method other than Paypal after checkout, select "Pay with Debit or Credit Card".
* Tie Break format for U400/U800 sections - If there are 2+ top players tied in a section, a playoff will determine the section winner and trophy recipient, and will immediately follow the last round. The playoff format will be G/5/4 d2 Armageddon game, blitz rules apply, with pawn hand determining player color (tournament director will have black and white pawns in hand, players choose hand to determine color). All other ties broken by US Chess standard tie break rules.
* To confirm if a player was successfully registered after submitting the registration fee, check the Participants list. If the player is listed, registration was successful.
* An orientation email will be sent out at 8 AM day of event with additional details for first-time parents and players, but parents/players can email tournament director with any questions.
* Printable flyer: https://www.events4chess.com/dashboard/events/rds_generate_flyer.php?event_ID=2543

TCA Region V Scholastic 2026
(Middle School)

Date: March 15, 2026

Pricing
Early Registration: $32, ends on March 1, 2026
Regular Registration: $37, between March 2-8, 2026

Active USCF membership is required by March 1, 2026. Visit new.uschess.org/join-us-chess starting at $24 to join USCF or renew your membership!
Visit chess.jliptrap.us/hgroup.htm for $13 discount Scholastic memberships and renewals!
TCA Tournament membership is included in the tournament entry fee. Visit texaschess.org/memberships to join TCA or renew your membership!
Pricing is included in the registration form automatically.
Eligibility
Participants must live or attend school in one of these counties:
Austin, Brazoria, Brazos, Chambers, Fort Bend, Galveston, Grimes
Hardin, Harris, Houston, Jasper, Leon, Liberty, Madison
Matagorda, Montgomery, Newton, Orange, Polk, Robertson
San Jacinto, Trinity, Tyler, Walker, Waller, Wharton
The max number of registrations for this tournament is 74. Text Edgar Acosta to join a waiting list
Sections
Middle School Open: Any Middle Schooler (Junior High Student) may enter this section.
Middle School U800: Only Middle Schoolers rated 800 or below may enter this section.
Note: Sections may be combined in case of low registrations.
Definitions:
High School - Grades 9-12; in some districts 10-12, if Junior High is 7-9.
Middle School - Grades 6 to 8 or 9 depending on how the school district divides them.
Elementary - K-6 if 6th grade is in the Elementary building, K-5 if 6 is in Middle School. A 5th-6th campus has been ruled Elementary, a 6th-only campus as Middle School.
Primary - K-3. Note that a first grader could enter K-1 or K-3 or K-5.
K-8 and K-12 schools and Home School Associations are divided K-5, 6-8, and 9-12.
Students not assigned a grade in school will be assigned a grade at the tournament based on their age as of September 1 of that school year as follows: six years old is assigned first grade, seven years old is assigned second grade, and so on through grade twelve.
Note: Sections are based on USCF January 2026 ratings. "Current" ratings may be used to pair unrated players but will not determine section placement. Accelerate Pairings will be used at the discretion of the TD the day of the tournament.
Tournament Format
Rounds: Swiss 5 Rounds, Game in 25 with a 5-second delay (G/25 d/5).
Membership: USCF and TCA memberships required.
Rules: USCF rules apply.
Open sections require notation and clocks (if available). Players who opt to not take notation will have their time start at 20 minutes instead of 25.
Reserved sections are strongly encouraged to use notation and clocks.
Touch-move / Touch-take: Applies to all sections. Younger players, especially in Kinder-1st Open, will be encouraged to keep these rules with gentle reminders as needed.
Equipment: Plan on bringing your own chess set and clock if you have one, money for lunch, and a good attitude! Every player needs to bring their clocks!
Please make sure your clocks are labeled with the player's name and USCF ID.
Chess sets for the whole tournament will be provided!
Schedule
No At-Site Registration. All registrations must be submitted online at/or before 11:59pm on March 13, 2026.
Please arrive between 8:15 and 8:45 to check in and get ready to play.
Round 1: Starts at 9:00 AM SHARP; subsequent rounds will start ASAP. No elimination.
Players may request a single 1/2 point Bye missed, 0 point Bye for any subsequent Byes. Any Byes need to be requested by Friday February 13th, 2026 at 7pm.
Lunch break after Round 3, estimating 12pm-1pm.
Teams
Teams consist of two or more (2+) players in the same section from the same school/association.
Team members must attend the same school campus full-time or belong to the same Home School Association .
Sections are not combined for teams.
Team scores will be calculated by summing the top four (4) individual scores from each team.
Awards
Trophies: Top 5 individuals in each section and Top 4 teams in each section.
1st Place Finishers qualify for a spot in the State Regional Invitational April 18-19th .
Alternate awards (likely medals) to players who score 3 or more points but do not win a trophy.
Tie Breaks: Solkoff (sum of opponents' scores), Modified Median (dropping the lowest opponent's score), Cumulative of Opposition, then Cumulative (USCF Standard)

Event Overview
LOCATION: Panera Bread, 2001 Indian River Blvd, Vero Beach, FL 32960
Date : Tuesday, March 17, 2026
ROUNDS: Three Rounds: First round starts at approximately 6:30 PM .
TIME CONTROL : G15; d5
Limited to the first 32 players based on space and upper Quads will be FIDE rated.
PRIZES : $50 for first place at each Quad (if two players tied for 1st place $25 each) A donation of $5 will be made per Quad to Military Chess ( https://new.uschess.org/form/donate ).
ENTRY FEE : $20.00 if you pay by Tuesday March 16 by 11:59 pm. $25 after that and at the door. USCF membership is required. A donation of $5 will be made per Quad/Mini Swiss to Military Chess.
Register online: Click here .
Please check your USCF ID and renew it if it has expired.
IMPORTANT NOTICE : Due to space limitation to secure your spot and pay ahead of time! BRING YOUR CHESS CLOCK and Chess Board and Pieces!!!
WHAT IS THE QUAD CHESS TOURNAMENT? After all the players have entered, they’re ordered from highest rating to lowest. Unrated players are placed at the low end. The top four players are placed into their own section (a “quad”), then the next four highest in another section, and so on down the list. The players in each quad play a round robin, one game against each of the players in their section, for a total of three games each. If there is not an even multiple of four players, the lowest section (usually) will have the few extra players and play a three round Swiss tournament rather than a round robin. The quad format is popular in one day events, and results in players of the most similar playing strengths being paired together for all three rounds. A Quad Tournament consists of the top four ranked players (#s 1-4) on the Chess Ladder playing each other, then the second top four ranked players (#s 5-8) playing each other, then the third top four ranked players (#s 9-12) playing each other, and so forth. Each group of four chess players is called a Quad.
ADVANTAGES OF QUAD TOURNAMENTS : The advantage of Quad Tournaments, and why players enjoy them so much, is that players of the same strength and experience can compete against each other. In addition, the less experienced players can win the same "First Place" prizes as their more experienced, stronger counterparts in Quad I and II. You have the opportunity for your rating to go up faster!!!

SECTION B: 1400 - 1799 Open USCF rated

2026 SuperStates Blitz Championship
State Championship Event
LAX Marriott
Friday, March 20, 2026
Event Overview
Registration Online: SuperStates.org
Venue
Los Angeles Airport Marriott, 5855 West Century Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90045, US
(Click the link above to book a hotel room: $155/night)
🗓 Date & Time
Friday, March 20
6:30–8:30 PM
📍 Location
Los Angeles Airport Marriott
💵 Entry Fee: $40 by Mar 1 (11:59 PM)
Late: $50 by Mar 20 (6 PM)
⛔ Deadline: No entries after 6 PM, Mar 20
One OPEN Section: All students, adults, families, and coaches are welcome. (If entries exceed 60, the section will be split into two.)
🏆 Trophies to the Top 25% of players (max 10 trophies if exceeding 40 players for one section)
This is a US Chess Blitz-rated event. Current US Chess membership is required.
Format
2×4SS or 2×5SS (4 or 5 double-rounds with higher-rated partner playing White & Black against opposing higher-rated partner)
Time Control: G/3 +2
Touch-move (same as the main event)
Blitz Rules
The current edition of the Official Rules of Chess and the current online edition of “Rulebook Changes” shall be used to resolve any situation not covered by these Scholastic Blitz Rules.
Bring a clock. Each player is responsible for coming to the game with a clock. If neither player has a clock, then both players will receive a forfeit loss for both games. (Organizers will have a few clocks on hand, but not guaranteed.)
Know how to use your clock. All players are required to know how to operate their clock and how to make any changes that may be necessary during a game.
Only a TD can replace a defective clock. Only a TD may determine if a clock is defective and change the clock once the game begins.
Same hand rule. Each player must press the clock button with the same hand used to move the pieces. This also applies to castling and capturing.
Clock direction & seating. The TD may state the direction clocks face. The player with Black chooses which side of the table to sit on.
Pressing the clock.
a) Except for pressing the clock button or straightening the clock, neither player should touch the clock.
b) If a player knocks over the clock, the opponent gets one minute added to the opponent’s clock.
c) If a player’s clock does not start, the opponent may try to start it by pressing the player’s clock button; if unsuccessful, signal for a TD.
d) After moving, each player must always be allowed to press the player’s clock.
e) Neither player should keep a hand on (or hovering over) the clock.
Knocking over a piece.
a) It is unsportsmanlike conduct to knock over a piece and then press the clock.
b) First offense: warning. Second: one minute added to opponent. Third: loss of the game.
c) A player will not lose a game on time if the opponent knocks over a piece and presses the clock without picking it up; the player receives an additional minute to continue.
Disputes. Either player may stop the clock to summon a TD. The TD will consider testimony and reliable witnesses. Appeals must be made to the Chief TD.
Conduct. Excessive banging of pieces or clock will not be tolerated. The offending player may be penalized with loss of time.

events.sourceText:
5th Annual Old Line Open
Rockville Hilton
Friday, March 20, 2026
- Sunday, March 22, 2026
Event Overview
5th Annual Old Line Open
Rockville, Maryland
Individual Registration
Group Registration
Championship, U2100, U1900, U1700, U1500: 5SS, Game/90 inc/30 -- (2-day schedule: Rnds 1-2 Game/45 inc/30)
U1250 and U1000 : 5SS, Game/75 d/5 with Rnds 1-2 at Game/45 d/5;
U1250 3-day schedule : all rounds Game/75 d/5
Playing Site
Rockville Hilton, Rockville, MD
We aim to create a pleasant environment for playing chess. Below are the answers we received at a previous tournament to the question of what do we do better than other tournaments.
Advance Entries
Tournament Features
We pair rounds as early as possible and start rounds on time → You have time to get ready and don't have to waste your time waiting for the round to start
30" increment time control in the top five sections → No more clock smashing scrambles at the end of the game.
Score-based prizes → See the advantages below.
Additional 1st place prizes to clear first when there is no 5-0 player in the section, added to your score prize → More prize money
Minimum ratings to play in the top 5 sections → Less mismatch games.
Sets, boards and clocks provided for everyone → No more carrying around pieces and a board, just bring a clock.
Free Sunday morning Continental breakfast → Relax, have some coffee and a danish before you start your game.
Texting or emailing of pairings to your cell phone available → No rush at the pairing chart before the round
$149 hotel rate, Reserve a room → Relax and stay at the tournament hotel. $5 EF discount if staying at hotel.
Hotel next to DC Metro stop → Take the Metro directly to the tournament.
Shorter time controls in lower sections → Less waiting around between rounds.
Prizes
This tournament will pay prizes based solely on your final score. All the prizes are guaranteed. If the total pay out in the Open section is less than $1500, extra money will be added to the pay out of the top score group to bring the total to $1500.
Advantages over place-based scoring
Less Waiting
Your score determines your prize. Once you finish your last game, you can receive a check.
Less Uncertainty
Your prize does not get lowered if others tie with you. For example, if there are two 5-0 players, both receive the full amount for 5-0.
Less short draws
The total payout is always higher when games are decisive.

Individual Registration
Group Registration

Maryland Chess Assn.
1827 Thornton Ridge Road
Towson, MD 21204
Mailed registrations should include name, section, schedule(2-day or 3-day). The chief TD for the tournament will be Mike Regan. If you have any questions about the tournament email him at [email protected] .
Advance Registrations
Schedules
3-day schedule Champ - U1500: Reg ends Fri 6 pm, rds. Fri 7 pm, Saturday 11am and 5:30, Sunday 9:30 am and 2:45.
2-day schedule Champ - U1500: Reg ends Sat 10 am, rds. Saturday 11am, 2:15 and 5:30, Sunday 9:30 am and 2:45.
U1000 and U1250 2-day schedule: Reg ends Sat 10 am, rds. Saturday 11, 12:45 and 3:00, Sunday 9:30 am and 12:15 pm.
U1250 3-day schedule: Reg ends Fri 6 pm, rds Friday 7 pm, Saturday 11 and 3:00, Sunday 9:30 am and 12:15 pm.
Byes
Half point byes: all must commit before rd 3
Reentries:
all, $80 except U1000 and U1250 $40. You can reenter any schedule taking 1/2 point byes for unplayed games. If you reenter with a single 1/2 point bye, the cost is $70/$35. If you reenter with two 1/2 point byes, the cost is $60/$30.
Hotel Rates: $149 per night $5 EF discount if staying at hotel. Reserve a room
Parking : $6 for day guest and $10 overnight. Parking is free in Metro parking lot over the weekend.
Rooms are limited. So make your reservations early.
Rule Variations
In sections that the organizer provides clocks, if both players are not present at the start of the round, the tournament director will start white's clock.
Clocks that halt on end are preferred in all sections with increment time controls.
Any player forfeiting a round must pay a $50 fine before being allowed to play in a future tournament organized by MCA or Baltimore Chess.
The electronic score keeping devices, ChessNoteR and eNotate, cannot be used at this tournament.
All players with provisional ratings will have 100 points added to their rating for determining section eligibility
Players with byes who are eligible to play in a lower section that also has a bye player may get paired in that section as a house player. They will still have the bye for standings in their original section. The game in the lower section does count for standings and must be played.
The TD will specify which direction the clocks must face.
The provided clocks will be set to "halt on end".
FIDE rated sections will use FIDE rules. A summary of the differences is here.
Phone Rules
All phones should be off. Phones should not be on your person when you leave the room. In non-FIDE rated sections you can store you phone on the table or in a bag next to your chair. Phone lockers are available for all sections.
Any with ringing phone or leaving (or returning to ) the playing hall with a phone will receive a time reduction of 30 minutes or half your remaining time which ever is less.
Anyone using their phone to affect the game will be forfeited.

Dates: March 21-22

Sections: Two sections, U1200 and Open. Players with ratings U1200, along with Unrated players, may register for either the U1200 or Open section.

email: Click here to show mail address

2026 TEXAS SENIOR STATE CHAMPIONSHIP
State Championship Event
THE HOUSTON CHESS STUDIO
Saturday, March 21, 2026
- Sunday, March 22, 2026
Event Overview
2026 Texas Senior Chess Championship
REGISTRATION: https://www.kingregistration.com/event/2026SeniorChamp
$375 First Place plus Trophy, 2nd & 3rd place trophies. PLUS the TCA will pay a $500 stipend for the winner to attend the 2026 Irwin tournament of Senior State Champions
A US Chess & Texas Chess Association sanctioned State Championship event
Organized by the Poison Pawns Chess Club , played at The Houston Chess Studio , 250 Patton St. Suite H, Houston TX 77009.
Always Plenty of FREE Parking at The Studio.
WHEN: Saturday, March 21, 2026 - Sunday, March 22, 2026
WHO CAN ENTER? - Any player aged 50 and over as of the first day of the John T. Irwin National Tournament of Senior State Champions 2026. The Texas resident winner of the Texas Senior Championship will be invited to play in the Irwin.
Entry Fee: $65 if received by March 1st, 2026, otherwise $85. GMs & IMs get free entry, entry fee deducted from any winnings.
US Chess and TCA Memberships Required.
Out of state players are not eligible for any prizes
5 Rounds of G/75,d5
Rounds: Saturday 10:00 am, 2:00 pm, 6:00 pm; Sunday 9:00 am, 1:00 pm.
Tie-breaks used are: 1) Modified Median, 2) Solkoff, 3) Cumulative, 4) Cumulative of Opposition.
One 1/2 point bye (rounds 1-4 only) is allowed if requested before round one
Prizes: Trophies to top 3. $375 for first place, plus the trophy, plus the TCA will pay a $500 stipend to play in the "John T. Irwin National Tournament of Senior State Champions." 2nd & 3rd place trophies to Texas residents.
The Texas resident with the highest score after round five will be named, " 2026 Texas Senior Chess Champion ". If two or more Texas residents are tied with the highest score after round five, they will all be named co-champions. Out of state residents are not eligible for any prizes. Trophies will be awarded to the top three Texas resident finishers using tie breaks.
The Texas Senior Champion will be invited to represent Texas in the 2026 Annual "John T. Irwin National Tournament of Senior State Champions" and, after competing in that tournament, will receive a stipend of $500 from the TCA to help cover expenses of attendance at that event. If there are co-champions, the champion with the highest tie breaks will be invited to represent Texas in the national tournament and receive the $500 stipend. If the first place winner does not play in the National Senior Tournament then the 2nd place finisher will be eligible for the $500 stipend. If the second place winner does not play then the 3rd place finisher will be eligible.
HOTEL INFO: Holiday Inn Express, 3401 N. Main St., is less than a mile from The Studio. Phone 832-834-6197 and ask for The Houston Chess Studio discount, or if booking online use code ALDR9. Also within a mile is the Heights House Hotel , an America’s Best Value, and a Luxury Inn . Google them for info.
RESTAURANT INFO: There are 3 restaurants in the same strip center as The Studio: The Red Hot Noodle (Asian), Subway, and Patron Pizza. Several others are within walking distance.

K-12 TEAM VARSITY FORMAT : 5-Round team Swiss tournament with 4 players per team and one optional alternate. A match is won by the team scoring the most game points (2.5 points or more out of 4 games).
Varsity I Division is Open to teams with any average rating. Varsity II Division is open to teams with an average team rating of less than 1100. Teams will be seeded based on a team rating derived from the rating average of the four players. Players must play in rating order except that the players within 50 rating points of each other may permanently switch positions prior to round one.
Unrated players can play on any board. In calculating the average team rating, an unrated on board four is assigned 50 points below the rating of board three. An unrated on board three is assigned the average of the board two and four ratings. An unrated on board two is assigned the average of the board one and three ratings. An unrated on board one is assigned 50 points above the rating of board two.
Schools may enter multiple teams in either section. No club teams are allowed. Players of all abilities are encouraged to participate. This is not a US Chess rated event.

A home school or virtual school student may play on either a public or private school team. To play on a public school team, the student must live within the attendance boundary (not district) from which that public school draws. Any private school seeking to have these students on their team must use the same public school attendance boundary in which their school building is located. Players from outside their boundaries are not allowed to play on that school’s team. Home-schooled students are considered to be in 9th grade when they are 14 as of September 1st of the school year. Players must be under the age of 19 as of September 1st of the school year.
RATINGS : March rating supplement will be used. Tournament Directors can choose the highest of the US Chess ratings (regular, quick, live, online) for pairing purposes only. Ratings are not affected by this event.

events.sourceText:
Battle on the BB-64
Nauticus / Battleship Wisconsin
Saturday, March 21, 2026
Event Overview
Hampton Roads Chess Association
and
Nauticus / Battleship Wisconsin
present
Battle on the BB-64
A chess tournament on the ship!
Norfolk, Virginia
March 21, 2026
REGISTER HERE: Battle on the BB-64
Hampton Roads Chess Association and Nauticus / Battleship Wisconsin join forces to present the third annual chess tournament to be held on board the Battleship Wisconsin (BB-64) docked at Nauticus on the Norfolk Waterfront! Games will be played in the Crew Mess, where sailors from WWII to Operation Desert Storm dined while underway!
There is a LOT of information to share for this event, and most questions can be answered below. Please read thoroughly!
By registering and attending in this event (as participant or guest), you acknowledge and agree to abide by the US Chess Federation's Safe Play Policy , and HRCA's Code of Conduct and General Liability Waiver and Release. More details below.
Registration for this event closes at 11:59pm EST on Thursday, March 19th! No last-minute or on-site registration!
This is an HRCA Scholastic Cup Event!
HRCA membership is not required for the tournament but IS required to participate in the Scholastic Cup awards.
New Memberships must be purchased within one week of event conclusion for points to qualify.
For more information visit https://hrchessclub.org/scholastic-cup/
SCHEDULE
9:15-10:00 AM - Recommended time to arrive for parking and walking to the venue. Check-in table to pick up pre-ordered wristbands on the deck outside the main entry to the Nauticus will be open by 9:30AM.
10:00 AM - Doors open
11:00 AM -- Round 1
12:15 PM -- Round 2
1:30 PM -- Round 3
2:45 PM -- Round 4
3:45 PM -- Awards in the Brock Theater
4:45 PM -- Photos on the fantail
5:00 PM -- Everyone must be off the ship / Nauticus closes
PARTICIPANTS
***NEW THIS YEAR -- THIS IS AN ALL-AGES EVENT!!!***
Players under age 14 require an adult to be onsite for the duration of the event -- All guests must have a Nauticus day pass (see below). We have a special group rate through March 19th. After that, you may purchase regular admission or utilize any discount programs directly with the front desk.
PLAYER REQUIREMENTS:
US Chess membership is required for Open, Amateur, and Novice -- these are rated sections.
US Chess membership is NOT required for Rookie sections.
HRCA membership is only required if you want your points counted for the HRCA Scholastic Cup.
FORMAT
A Swiss System (like a bracket system -- NOT an elimination event! ) tournament of four rounds. Time control is G/25; d3, meaning each side has 25 minutes to complete all their moves, and the clock will not start counting down for the first 3 seconds of each move. Select a bye during registration ONLY if you know you will be missing a round due to a conflict with another event. One half-point bye allowed if requested prior to the start of Round 3.
Boards, sets, and clocks are provided. Notation is NOT required in any section due to Quick time control, but notation sheets and pencils will be provided if desired.
Section choices are:
K-3 Rookie: Grades Pre-K through 3rd with little to no tournament experience. No rated players allowed. US Chess membership is not required.
K-6 Rookie: For youth in grades 4th-6th with little to no tournament experience. No rated players allowed. US Chess membership is not required.
Senior Rookie : For ADULTS and youth in grades 7th-12th with little to no tournament experience. No rated players allowed. US Chess membership is not required.
Scholastic Novice (U300): Youth in grades PK-12th who are US Chess members with a Regular over-the-board (OTB) rating Under 300. The March supplement will be used. Unrated players are allowed in the Novice section and are eligible for place prizes or Top Unrated prizes only.
Amateur (U800): All ages who are US Chess members with Regular over-the-board (OTB) rating Under 800. The March supplement will be used. Unrated players are allowed in the Amateur section and are eligible for place prizes only.
Open: All ages who are US Chess members -- unrated or of any rating -- but designed for players rated over 800. Playing up is allowed. Unrated players are allowed in the Open section and are eligible for place prizes only. The March supplement will be used.
A note on Unrated players: Per new US Chess Scholastic Regulations, HRCA will apply the current Regular OTB rating to Unrated players, if applicable, even if earned after the cut-off for the supplement used for the tournament. In a dual-rated event, if there is no Regular OTB rating, a current Quick rating will be applied, if applicable, but only for prizes, not sectioning (e.g. someone with a 500 published Quick rating but Unrated Regular may still play in the U300 section but is ineligible for Unrated prizes). Bottom line -- only actually Unrated players at the time of the event will be allowed in Rookie sections and eligible for Unrated class prizes in rated sections.
Check your US Chess membership here
AWARDS
Individual: TROPHIES to the Top 5 finishers in each section. Trophy to Top U1000 in Open. Trophies to Top U500 in Amateur and Top Unrated in Novice. Trophy to Top K-1 in K-3 Rookie. Medals to additional players with at least 2 points. Participation ribbons to all remaining players.
Team: A team is comprised of two or more players from the same school, with the top four scores counting toward the team score. Team awards will be cross-section with trophies for Top 3 Elementary Schools and Top 2 Middle Schools. Top High School trophy will be added only if more than one high school team enters by March 9th.
ENTRY FEE
$35 Early Entry Fee through 11:59 PM on Sunday, February 22nd.
$40 Standard Entry Fee through 11:59 PM Sunday, March 8th.
$45 Late Entry Fee through 11:59 PM Sunday, March 15th.
$50 Last Week Entry Fee through 11:59 PM Thursday, March 19th.
TOURNAMENT REGISTRATION WILL CLOSE AT 11:59 PM ON MARCH 19th. NO EXCEPTIONS. NO WALKUPS.
There are no scholarship or Title 1 entry fee waivers for this event.
REFUNDS
If you need to withdraw, please contact the Event Organizer.
Refunds will be given as a tournament credit ONLY. Refunds create a lot of administrative work and loss of important operational revenue to HRCA. Our default refund is to now give participants a CREDIT towards a future HRCA tournament. The credited amount will be $30 and is valid for 1 year. After February 8th, there is a 50% credit. No refunds after February 19th.
** Please check the ENTRY LIST before registering to make sure you do not register multiple times. Duplicate entries are subject to an administrative refund fee of $10.
Nauticus guest tickets must be purchased separately and are NOT refundable.
Tournament Orientation for New Players
There will be no New Player Orientation the day of the event -- Use this link and passcode for a recording of a complete orientation to tournament procedures and rules.
https://us02web.zoom.us/rec/share/k1QA3hzoj0hYP7z5uwD7DYE2Mn-atQYhQO6YHRxyvfL_FDVO5HqW1C_6MDyyTNmv.NxHuuWAIwUzGT4sB
Passcode: h.8mre41
A copy of the slides will be sent to all registered players the evening of March 19th. For an earlier copy, contact the event organizer.
Special Notes for Event Day
PARKING :
Adjacent garages are approximately $13 a day; the MacArthur Center garage within walking distance is $1 a day on weekends!
MEALS :
No outside food or drink is allowed inside Nauticus or the Battleship. For anyone bringing their own lunch and eating on the front porch, they have a lunch bin system. Guests can drop their lunches in the bin at check-in, and they’ll wheel it into storage. At lunchtime, you can bring it back out to the porch.
If you leave the museum, your wristband will give you re-entry. Please make sure your player knows where to find you or designate another adult to supervise if you leave the premises without your player. Be aware the tournament rounds are very close together, so do not depart the site with your player and risk missing a round.
The on-site cafe is under new management, and they are offering pre-orders of box lunches, which is strongly recommended to get your food on time for your player to eat between rounds -- Click here for a menu .
CLICK HERE TO PRE-ORDER LUNCH .
WAITING AREAS ("SKITTLES") :
Please enjoy the venue and pack light (you may go back to your vehicle if needed). All players and accompanying family members / friends are strongly encouraged to explore Nauticus and the Battleship between rounds! Camp chairs are not permitted at the venue.
The Brock Theater on the 3rd floor of Nauticus is the main waiting area for parents. This will be open to all museum guests, so please be mindful of others enjoying the space and secure your belongings. A short film will be shown at 11am and 2pm for all museum guests.
YOU MAY NOT USE THE NAUTICUS CAFE AS A WAITING AREA. Volunteers will be enforcing this.
*Parents of younger children who may not be able to navigate from the ship's crew mess back to Nauticus will be allowed to wait in the galley (standing) next to the crew mess.
Please make sure your players know where to find you after each round!
BATHROOMS :
There is ample access to public bathrooms in Nauticus. There is one bathroom available on the deck of the ship prior to descending the stairs to the crew mess. We STRONGLY urge parents to ensure their kids use the bathroom BEFORE the start of a round. Once the round has started, getting a child back and forth to a bathroom on the ship is challenging.
HANDICAPPED ACCESSIBILITY :
Access to the ship's galley requires the physical ability to climb up and down one short but steep ladder. Players unable to make that climb can contact us in advance to make arrangements for an alternative assigned board in an accessible area of the ship or Nauticus.
Discounted Group Nauticus/Battleship Tickets :
Required for all guests. Admission to Nauticus and the Battleship is included in the entry fee for players only.
IMPORTANT - After registering your player for the tournament, go to 2026 Battle on the BB-64 ADMISSION tickets to purchase your group rate admission tickets for family members or friends accompanying the player. You will receive a wristband upon arrival for entry. These tickets are non-refundable. Your PLAYER'S admission is included in their entry fee - do NOT purchase a ticket for registered players.
For accompanying parents / siblings / guests, the group admission rates (tax included) are: $15 for students (ages 3-17)
$18 for adults (ages 18+)
ages 0-2 free but must be listed on reservation
NO PLAYER UNDER THE AGE OF 14 MAY BE DROPPED OFF / UNACCOMPANIED FOR THIS EVENT. Carpooling is welcome. All players under age 14 must have a designated adult onsite for the duration of the day.
Group sales end March 19th at 11:59PM -- No exceptions. Regular admission fees may be paid at the door the day of event. Please visit the Nauticus website for any other eligible discounts and ticket reservations if not purchasing group tickets through HRCA. You will receive a confirmation with check-in instructions when you order tickets through HRCA.
VOLUNTEERS NEEDED !
Volunteers help ensure our events run smoothly and that players and families have an enjoyable experience. Volunteer spots include set up, clean up, wristband distribution, player escorts (Safe Play certification required), scorekeepers, CERTIFIED Tournament Directors (TDs), and assistant/junior TDs (not certified). Key (all-day) volunteers receive complimentary entry.
Sign up to volunteer for a part of the day here: Hampton Roads Chess Association: Battle on BB-64
CONTACT US
Please contact the Tournament Organizer:
For more information/questions, contact the Tournament Organizer, Tina, at [email protected] or 757-472-5909.
Email is the fastest way to reach us.
POLICIES AND RULES
It is our goal to provide a fun, safe, and supportive environment. Community partnerships are vital to HRCA, and we want to ensure we remain good stewards to our partners and their facilities. There is a lot of downtime during tournaments -- parents are responsible for supervising their children when they are not playing a scheduled match. Please note only designated areas of the facility are open to players and guests. No one is allowed in undesignated areas (including classrooms) at any time. No drop-offs for youth under age 14.
By registering and attending in this event (as participant or guest), you acknowledge and agree to abide by the US Chess Federation's Safe Play Policy , and HRCA's Code of Conduct and General Liability Waiver and Release. For more information on Safe Play or HRCA's Code of Conduct and General Liability Waiver and Release, please click the BLUE links above. Violations of these policies may result in warnings, or ultimately, disqualification or dismissal from the event without refund.
Photo Policy: Please be advised that photos and/or videos may be taken at HRCA events for use in HRCA's marketing, grant reporting, educational, news, or other promotional materials, whether in print, electronic, or other forms of media, including on our website and social channels. HRCA will not identify images using the full names of those photographed without express written permission. By attending an HRCA event, you consent to have your image recorded for distribution and agree to release, defend, hold harmless, and indemnify HRCA from any and all claims, including compensation, involving using your picture or likeness. CKQ Saturday Piscataway Rapids
Chess Kings & Queens Academy
Saturday, March 21, 2026
Event Overview
CKQ Saturday Piscataway Rapids
Start time: Players should arrive no later than 4:15 p.m. The first game begins promptly at 4:30. Latecomers risk their clock running when they arrive.
End time: The Under 600 section typically ends by 8:30 p.m., the Under 1200 section more like 9:00. The tournament could go a bit longer if players use all their time.
Players: Most players at this event will be children (ages 6-16), but adults are welcome to play. Beginners are welcome, but at a minimum players should know how to legally move chess pieces, recognize when they’re in check, and how to perform basic checkmates (ex; king and queen vs. king).
Structure / time controls: 4-SS, G30 +5. (Each player will play four games. Each player receives 30 minutes per game, plus another five seconds per move.)
Sections: Under 600 and Under 1200 rating sections. The Under 1200 section requires at least 500 rating to enter. Lower-rated and unrated players may enter with the tournament director's permission.
Requirements: A USCF membership is required to play in the tournament. Contact the tournament director if you need assistance creating or renewing a membership.
Equipment: Players do not need to bring any equipment. Players are recommended to eat before arriving, or at least bring a snack.
Registration: The registration fee is $30. Online registration closes at 5pm on the day of the event.
Byes: If you can’t attend the entire tournament, a half-point bye (limit one) is available for any round. Byes must be requested before the tournaments starts. If you are going to take first-round bye please contact the tournament director at least one hour before the tournament starts.
Prizes: Top three winners in each section receive a trophy or a medal.
For more information: Contact tournament director Stephen Lorimor ( [email protected] , phone/text: 908-286-0720).

Evanston 3x3, 3/SS G/60, d5
Levy Activity Center
Saturday, March 21, 2026
Event Overview
3SS G/60, delay 5. USCF Dual Rated
Open to players who are EITHER age 14 and older OR whose US Chess Current Published Regular Rating for the month of the tournament is 900 or higher.
US Chess Membership is required.
Three Sections
Section Gold: 1700 and over (1600 - 1699 may play up to Gold)
Section Silver: 1200-1699 (1100 - 1199 may play up to Silver)
Section Bronze: U1200 and unrated
Sections may be combined at TD discretion. IMPORTANT: We use the US Chess Current Published Regular rating for the month of the tournament to place players in sections. We don’t make exceptions.
Junior players: Junior players (under fourteen years) rated 900+ are welcome. Must be accompanied by an adult throughout the event. We do not accept junior players rated under 900.
Three rounds. Digital clocks are required and will be set to G/60, delay 5 . You may take one half-point bye in round 1 or round 2.
Prizes: Your prize is an excellent playing experience at a reasonable cost. We've been running these since 2007 and people like playing here.
Entry fee is $20. Please pre-register and pay here when registration opens. Online registration closes when the tournament is full; we don’t have a wait list; we reopen registration if spaces become available.
On-Site Entries: Check evanstonchess.org the morning of the tournament. If space is available on-site entries for $20 cash are taken on an as-available basis starting at 9:00 a.m.
Master and Expert Entries: First two Masters or Experts who sign up get free entry. If your USCF or FIDE regular rating is 2000 or higher, email your name and USCF ID to Click here to show mail address by 5 p.m. the Tuesday before the tournament to pre-register.
Schedule:
Check-in and On-site Registration from 9:00 to 9:30 AM.
Players must check in on the posted registration list by 9:30 am; players who don’t check in receive a half-point bye for the first round or will be paired with another late arrival.
First Round 9:50 am, last round over roughly 5:00 pm.
Bring your lunch! We will have a brief lunch break with no time to go out for food. On-site we have vending machine snacks, coffee and soft drinks.
Other information: Sets supplied. Bring digital delay clocks. Wheelchair accessible. No Smoking. Limit 50 players.

Fairfax Chess Tournament 3/21/26
Pozez Jewish Community Center of Northern Virginia
Saturday, March 21, 2026
Event Overview
Register at chessacademy.com/tournaments !
This tournament is for scholastic players in grades K-12 with and without prior tournament experience. We recommend that players in their first tournament choose the Unrated option, where they will be grouped by age and play 3 or 4 games.
Players who've previously done well in an Unrated section or have previous rated tournament experience should choose the Rated option, where they'll be placed in a group of 4 players according to their age and rating. Each participant then plays one game against each of the other three players in their group. At the end of the third game, the winner of each group receives a trophy.
This event should typically finish in 1-2 hours, but can potentially take as long as 3 hours for the most advanced players (although that is rare).
Everyone will use a clock! We'll go over how to use clocks on-site, and you can watch this short video to see how they work. Unrated section players will play a game in 10 minutes with a 5 second delay, and Rated games are 25 minutes with a 5 second delay for each player.
Players can play in the morning at 10am, the afternoon at 1pm, or both!
All sections are non-elimination, and all players participate in all rounds
If you're playing in the Rated sections and have a US Chess ID# and membership, please include it. If you don't have one, we will purchase it for you ($24 value!). If you're not sure what your ID# is you can look it up here
Please arrive 15 minutes before games start. Players who arrive after that may not be placed in quads.
Prices increase by $10 at noon the Tuesday before the tournament.
Questions? Please let us know at Click here to show mail address !

Mandatory to Submit this form online AFTER making the Zelle Transfer - Registration ends at 11:00pm the day before the event.
Payment : Zelle Transfer to [email protected] .(Include Participant Full name in the Memo Field during Zelle Transfer)
Inquiries : [email protected]
Lunch\Drinks : Not available at Location - Participants may bring sack lunches. Please plan accordingly
Tournament Policy :
Refunds: A player can receive Tournament credits if notified in an email by 11:00pm the day before the event. Players that no-show do not receive a refund. No exceptions.
Photography: Photos will be taken of the tournament
Note :
Parents/Guardians of Minors
We welcome children to play in our tournament, but please be aware of the following:
Your child will play against adults, will be treated like an adult, and will be expected to interact like an adult. Your child will not be supervised by us. If a child is under 16 years old, a parent/guardian must remain in the building.
Rule Variations in Effect at the Tournament
1H1. Director as witness only. In an event in which most games are not watched by directors, a director may refrain from correcting all illegal moves he or she may notice but simply serve as a witness should one of the players point out the illegal move before any moves have been made.
15A. Paper scoresheet variation. The player using a paper scoresheet may first make the move, and then write it on the scoresheet, or vice versa.

Event Overview
K-12 Under 1200 Swiss Tournament
Our tournaments are open to K-12 students rated under 1200 from any school!
This tournament has three sections based on age and rating, and players will only play opponents in their section.
All sections begin at 9am, and they are all four rounds and non-elimination. The tournament will conclude between 12-1pm with an awards ceremony, in which the top individuals and top team (min. two players from the same school, same section) in all three sections will win trophies.
Games are 25 minutes with a 5 second delay, for players using a clock
Clocks, sets, boards, score sheets and pencils provided
Free WiFi
Trophies awarded to top 3 individuals and top team in each section
Arrive and check-in by 8:45am at the latest. Announcements will begin promptly at 8:55, and round 1 will start at 9am
Early-bird entry fee of $40

4 round Swiss. Time control: Game in 25 minutes with 5 sec delay. Boards, sets, clocks and scoresheets will be provided.

events.name: RiseNShine Monthly Quads - Mar 22nd
events.sourceText:
RiseNShine Monthly Quads - Mar 22nd
Holiday Inn Express & Suites Gilbert near Mesa Gateway Airport
Sunday, March 22, 2026
Event Overview
OVERVIEW
Tournament Format: Round-Robin
Total Rounds: 3
Round Times: 2 pm and Rounds 2 & 3 on a rolling schedule
Time Control: G/30;+5 (Game in 30 minutes with a 5-second increment at each move.)
Games will be US Chess regular & quick-rated (so called dual-rated).
Players will be split into groups of four (quads) based on their ratings, from the highest-rated to the lowest-rated.
In case the last quad is not four players, they will play a mini-3 round Swiss tournament with 5-7 players or they may play double round robin.
Monthly supplemental OTB regular rating will be used. The Chief TD has discretion to use a player's USCF online rating (ONL) or live rating for pairing purposes in extreme cases where fairness will be preserved by doing so
Minor roster shifts to avoid family member pairings may be possible
No byes are available
Forfeit time is 30 minutes
WHEN
March 22nd , 2026 (Sunday) @ 2:00 PM
Please arrive at the venue at least 10 minutes before the start time.
WHERE
​Holiday Inn Express & Suites Gilbert near Mesa Gateway Airport
5530 S Power Road, Gilbert, AZ 85295, USA
Intersection: Power Rd & E Ray Rd
APPROXIMATE HOURS
2:00pm – 5:30pm
Might end early based on the quad.
REGISTRATION
Registration Link https://pci.jotform.com/form/260106735864156
Entry List
https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1pLx0Snwqym2nb8_dbdGhhH_MWYSULrSN0El3L18iKQs/
Entry Fee:
$25 on or before March 16th (Monday)
$30 through March 21st (Saturday)
$35 on March 22nd (Sunday) until 12:00 PM (noon)
Refunds are available only for cancellations made on or before Saturday, March 21st , and will incur a $5 administrative fee.
Registrations may also be transferred to a future tournament if requested on or before Saturday, March 21st .
No refunds for no-shows.
For cancellations, refunds or transfers, email [email protected] . Refunds will be processed after March 22nd .
PRIZES
For each quad,
- Trophy for 1st place.
- Trophy for 2nd place.
- Participation medals for all other players.
Special prizes:
- Trophy for best parent-kid pair (cumulative score and cumulative tiebreak score)
- Trophy for best siblings pair (cumulative score and cumulative tiebreak score)
REQUIREMENTS
Players must have current US Chess Federation membership. Expiration date of their US Chess membership must be later than the last day of the tournament.
Not sure if you have a membership? Need to check the expiration date of your membership? Visit: https://ratings.uschess.org/
Become a member or renew your membership: https://new.uschess.org/join-us-chess
ROUND TIMES
Round 1: 2:00 pm
Round 2: ASAP
Round 3: ASAP
End Time: Around 5:30 pm. Might end early based on the quad.

events.sourceText:
Super Sunday FIDE Tournament
Chess Kings & Queens Academy
Sunday, March 22, 2026
Event Overview
Note: This is a dual USCF - FIDE section of a larger USCF tournament (Super Sunday). Please read the information carefully. For the other sections and more events, please check our other listing.
Structure
- 3 rounds Swiss-Style. G75 +15. Accelerated pairings at the director's discretion.
- One half-point bye is available for any round, but must be requested before tournament start. All other requested byes are zero points.
- Clocks, boards, and weighed plastic pieces are provided. Players may use their own equipment with the agreement of their opponent.
- FIDE notice: Rules for late arrival will match standard USCF 60 minute rule.
Schedule
- Round times: 10:00 am / 1:30pm / 5:00 pm
USCF
- A current USCF membership is required to play.
- Players MUST have at least 1) 1700 USCF rating (live or current published), or 2) 1600 FIDE rating
FIDE
- A valid FIDE ID is required to play. Most players with a valid USCF membership may request a USA-flagged FIDE ID at this URL. Note that it may take several days to process. https://tinyurl.com/3zcjwmex
- There is no minimum FIDE rating for this event. There is a maximum rating of 2399.
- FIDE norms are not available at this event.
Registration
- Registration fee: $45
- Online registration only. Registration closes at 9:00 a.m. on the day of the event. On-site registrations are discouraged but may be accepted at the TD's discretion.
- Registration link: https://chesskq.com/tournament
- Free entry for all players rated 2200 or higher. ($45 will be deducted from the player's prize winnings.) E-mail name, USCF ID, and FIDE ID to Stephen Lorimor at [email protected] to sign up.
- This event has no age restrictions.
- Players signing up for a section they are not eligible to join will be automatically shifted to the appropriate section.
- Players ineligible to participate in any section of this event, or withdrawing before 9:00 AM on the day of the tournament, will receive a credit for a future class or tournament.
Prizes
Prizes are paid out via Zelle or PayPal. Check-by-mail available for anyone without these options.
- 1st place: $200
- 2nd place: $100
- Top U1800 (FIDE): $60
@45 players (across all three sections) - we serve doughnuts and coffee. Everyone wins!
@50 players - we add a Top Junior (under age 12) award to each section
@55 players - we add a Top Senior (age 55+) award to each section
@60 players - we increase 2nd place and "top under __ rating" prizes for all sections by $15
@65 players - we increase 1st place prizes for all sections by $20.
Additional information
- The tournament director for this event is Stephen Lorimor. Bye requests and other issues may be e-mailed to [email protected] , or by voice/text to 908-286-0720. Note that he may not notice or respond to e-mails, texts, or calls after 9:00 am the day of the event.
- The venue is located within walking distance of multiple restaurants and fast food businesses. No food is allowed at the playing tables, but a waiting room with tables is available.

Speedy Quads 65
J. Gilligan's Bar and Grill
Monday, March 23, 2026
Event Overview
Speedy - because the time control is G/5;d0 (each player gets 5 minutes to make all their moves.)
Quads - because we divide the players in groups of four based on ratings or skill level.
Players play two games against each of the three other players in their quad.
We hold a Speedy Quads tournament every fourth Monday each month. Speedy Quads has a FREE entry (but we do accept donations to cover the rating fees). There are no prizes. The games are blitz-rated and do not affect regular or quick ratings.
Time Control is G/5;d0; and we play double-round quads.
Register on site only - please arrive before 7:30pm. US Chess members will play rated quads. Non-members will play in an unrated small Swiss blitz tournament.

MSJE Chess Puzzle-Solving Championship 2026
Mission San José Elementary
Thursday, March 26, 2026
Event Overview
Our annual MSJE Chess Puzzle-Solving Championship is a free event for all MSJE students in kindergarten through second grade. The Puzzle-Solving Championship concludes our series of Thursday Night Tactics (TNT) in December through March.
Time: Thursday March 26, 2026, 7pm - 7:45pm
Format: a total of 4 rounds
Speed round: 18 chess puzzles, all puzzles on paper to solve in 10 minutes
Mathematics round: 4 chess-themed combinatorics questions, courtesy of MSJE Math Club
Blindfold round: 4 chess puzzles, 1 puzzle at a time is read out and also given out in text (but no pieces and board) and 2 minutes for contestant to write down a solution
Target round: 4 chess puzzles, 1 puzzle at a time is shown on demonstration board and 2 minutes for contestant to write down a solution
We may update event details, like sections and number of rounds, as the competition date approaches to ensure the best possible experience for all players.
Sections: one single section (K-2)
Prize: trophy to top solver in each grade

events.sourceText:
2025-26 CalChess Super States: K & K-5 Championship and K-12 Sections
Santa Clara Convention Center
Saturday, March 28, 2026
- Sunday, March 29, 2026
Event Overview
Join the 2025-26 CalChess Super States K & K-5 Championship and other K-12 sections for a high-level weekend of friendly chess competition! This is the greatest opportunity for scholastic players to earn state-level recognition in a supportive competitive environment, as well as to earn personal trophies.
Register here
You must log in or sign up before you can register.
Online registration closes at 12:00 a.m. the day of the tournament.
Onsite registration is subject to availability ($44 additional fee incurred).
Late fees applied starting March 21 or when reaching capacity.
Sections
Players will need to register based on their 2025-26 school grade and their March Supplement Rating (i.e., rating as of Feb. 19) into one of the following sections: K-12 Rookie (unr.)
K-12 Beginner (100-399)
K-5 Jr. Varsity (400-799)
K-12 Intermediate (400-799)
6-12 Jr. Varsity (800+)
KG Champ (400+)
K-5 Champ (800+)
6-12 Advanced (800+)
Play-up rule
A player may pay to play up one higher section, double play up is NOT allowed.
Players must be within 300 points of the rating cutoff to play up.
(Note: The rating used to determine if a player may play up is their March USChess Published Supplement Rating)
Schedule
K-5 Jr. Varsity, K-12 Rookie, K-12 Beginner & K-12 Intermediate: Time Control: 5x G/25 d5
Two schedules available: Saturday OR Sunday
Round Times: Sat, Mar. 28 - 9:00 a.m., 10:40 a.m., 12:20 p.m., 2:00 p.m., 3:40 p.m.
OR
Sun, Mar. 29 - 9:00 a.m., 10:40 a.m., 12:20 p.m., 2:00 p.m., 3:40 p.m.
6-12 Jr. Varsity: Time Control: 5x G/25 d5
Round Times: Sat, Mar. 28 - 9:00 a.m., 10:40 a.m., 12:20 p.m., 2:00 p.m., 3:40 p.m.
KG Champ: Time Control: 5x G/25 d5
Round Times: Sun, Mar. 29 - 9:00 a.m., 10:40 a.m., 12:20 p.m., 2:00 p.m., 3:40 p.m.
K-5 Champ & 6-12 Advanced: Time Control: 6x G/65 d5
Round Times: Sat, Mar. 28 - 9:00 a.m., 12:00 p.m., 2:50 p.m.
Sun, Mar. 29 - 9:00 a.m., 12:00 p.m., 2:50 p.m.
½-point bye is available for ONE (1) round, except for the last round (Byes must be requested at least 30 min before that round's start).
0-point byes are available for any round.
If you request more than one bye, we will give you a ½-point for the latest round possible except for the last round (0-point byes for all other rounds).
Awards
Personal Trophies to all players with a winning record. One trophy per player.
Trophy size vary based on standings.
Medals to all other players.
Team Trophies to all of the following with two or more players in all sections combined: Clubs
Schools
A player who withdraws during the tournament is not eligible for awards.
Fees
Entry fee: K-5 Champ and 6-12 Advanced: $113
All other sections: $79
Play up fee: +$29
Discount for BayAreaChess Membership Subscribers ( More info ).
Late fees, starting: Mar. 22: +$11
Mar. 24: +$22
Mar. 26: +$33
Onsite fee: +$44
BayAreaChess Membership discounts are NOT redeemable for late and onsite fees.
Withdrawals
Withdrawals are eligible for a partial refund, subject to the following deductions: until Mar. 21, 4% processing fee.
from Mar. 22 to Mar. 23, $11 withdrawal fee + 4% processing fee.
from Mar. 24 to Mar. 25, $22 withdrawal fee + 4% processing fee.
from Mar. 26 onward, NO REFUND will be issued.
Only withdrawals made before or on Mar. 25 are eligible for refund.
Change requests
After registration, changes can be requested at bayareachess.com/changeform and are subject to the following fees: until Mar. 26, $7 change fee.
on Mar. 27, $15 change fee.
The following requests are exempt from the change fee: playing up to a higher section.
requesting byes.
updating club and/or school.
Other requirements
USCF membership must be active.
More info available here .

events.sourceText:
2nd DMV Adults-Only Classical Tournament (In Person)
SpringHill Suites by Marriott Dulles Airport
Saturday, March 28, 2026
- Sunday, March 29, 2026
Event Overview
2nd Annual DMV Adults-Only Classical Tournament
SpringHill Suites by Marriott Dulles Airport
22595 Shaw Road, Sterling, VA 20166
NOTE: This is a different hotel than the one we used last year.
Saturday and Sunday, March 28-29
Register here: https://caissachess.net/online-registration/index/8462
Adults Only!
This tournament is only for adults. All players must be at least 18 years of age. If you are under 18, please do not register for this event. Thank you.
Tournament Information:
4 round Swiss tournament.
USCF regular rated. Time control: Game in 95 minutes with a 10-second increment.
Only open to adults (18+). No exceptions.
Round times: Saturday at 2 pm, Saturday at 6:30 pm, Sunday at 9 am, Sunday at 1 pm Later start on Saturday and earlier finish on Sunday allows players to drive to this tournament who live several hours away.
Entry fee: $58 by 3/15, $65 by 3/21, $70 by 3/27, $75 on the day of the tournament. National masters will current ratings over 2200 play for free ($58 entry deducted from prizes). Email [email protected] to register for free as a 2200+ rated player.
Three Sections: Premier (also FIDE rated), Under 1800, and Under 1400.
Note: Players may not play up more than 100 points. A player may use either their live (unpublished) or published rating to qualify for a higher section. Players may also use their FIDE rating to qualify for a higher section. In the event that a player uses their live rating (or FIDE rating) to qualify for a higher section, this rating will also be used for pairings.
Forfeit policy: A player who is more than thirty minutes late can be forfeited.
PRIZES: $200 for 1st, $100 for 2nd in Premier; $100 for 1st in U1800, $100 for 1st in Under 1400; Top senior overall in the tournament (50+) prize of $100 (includes $50 donated to this prize from last year's winner). (Note that the top senior prize is accross all sections and is calculated completely separately from the other prizes. It is possible for a player to win the top senior prize in addition to another prize.)
Up to two half-point byes are allowed. Half-point byes can be requested for any round. The deadline to request a half-point bye is prior to the start of round 3.
We will have enough chess sets for all players, but clocks will not be provided for everyone. If you have a clock, please bring one.
There is plenty of free parking at the playing venue.
For questions, please email us at Click here to show mail address or call us at 703-609-0499.
How to Register

events.name: Arizona Golden Cup 🏆
events.sourceText:
Arizona Golden Cup 🏆
Phoenix Chess Academy
Saturday, March 28, 2026
Event Overview
Arizona's Premier Year - Long USCF Chess Series.
Earn Points. Win Gold. Become a Champion. 🏆
A year-long USCF-rated chess series. Players earn Golden Points at each monthly event. Final standings after December determine the Arizona Golden Cup Champion, 2nd and 3rd Place in each section. Players may enter the series at any time during the year. Tournament is open to everyone. USCF membership is required.
4 Round Swiss G/30; d5 USCF-rated tournament series with cumulative points.
Sections: Open (1800 +). Under 1800. Under 1200. No playing up allowed. Official rating will be used for sections and prizes. Half point Byes available in all 4 rounds (Max 2) and must be requested before round 2. If a player moves to a higher section during the year, points earned in the previous section do not transfer. The player begins earning Golden Cup points in the new section.
Schedule: Round 1: 9:00 AM. Round 2: 10:15 AM. Round 3: 11:30 AM. Round 4: 12:45 PM. Ceremony will follow right after last game is over.
Entry Fee: $35.00 by Wednesday, $40.00 by Friday, $45.00 Same Day. Refund Policy: Full refund if canceling up to 1 hour before the event. No refund after that.
Awards: Top 3 Trophy in each section, Best U1400 and Best U800 in each monthly event.
At the end of the series-After December event: Champion Trophy (in each section) + 7 Months of Free entry for 2027 series. 2nd Place Trophy (in each section) + 5 Months of Free entry for 2027 series. 3rd Place Trophy (in each section) + 3 Months of Free entry for 2027 series. Players are eligible to win only one Arizona Golden Cup prize, awarded in the highest scoring section in which they competed.
Golden Points System:
Finish Points
1st Place 20
2nd Place 16
3rd Place 13
4th Place 10
5–6 8
7–10 5
Participation 3
Bonus Points:
+3 points — Perfect score (4/4).
+2 points (only in December) — Played Most consecutive months.
Monthly Event Tie-Handling (Point Splitting): When two or more players are tied for placement in a monthly Arizona Golden Cup event, Golden points are split evenly among the tied positions.
Tie-Breaks (Year-End):
1. Most 1st-place finishes.
2. Head-to-head results.
3. Most tournaments played.
4. Best December result.
TD decisions are final.

CKQ Saturday Piscataway Rapids
Chess Kings & Queens Academy
Saturday, March 28, 2026
Event Overview
CKQ Saturday Piscataway Rapids
Start time: Players should arrive no later than 4:15 p.m. The first game begins promptly at 4:30. Latecomers risk their clock running when they arrive.
End time: The Under 600 section typically ends by 8:30 p.m., the Under 1200 section more like 9:00. The tournament could go a bit longer if players use all their time.
Players: Most players at this event will be children (ages 6-16), but adults are welcome to play. Beginners are welcome, but at a minimum players should know how to legally move chess pieces, recognize when they’re in check, and how to perform basic checkmates (ex; king and queen vs. king).
Structure / time controls: 4-SS, G30 +5. (Each player will play four games. Each player receives 30 minutes per game, plus another five seconds per move.)
Sections: Under 600 and Under 1200 rating sections. The Under 1200 section requires at least 500 rating to enter. Lower-rated and unrated players may enter with the tournament director's permission.
Requirements: A USCF membership is required to play in the tournament. Contact the tournament director if you need assistance creating or renewing a membership.
Equipment: Players do not need to bring any equipment. Players are recommended to eat before arriving, or at least bring a snack.
Registration: The registration fee is $30. Online registration closes at 5pm on the day of the event.
Byes: If you can’t attend the entire tournament, a half-point bye (limit one) is available for any round. Byes must be requested before the tournaments starts. If you are going to take first-round bye please contact the tournament director at least one hour before the tournament starts.
Prizes: Top three winners in each section receive a trophy or a medal.
For more information: Contact tournament director Stephen Lorimor ( [email protected] , phone/text: 908-286-0720).

events.sourceText:
DMV Spring Scholastic Tournament (In Person)
SpringHill Suites by Marriott Dulles Airport
Saturday, March 28, 2026
Event Overview
The DMV Spring Scholastic
SpringHill Suites by Marriott Dulles Airport
22595 Shaw Road, Sterling, VA 20166
Saturday, March 28, 2026 at 9 am
Register here: https://caissachess.net/online-registration/index/8461
Note about special rules for pairings:
This tournament will feature Monrad pairings, which is a variation on Swiss pairings that reduces mismatches. The use of Monrad pairings eliminates the need for multiple sections as players are often paired against closely related opponents, especially in early rounds. To read more about Monrad Swiss pairings, visit Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swiss-system_tournament#Monrad_system Because we are using Monrad pairings, which are better at reducing mismatches, there are no separate K-3, K-5, K-8, and K-12 sections. Instead, there is just one section for everyone. To be eligible for grade-based prizes, please include the player's grade in the "grade" field when you register.
Advantages of Monrad Pairings:
Fewer mismatches, more games against closely-rated opponents
Eliminate need for multiple sections
Anyone can win the tournament (lower-rated players are more likely to play each other, which means that anyone has a chance to win)
Less playing down (higher-rated players are less likely to have to play down)
Tournament Information​
Four rounds: first round at 9 am, subsequent rounds occur as soon as possible
One section: Monrad pairings reduce mismatches, eliminating the need for separate K-3, K-5, K-8, and K-12 sections (see note above)
Time control: Game in 25 minutes with a 5-second delay ( US Chess regular and quick rated)
Prizes: trophies for 1st, 2nd, and 3rd in each section
Entry fee: $35 by 3/16, $40 by 3/23, $45 by 3/27, $50 by 3/28 (on-site registration closes 30 minutes before round 1)
Boards and pieces will be provided for all players, but we don’t have enough clocks for everyone (those who have clocks are welcome to bring them)
This tournament is US Chess rated, so an active US Chess membership is required. Click here to join the US Chess Federation for the first time or to renew an inactive membership: https://new.uschess.org/user/login?destination=/form/membership
Don’t hesitate to reach out to us at Click here to show mail address with any questions
Venue Information/Logistics
PARKING: The hotel has free parking on the street. In the event that street parking is full, the hotel also has a garage. Chess players can park for a special rate of $5 in the garage.
Free water will be provided for attendees.
There is no scheduled lunch break, but there is almost always time for players to have food between games. There aren't any scheduled round times--rounds will occur as soon as possible.
How to Register

EASTERN KENTUCKY OPEN
Morgan County Fiscal Court Building
Saturday, March 28, 2026
Event Overview
This is a qualifying event for the 2026 Kentucky Closed Championship. The top Kentucky player who has not already qualified will receive an invitation to this event.
US Chess Membership is REQUIRED. All US Chess rules will be followed.
Membership must be current through March 2026
Membership will NOT be available onsite, sign up at uschess.org
Please bring membership ID number to the tournament
Notation is required for all players. Players 8 years old or younger (or their parents) can ask
tournament director before Round 1 for an exemption.
Players younger than high school age (~14) must be accompanied by an adult.
FORMAT
Two Sections: both will be 4 Rounds - Swiss System
OPEN Section: open to all USCF players and any rating level
U1500 Section: open to USCF players with ratings below 1500 (unrated to 1499)
G30;d5 (clocks will be set to 30 minutes per player, 5 second delay)
Note: we reserve the right to have only one OPEN section if there is a low turnout the day of the tournament.
ENTRY FEE
$30 if pre-registered online by Friday, March 27th, 2026, otherwise $35 the day of the tournament.
CASH ONLY PAYMENT IS DUE BEFORE ROUND ONE BEGINS
SCHEDULE
Check-in and registration will take place from 9:15 AM to 9:45 AM on Saturday.
Round 1 will commence at 10:00 AM or soon thereafter, and the subsequent rounds will begin as soon as possible, approximately at 11:30 AM, 1:00 PM, and 2:30 PM.
Players who arrive late after round 1 is paired will receive a half-point bye in the first round and will be paired in subsequent rounds. One 1/2 point bye’s available for any round. Must declare during registration.
PRIZES
The tournament offers a prize fund of $1200 based on 30 players, and cash prizes will be
distributed promptly after the conclusion of the fourth round.
The distribution of closed championship invitations will be determined by a KCA (Kentucky
Chess Association) representative at a later date.
Please note that for the top female player, the cash prize will be awarded, but the invitation is for an alternate only.
One cash prize per player. Standard USCF Tiebreakers will be used in all sections to determine
the winner. If there are ties, the prize money will be equally divided.
In the event of a perfect score tie (4.0/4.0) in the OPEN SECTION for qualifying for the closed event a tie break game will be played G10;d5.
