Top adult player (21 and over) $200
Top junior player (under 21 at time of this tournament) $200
Top female player (USCF record must list "F" under gender) $200
Top U1900 $100
Top U1700 $100
Under 1500 Section
Top U1500 $100
Top U1300 $100
Top U1100 $100
Top Unrated $100
OTHER
A limited number of chess boards, pieces, and clocks are available, please bring your own if you have them.

Event Overview
Strategic Thoughts NOLA, Crescent City Chess, and Downriver Chess Present:
CLICK HERE TO REGISTER!
THE NEW ORLEANS YOUTH CHESS 2025-2026 SEASON
Venue: St Catherine of Siena Catholic School, 400 Codifer Blvd, Metairie, LA
Format: Four round swiss format, G/25;d5 tournament. Five sections: K-2; K-4; K-6; K-8, K-12
Prizes: Individual and team trophies in each section
Registration: 8:45AM-9:15AM; Anyone not registered by 9:15AM will be given a first round bye
Check in: Check in is not necessary if your name is on the "entry list" tab of the King Registration page and there are no problems listed
Round times: 10AM, 11:15AM, 12:30PM, and 1:45PM
Entry fee: $30 if received by midnight one week before the event date (Saturday night). $35 if received by midnight two days before (Thursday night). $40 day before or same day (Friday-Saturday).
USCF requirement: Current USCF membership required, join here. If your membership does not have an expiration date, it is not yet current.
Eligibility: All K-12 students are welcome. You do not need to be part of a school or chess team to compete.
Discount codes: Use code FAMILY for a $5 discount when registering multiple siblings of the same family. Use code LUNCH for a $10 discount if student or family receives free or reduced lunch benefits.
Contact: email Click here to show mail address .
Byes: Two half-point byes available upon request. All byes must be requested before round 3, with exceptions made for emergency situations. All bye requests final after beginning of round 1.
Teams: Teams are comprised of the top four players per school per grade section. Minimum two players to qualify as a team. Team totals are calculated using cumulative score of each player.
Late arrivals: Games are forfeited 30 minutes after the round start time if a player has not arrived.
Refunds: Players who withdraw 30 minutes before round one are eligible for a refund of their entry fee, minus any applicable payment-processor fees (typically 5-7%).
Calendar: Full season calendar here .

TCA Region V Scholastic 2026 (High School/ Young Ladies)
The Houston Chess Studio
Saturday, March 28, 2026
Event Overview
TCA Region V Scholastic 2026
(High School/ Young Ladies)
Date & Location
Date: March 28, 2026
Location: The Houston Chess Studio 250 Patton St. Suite I Houston, TX 77079
Contact Info
Organizer: Edgar Acosta
Email: [email protected]
Phone: (281) 844 4139
Pricing
Early Registration: $32, ends on March 1, 2026
Regular Registration: $37, between March 16-22, 2026
Late Registration: $40, between , March 23-26, 2026
Active USCF membership is required by February 15, 2026. Visit new.uschess.org/join-us-chess starting at $24 to join USCF or renew your membership!
Visit chess.jliptrap.us/hgroup.htm for $13 discount Scholastic memberships and renewals!
TCA Tournament membership is included in the tournament entry fee. Visit texaschess.org/memberships to join TCA or renew your membership!
Pricing is included in the registration form automatically.
Eligibility
Participants must live or attend school in one of these counties:
Austin, Brazoria, Brazos, Chambers, Fort Bend, Galveston, Grimes
Hardin, Harris, Houston, Jasper, Leon, Liberty, Madison
Matagorda, Montgomery, Newton, Orange, Polk, Robertson
San Jacinto, Trinity, Tyler, Walker, Waller, Wharton
The max number of registrations for this tournament is 74. Text Edgar Acosta to join a waiting list
Sections
High School Open: Any High Schooler may enter this section.
High School U1000: Only High Schoolers rated 1000 or below may enter this section.
Girls Open: Any Young Lady from Grade K-12
Girls U1000: Any Young Lady Under 1000
Note: Sections may be combined in case of low registrations.
Definitions:
High School - Grades 9-12; in some districts 10-12, if Junior High is 7-9.
Middle School - Grades 6 to 8 or 9 depending on how the school district divides them.
Elementary - K-6 if 6th grade is in the Elementary building, K-5 if 6 is in Middle School. A 5th-6th campus has been ruled Elementary, a 6th-only campus as Middle School.
Primary - K-3. Note that a first grader could enter K-1 or K-3 or K-5.
K-8 and K-12 schools and Home School Associations are divided K-5, 6-8, and 9-12.
Students not assigned a grade in school will be assigned a grade at the tournament based on their age as of September 1 of that school year as follows: six years old is assigned first grade, seven years old is assigned second grade, and so on through grade twelve.
Note: Sections are based on USCF January 2025 ratings. "Current" ratings may be used to pair unrated players but will not determine section placement. Accelerate Pairings will be used at the discretion of the TD the day of the tournament.
Tournament Format
Rounds: Swiss 5 Rounds, Game in 25 with a 5-second delay (G/25 d/5).
Membership: USCF and TCA memberships required.
Rules: USCF rules apply.
Open sections require notation and clocks (if available). Players who opt to not take notation will have their time start at 20 minutes instead of 25.
Reserved sections are strongly encouraged to use notation and clocks.
Touch-move / Touch-take: Applies to all sections. Younger players, especially in Kinder-1st Open, will be encouraged to keep these rules with gentle reminders as needed.
Equipment: Plan on bringing your own chess set and clock if you have one, money for lunch, and a good attitude! Every player needs to bring their clocks!
Please make sure your clocks are labeled with the player's name and USCF ID.
Chess sets for the whole tournament will be provided!
Schedule
No At-Site Registration. All registrations must be submitted online at before 11:59pm on March 26, 2026.
Please arrive between 8:15 and 8:45 to check in and get ready to play.
Round 1: Starts at 9:00 AM SHARP; subsequent rounds will start ASAP. No elimination.
Players may request a single 1/2 point Bye missed, 0 point Bye for any subsequent Byes. Any Byes need to be requested by Thursday March 26th, 2026 at 7pm.
Lunch break after Round 3, estimating 12pm-1pm.
Teams
Teams consist of two or more (2+) players in the same section from the same school/association.
Team members must attend the same school campus full-time or belong to the same Home School Association .
Sections are not combined for teams.
Team scores will be calculated by summing the top four (4) individual scores from each team.
Awards
Trophies: Top 5 individuals in each section and Top 4 teams in each section.
1st Place Finishers qualify for a spot in the State Regional Invitational April 18-19th .
Alternate awards (likely medals) to players who score 3 or more points but do not win a trophy.
Tie Breaks: Solkoff (sum of opponents' scores), Modified Median (dropping the lowest opponent's score), Cumulative of Opposition, then Cumulative (USCF Standard)
We look forward to seeing you at The Houston Chess Studio on March 28, 2026 for a day of competitive and fun scholastic chess!

West Texas '26 March Open
Mad Hatter's House of Games
Saturday, March 28, 2026
Event Overview
PURPOSE: Our goal is to expand rated chess opportunities in our community to benefit and encourage both new and experienced players.
MONTHLY SPECIAL PROMOTIONS & ANNOUNCEMENTS:
Always FREE registration for players with current USCF rating over 2000! Entry fee deducted from winnings.
SPECIAL AWARD: Check registration form for details
2025-2026 SEASON SPECIAL PROJECTS, CONTESTS & SPECIAL RECOGNITIONS:
2025-2026 Brilliancy Award - Throughout the 2025-2026 season, players may submit notation to report their, or their opponent's, most brilliant moves! The notation must be legible, clearly labeled with player names, and the brilliant move must be marked. All submissions will be reviewed, and the player with the most brilliant move this season will receive an award at the May Open! SUBMISSIONS DUE BY APRIL 30.
2025-2026 Texas Chess Association Region I Recognition Program (Details are to be determined) - Categories and nomination procedures will be announced in the spring. You'll be able to make nominations; self-nomination will not be allowed. Winners must be TCA members. Awards will be presented at the May Open! SUBMISSIONS DUE BY APRIL 30.
DATE: Saturday, March 28, 2026
LOCATION: Mad Hatter's House of Games; 1507 Texas Ave., Lubbock, TX 79401
START TIME: Round 1 begins at 11 AM (Players registered in advance online arrive to pay and check-in before 10:45; Players registering onsite arrive before 10:30am)
***NOTE: If you have not checked in by 10:45 you may receive a round 1 bye.
END TIME: Most sections will finish at approximately 5:30 PM. The Novice Sections will finish at approximately 4:30 PM if players use full time allowed, but usually end earlier. Section awards will be presented shortly after all players in a section have completed their final round. Lower sections typically wrap up earlier than higher sections.
COST: FREE REGISTRATION for players with current USCF rating over 2000 (entry fee deducted from winnings); $16/player for Early (Online at https://forms.gle/Uaj9FQctxt5TD73B7 ) or $21/player for Late (On-site) registration. Payment options include PayPal at the time of online registration or cash on-site at the door. ***There is a $1 cash payment discount, bringing cash payments down to $15 for early registration or $20 for onsite registration.***
REGISTRATION DEADLINES: Early (Online at https://forms.gle/Uaj9FQctxt5TD73B7 ) pre-registrations are due by 6 PM Friday, March 27, 2026. Late (On-site) registrations must be done between 10:00 and 10:30 AM on Saturday, March 28, 2026.
TOURNAMENT DETAILS:
Tournament Director: Robert Moore, Region I Director – Texas Chess Association
USCF Rated Event: Current USCF membership required - PLEASE update your membership prior to tournament day. Contact us if you need help registering or renewing your USCF membership.
Schedule: This is a swiss style tournament; See below for number of rounds and time controls for each section. Pairings will be posted 5 minutes after the last game in the previous round ends, and the new round will begin 10 minutes after the previous round is complete. This effectively adds a 10-minute break for players who are the last to finish a round. Round 1 begins promptly at 11 AM; if you are not checked in by 10:45, you may receive a round 1 bye.
Equipment: Chess sets and notation supplies will be provided. Some chess clocks will be available, but please bring your own clock if you have one .
Five sections as follows:
Open Championship - Must be rated above 1300. If fewer than 8 players are above 1300, highest rated players below 1300 will be used to ensure at least 8 players in the section; 4 Rounds, G/40;d5
Reserve A (U1300) - Rating between 950 and 1300 and unrated players; 4 Rounds, G/40;d5
Reserve B (U1000) - Rating between 750 and 1000 and unrated players; 4 Rounds, G/40;d5
Novice A (U800) - Rating between 350 and 800 and unrated scholastic players; 5 Rounds, G/25;d5
Novice B (U400) - Rating under 400 and unrated players 5th grade or below; 5 Rounds, G/25;d5
EXCEPTIONS FOR PROVISIONALLY RATED PLAYERS : Adult players with provisional ratings below 750 may choose to play up into a Reserve section, but they may also register for the novice section that matches their provisional rating. Scholastic players with provisional ratings may be placed in an appropriate section by the tournament director.
NOTE ABOUT PLAYERS' SECTION PLACEMENT: At the TD's discretion, sections may be added, deleted, or combined. A player near the rating cut-off may be moved to maintain an even number of players in as many sections as possible. Also, at the TD's discretion, section rating ranges may be revised onsite based on natural breaks in rating distributions, which could increase the number of players in the Open Championship section to more than 8.
RATING DETERMINATION: USCF ratings as of March 23 will be used to determine section eligibility for this event.
Prizes:
Cash prizes for Open Championship and Reserve Sections: Cash prize guarantees are based on 50 registered players .
The total guaranteed prize fund for 50 players is $350.
The available cash prize fund will be increased or decreased based on registration variance from 50 players. At 100 players, the prize fund will grow to $1000!
If there are fewer than 50 players, prizes may be given for fewer than 3 places in each section.
Ties will follow USCF rules for splitting cash prizes.
Trophies & medals for Novice sections:
Trophies will be awarded to the top three finishers in each Novice section.
Medals will be awarded to players who tie for third but do not receive a trophy.
Standard tie breaks will be used.
PHOTOGRAPHY: Photos may be taken during the tournament and awards ceremony. These images may be shared with Texas Chess Association, news outlets, or other interested groups or individuals. Images may be used for promotion of subsequent chess events.
CONTACT: Completing the registration form linked below should generate an email to the address used to complete the form. Prior to the tournament, another email communication will be sent with a link to check tournament registration details.
If you have any questions please email us:
Robert Moore - [email protected] ; 334-233-4373
Amy Jones - [email protected] ; 806-787-3568

Additional info:
US Chess Federation (USCF) membership required. On Site Registration Available. $3 off for adults, young adults and students if you register through our affiliation.
Parents/Guardians of young chess players are responsible for their children. Parents/Guardians must be present at all times of the tournament and may enjoy some light snacks or coffee in waiting area while games are in progress.
Boards and clocks will ONLY be provided for the Beginner/Youth section games. Open and Reserve section players must bring their own regulated clock and board (dimensions listed below).
Notation of moves on scoresheet is mandatory for Open and Reserve sections games. Scoresheets will be provided. No electronic scoresheets allowed.
By registering for this event, you also agree to have your photo taken to be used on our facebook page for promo purposes. Sometimes the local news stations show up as well.
♟️♟️♟️
For questions: Contact Luis Peralta or Mariela Treviño at [email protected] or (309) 737-2890
♟️♟️♟️
Tournament Directors: Gary Nordick & Mariela Treviño
♟️♟️♟️
Key Rules, Procedures, Cheating & Etiquette:
Scoresheets: Notation of moves in Open and Reserve sections is required. Players must record moves in algebraic notation, typically writing the move after executing it on the board.
Contacting the TD: Stop the clock and immediately call the Tournament Director for any rule violation, illegal move, or dispute.
Touch-Move Rule: If you touch one of your pieces, you must move it if it has a legal move. If you touch an opponent's piece, you must capture it if possible.
One-Hand Rule: Use only one hand to move a piece and press the clock.
Clock use: Make your move then press the clock to stop your time until it is your turn again. Running out of time before checkmate means you lose the game automatically.
Illegal Moves: If you make one, your opponent stops the clock, shows the TD the illegal move, and you get a time penalty (2 minutes extra time will be added to your opponent).
Castling: Touch the King first, then the Rook, using one hand.
"J'adoube" (I adjust): Say this before touching a piece to adjust it, not to move it.
Pawn Promotion: The pawn is considered "touched" when it reaches the promotion square and must be promoted immediately to the piece you place on that square.
No Outside Help: No computers, phones (strict penalties), books, or talking to others about the game during play.
Communication: Only talk to your opponent or the TD. Be courteous. Be courteous of the players and their ongoing games around you. Whisper if talking must happen.
Cell Phones: Keep them off and away; penalties are severe.
Disputes: Handle calmly; argue with the TD, not your opponent.
USCF Board Regulations & Features:
Square Size: 2.25 inches is standard, though 2 to 2.5 inches is permissible.
Overall Size: 20" x 20" or 22" x 22" (approx. 50-55 cm).
Material: Usually flexible vinyl, often featuring algebraic notation on all sides.
Proportion Requirement: The King's base diameter should occupy roughly 75% to 80% of the square size.
Where to Find More rules: The full rules are in the US Chess Federation's website under Official Rules of Chess section.
♟️♟️♟️

2026 Spring Tournament

Sunday, March 29, 2026
Event Overview
Organizer
Azeri Chess Academy LLC ( USCF Affiliate ID A9567106 )
Tournament Director
International Grandmaster and Local TD Ulvi Bajarani ( USCF ID 17112757 )
Tournament Purpose
This tournament is part of the Azeri Chess Academy Houston Circuit 2026.
Date & Time
Round 1 starts on March 29, 2026, at 10:00 AM .
Venue
Houston Chess Studio, 250 Patton Street Suite H Houston, Texas 77009.
Time Control
G/30, d10 (Each player gets 30 minutes with a 10-second delay per move).
Format
6-round Swiss system.
Pairings will be generated using ChessRoster SwissSys 11.75 (subject to updates to more recent versions).
Ratings
This tournament is USCF-rated , and the official April 2026 USCF ratings will be used.
Byes
Up to two (2) half-point byes is allowed and must be declared during registration.
No additional byes are permitted except for 0-point byes .
A 1-point bye is awarded to a player who is left without an opponent when the number of players is odd in a given round.
Entry Fee
$60 – Until February 28, 2025, or for the first 10 players, whichever comes first.
$80 – Until March 14, 2026, or for the next 20 players, whichever comes first.
$100 – Until March 29, 2026 at 12:00 AM (midnight), or until all spots are filled.
Cancellation & Refund Policy
A 50% refund will be granted if a player requests cancellation by March 25, 2025, at 12:00 AM (midnight) .
No refunds will be issued after this deadline.
Withdrawal Policy
Players must notify an arbiter before the start of a round if they intend to withdraw.
Failure to notify an arbiter may affect eligibility for future tournaments organized by Azeri Chess Academy LLC.
Number of Entries
Maximum of 64 participants.
Eligibility
Open to all players with active USCF membership .
Players must ensure their USCF membership is active before the start of Round 1.
Onsite check-ins may be available for players needing USCF membership renewal. They must pay the required renewal fee plus an additional $10 processing fee.
Failure to renew an expired membership before the tournament will result in exclusion without a refund .
Tournament Schedule (Estimated Round Start Times)
1st Round – 10:00 AM
2nd Round – 11:25 AM
30-minute break
3rd Round – 1:20 PM
4th Round – 2:45 PM
5th Round – 4:05 PM

Prize Fund

If rating prizes are offered, unrated players are eligible only for prizes in the lowest rating group . This does not affect their eligibility for the overall (main) prizes.
Prizes are equally shared in case of a tie .
Payments will be sent via Zelle/PayPal before April 5, 2026. Prize-winners must contact the organizer immediately after the final round to confirm their preferred payment method. Additionally, the prize winners are required to participate in the prize ceremony following the tournament. Failure to complete these actions will result in disqualification from receiving the prize.
Tiebreaks
Tiebreaks will be determined using ChessRoster SwissSys , applying standard USCF tiebreak methods :
Solkoff
Modified Median
Cumulative
If players are tied for 1st place and all tiebreaks are equal , a coin toss will determine the winner.
Anti-Cheating Measures & Electronic Devices Policy
All players are subject to electronic device scanning (“wanding”) .
No electronic devices (phones, smartwatches, etc.) are allowed unless explicitly permitted by the arbiter for medical reasons .
A designated storage box will be provided for electronic devices.
Photography & Video Recording
By registering, players consent to being photographed and recorded by the Tournament Director and their associates for promotional purposes.
Equipment & Notation Rules
Chess sets, clocks, scoresheets, and pens will be provided by the organizer.
Notation is mandatory unless a player has less than 5 minutes remaining on their clock.
Players may keep a yellow scoresheet copy and a pen . However, players are encouraged to bring an extra pen , as available pens may be limited .

Entry fee: $30 on or before Wednesday the week of the tournament, $35 on or before Saturday, $40 on Sunday (on-site registration is allowed, registration for round one closes at 4:45 pm on Sunday). Free entry to players over 2200 ($30 entry deducted from prizes--please email to register).
Two Sections: Open (minimum 1300 rating to play) and Under 1500.
Note: In order to play in the open section, players must have a USCF rating of at least 1300. Players rated between 1300 and 1499 can play in either section. Players under 1300 should play in the Under 1500 section. A player can still join the open section if their unpublished (live) rating is over 1300, even if their monthly rating isn't 1300 yet. The tournament director may decide to have a lower rated player join the open section to maintain an even number of players in the section. The tournament director has the option to use a provisionally-rated player's live rating (regardless of whether it is higher or lower than the player's official rating) for pairings purposes and section eligibility.
PRIZES: $100 for 1st in Open; $50 for 1st in U1500.
Up to two half-point byes are allowed. Half-point byes can be requested for any round. The deadline to request a half-point bye is prior to the start of round 3.
We will have enough chess sets for all players, but clocks will not be provided for everyone. If you have a clock, please bring one.
This tournament is open to everyone (adults and children of any skill level).
There is plenty of free parking at the playing venue.

events.sourceText:
MSJE 2026 Qingming to Lixia Monday Night Marathon
MSJE MUR
Monday, March 30, 2026
- Monday, May 11, 2026
Event Overview
MSJE 2026 Qingming to Lixia Monday Night Marathon is a USCF-rated tournament for all members of MSJE Chess community.
Qingming 清明, also known as Clear and Bright, is the 5th of the 24 solar terms in the Chinese lunar calendar.
Guyu 谷雨, also known as Grain Rain, is the 6th of the 24 solar terms in the Chinese lunar calendar.
Lixia 立夏, also known as Start of Summer, is the 7th of the 24 solar terms in the Chinese lunar calendar.
Date: Monday, Mar 30, 2026 - Monday, May 11, 2026
Rating: USCF Dual-Rated
Eligibility : The tournament is open to MSJE students, parents, and alumni. Players must have current US Chess Federation membership. Expiration date of their US Chess membership must be later than the last day of the tournament.
Capacity : 50
Tournament Format : Swiss System
Total Rounds : 7
Time Control : G/25;+5 (game in 25 minutes with a 5-second increment with each move. This means you get 25 minutes, your opponent gets 25 minutes, and with each move players get 5 seconds added to their clock.)
Round Times: 3/30 6:40pm, 4/6 6:40pm, 4/13 6:40pm, 4/20 6:40pm, 4/27 6:40pm, 5/4 6:40pm, 5/11 6:40pm
Sections: 800+, 400-799, Under 400
We may update event details, like sections and round times, as the tournament date approaches to ensure the best possible experience for all players.
Parental Guidelines:
Non-playing parents are kindly asked to drop off and pick up their children. Only players and tournament staffs are allowed to remain inside MUR while games are in progress. Thank you for your understanding.
Tournament Rules:
All US Chess tournament rules apply.
The tournament director's decisions are final.
Notation is required, per MSJE Chess Head Coach's policy.
Bye Request:
Maximum three half-point byes are available upon request. Please submit the request of half-point bye by 7pm Sunday before the Monday round.
Equipment:
Chess sets will be provided.
Please bring own notation sheets and pencils.

Event Overview
CCC FIDE Spring Classical Apr 2 to 5, 2026
Coppell Chess Club is proud to present the CCC FIDE Spring Classical 2026 , a FIDE & USCF rated classical tournament featuring guaranteed cash prizes of over $5,000 and 30 Grand Prix points.
When:

2-Day Schedule :

Where:

Irving, TX 75063
Hotel reservations & booking:
To book hotel click on the link below. If the link says Texas State Open do not worry, we are in process of correcting it.
https://app.marriott.com/reslink?id=1767373855911&key=GRP&app=resvlink
Complimentary Breakfast for up to 2 guests per room
Complimentary Self-Parking
Complimentary Airport Shuttle to/from DFW International Airport
Time Controls:
4-Day Schedule : All rounds G90; +30 sec
3-Day Schedule : Round 1: G60;+10 sec, Round 2-7: G90; +30 sec
2-Day Schedule : Round 1 to 3: G30;d5 sec, Round 4-7: G90; +30 sec
Sections and Prizes:
Championship Section (1800+) – FIDE and USCF rated
$1500 - $750 - $375
Under 1800 Section (1400-1799) – FIDE and USCF rated
$800 - $400 - $200
Under 1400 Section – USCF rated Only
$600 - $300 - $150
Entry Fee:
$149 Early Bird offer on or before Feb 28, 2026
$169 Regular Fee
$189 Late Entry Fee after March 22, 2026
GM/IM play for free if registered before Mar 9, 2026
Play up Fee:
Players may pay $35 extra to play up if your monthly/live rating is within 150 points for that section.
Monthly/Live rating will be used to determine if play up is needed or not.
Players will be added in the section based on the rating. If play up fee is paid, we will move them to the upper section if not they will be adjusted to appropriate section.
Re-entry:
Players playing 4-day or 3-day schedule can reenter the 3 or 2-day schedule by paying $40 extra.
Contact us at least 30 mins before the start of 3 day or 2 day schedule for re-entry.
Byes:
Up to Two ½ point bye allowed for any round except for the last round. Bye has to be requested before end of round 2.
Zero-point bye/withdraw has to be requested before the section pairing is done.
Withdrawals:
Withdrawals can be requested 1 week before the tournament start date. Refunds will incur a $15 processing and transaction fee.
NO REFUNDS/NO CREDITS after March 27, 2026 and NO EXCEPTION.
More Details:
March US Chess ratings and rules will be used for pairings and awarding prizes.
FIDE Laws of Chess apply to FIDE rated sections; US Chess rules apply to other sections
Unrated players will be placed at TD’s discretion. Foreign players must disclose FIDE ID, foreign ratings or online ratings before round one is paired. Failure to disclose playing history may result in forfeiture and withdrawal from the event.
USA players without a FIDE ID and playing in FIDE rated sections must obtain a FIDE ID from US Chess or must disclose city, state, email, date of birth and agree to receive a USA FIDE ID.
No Spectators allowed in tournament area.
All non-essential communication devices must be powered off completely while inside the playing hall (not just on silent) and must remain in the player’s bag or face up on the table. Devices must remain at the board during game play. Penalties up to or including loss of game and removal from the tournament for violations of this policy.
Only FIDE and US Chess approved electronic notation devices are allowed; players in FIDE sections must email (PGN) game files to the organizer. Duplicate scoresheets required in FIDE sections.
Notation required for all sections and must continue for the entire game. Per rules, moves must be made on the board before recording them and the king must be moved first when castling.
Please bring your own clock . Boards and sets will be provided.
Only snacks and drinks allowed at the chess board. All other food must remain outside the playing room.
Default late forfeiture time is one hour. TD may extend this time at TD’s discretion.

events.name: $2,500 APRIL CHAMPIONSHIP 2026
events.sourceText:
$2,500 APRIL CHAMPIONSHIP 2026
The Houston Chess Studio
Friday, April 3, 2026
- Sunday, April 5, 2026
Event Overview
$2,500 APRIL CHAMPIONSHIP 2026
Open to Poison Pawn members AND non-members*
US CHESS RATED - MUST BE A US CHESS MEMBER TO PARTICIPATE
WHEN: MARCH 3-5 or MARCH 4-5 Three-day or two-day schedule, take your pick.
WHERE: Houston Chess Studio, 250 Patton St. Suite H, Houston TX 77009
FORMAT: 5 round Swiss, G/90, +30. (round 1 of 2 day schedule is G/60,d5)
3 day schedule : Round 1 at 6:30pm Friday night . Round 2 at 1pm Saturday and Round 3 at 6pm. Round 4 at 9:30 am Sunday and Round 5 at 2:00 pm.
2 day schedule : Round 1 is at 9:30am Saturday morning and is G/60, d5. Then merges with the 3 day schedule for rounds 2-5.
ENTRY FEE: Non-members $105 thru Friday MAR 20TH; then $125 thru Wednesday MAR 25TH; $135 thereafter. Poison Pawns club members $80 anytime! For membership info contact Edgar at : Click here to show mail address GMs and IMs may enter free, their entry fee will be deducted from winnings.
2 SECTIONS: Championship (1900 and up); Challengers (U1900).
PLAYING UP: If you are rated U1900 but are at least 1700 you may play up into the Championship section for $35.
PRIZE FUND $2,500 - 1st place in each section is guaranteed . 2nd place and 3rd place 25% OF ENTRY FEES B/50 in all sections combined. 15% BONUS FOR CLUB MEMBERS . Championship 1st $800 ; Challengers 1st $550 . Un-rated may play in any section but are limited to winning $150 except in the top section where they are eligible for all prizes. DRAWS PRIOR TO 30 MOVES AND BOTH PLAYERS ARE INELIGIBLE FOR ANY PRIZE MONEY!
ONLY MEMBERS OF POISON PAWNS CHESS CLUB ARE ONLY ELIGIBLE FOR 100% OF THE CASH PRIZES ! (So isn't it time you joined!)
CLICK HERE TO BECOME A MEMBER
CANCELLATION: You may cancel up to 72 hours before the beginning of Round 1 and get a refund of what you paid minus $25, or you may apply the entire amount towards a future entry fee IF USED WITHIN 30-DAYS OF ORIGINAL EVENT .
BYES: One ½ point bye available, must be declared before the beginning of round 2. No last round byes except for zero point byes.
RE-ENTRY: If you are in the 3-day schedule, after round 1, you may re-enter immediately for $35 and be given a choice of a ½ point bye for round 1 OR you may choose to play in round 1 of the 2-day schedule. If you are in the 2-day schedule you may re-enter immediately after round 1 and take a ½ point bye for round 1.
HOTEL INFO: Holiday Inn Express , 3401 N. Main St., is less than a mile from The Studio. Phone 832-834-6197 and ask for The Houston Chess Studio discount, or if booking online use code ALDR9. Also within a mile is the Heights House Hotel, an America’s Best Value, and a Luxury Inn . Google them for info.
THE HOUSTON CHESS STUDIO: is dedicated to providing a quality, high tech, chess playing experience for players of all levels. Centrally and conveniently located at 250 Patton St., Suite H, Houston TX 77009. Just inside North Loop 610 and just 2 blocks off North I-45. There are 3 restaurants in the same strip center as The Studio: The Red Hot Noodle (Asian), Subway , and Patron Pizza . Several others are within walking distance. Plenty of FREE parking.
SCANNING All players are subject to being scanned (“wanded”) in order to help prevent cheating. Any excessive visits to the bathroom will trigger a compulsory wand. Any player found with a phone or electronic device during a tournament game will be disqualified.
UPCOMING EVENTS https://www.kingregistration.com/affiliate/poisonpawns
QUESTIONS? Contact Edgar at Click here to show mail address or 281-844-4139.

Suite H
Houston , TX 77009
United States

OPEN TO ALL K-12 PLAYERS (EVEN OUT OF STATE PLAYERS)

Register for 2026 Central PA K-12 Scholastic Championship

events.sourceText:
4th Austin Chess Tour: Junior Qualifier #4
Saturday, April 4, 2026
Event Overview
4th Austin Chess Tour: Junior Qualifier #4
In-Person Scholastic USCF Rated Tournament
April 4, 2026
12466 Los Indios Trail, Ste. 100
Austin, TX 78729
* USCF Membership Required *
Free Parking Provided
Capacity: 100 players
Note that this is a scholastic event, only players who are 18 years of age or under can play in this tournament.
All players will be divided into five sections:
SECTION A: 1600+ USCF rated
SECTION B: 1200 - 1599 USCF rated
SECTION C: 800 - 1199 USCF rated
SECTION D: 400 - 799 USCF rated
SECTION E: Under 400 USCF rated or unrated
**Players are not allowed to play up or down**
ENTRY FEES:
Early Bird: $40 before 11:59pm, March 15, 2026
Standard Fee: $50 before 11:59 March 29, 2026
Late Fee: $65 after March 30, 2026
PRIZES:
Trophies for 1st Place, Medals for 2nd and 3rd
Junior Qualifier Points:
Top 10 places in Section A will earn points according to the following table:
1st Place: 25 JQ Points
2nd Place: 18 JQ Points
3rd Place: 15 JQ Points
4th Place: 12 JQ Points
5th Place: 10 JQ Points
6th Place: 8 JQ Points
7th Place: 6 JQ Points
8th Place: 4 JQ Points
9th Place: 2 JQ Points
10th Place: 1 JQ Points
For more information about the point system, visit
https://austin-chess.com/tournaments/
TIME CONTROL:
Section A: G/60, d5 (60 minutes per player with a 5-second delay)
Section B: G/60, d5 (60 minutes per player with a 5-second delay)
Section C: G/45, d5 (45 minutes per player with a 5-second delay)
Section D: G/30, d5 (30 minutes per player with a 5-second delay)
Section E: G/30, d5 (30 minutes per player with a 5-second delay)
4-Round Swiss System Schedule
SECTIONS A and B:
1st round: 9:00 AM
2nd round: 11:15 PM
Lunch Break: 1:30-2:30 PM
3rd round: 2:30 PM
4th round: 4:45 PM
SECTION C:
1st round: 10:00 AM
2nd round: 11:45 AM
Lunch Break: 1:30-2:30 PM
3rd round: 2:30 PM
4th round: 4:15 PM
5-Round Swiss System Schedule
SECTIONS D and E:
1st round: 10:00 AM
2nd round: 11:15 AM
3rd round: 12:30 PM
Lunch Break: 1:30 PM
4th round: 2:30 PM
5th round: 3:45 PM
Closing ceremony: After the last game of the section finishes.
NOTE: Half-point byes are acceptable for all rounds, limit 1. Must commit before the 1st round.
PLAYERS MAY NOT POSSESS CELL PHONES DURING THE TOURNAMENT. Please leave your phone at home, in your car, or turned off (vibrate/silent not acceptable) on top of your table.
Any violators may be subject to disqualification and forfeiture.
CANCELLATION POLICY: If you do not wish to participate in our tournament after paying the entry fee, please email us at [email protected] no later than 24 hours in advance for an 80% refund. We reserve the right to charge a service fee for cancellations. NO refunds will be issued if we are notified of cancellation within 24 hours of the start of the event.
WITHDRAWAL POLICY: If you would like to withdraw from the tournament after it begins, please alert the tournament director. NO refunds will be issued after the tournament begins.
NO-SHOW POLICY: There are NO refunds or credit for players who do not show up for their scheduled tournament matches.
For additional questions, please contact us at [email protected]

Holy Cross Lutheran Church

Event Overview
G/45;d5 - Quad Format - No Prizes - All ratings welcome. $10 entry - cash only - Adults and Kids Welcome No Late Entries - No Byes - No Withdrawals ONSITE REGISTRATION ONLY US Chess Membership Required, will affect quick and regular rating. Location:
9:15 AM - Registration Begins
9:45 AM - Registration Ends (NO LATE ENTRIES)
10:00 AM - Round One
12:30 PM - Round Two
2:15 PM - Round Three
What is Quad Format? Players are grouped in order of rating. The top four are grouped, then the next four are grouped, and so on. The groups (quads) of four play each other in a three-round round-robin. No late entries, no withdrawals . Quads are round robins. Please do not play if you can't stay for all three games. Leaving in the middle of a quad is rude and provides an extreme inconvenience to the other three players in your quad.

Caveman April 3x3 Fundraiser
Signature Regus
Saturday, April 4, 2026
Event Overview
Saturday, April 4th, 2026.
Signature 222 South Prospect, Floor R, Park Ridge, IL 60068
3 Sections: Gold (1800 and up), Silver U1800 (1400 - 1799), and Bronze U1400 (below 1400). Play-up fee: $20.
Rounds/Style: 3-round Swiss System
No tournament check-in at the site is needed. Just verify your registration online before the tournament. If there are issues that require making changes to your registration, please visit cavechess.cc/change .
This is a fundraiser tournament. All proceeds are going to Caveman Chess Charities, a registered 501(c)(3) in the state of Illinois. A donation of $20 is required. Anything more than $20 is optional and very appreciated.
Caveman Chess Charities focus on the disabled (at this point, primarily the blind) and the disadvantaged. The blind often have limited income, and we are raising funds to assist them with the upcoming US Blind Championships. Our focus is to reduce hotel costs. You may donate via GoFundMe at https://cavechess.cc/Donate . THANK YOU!

Schedule: 9:00 AM, 12:00 PM, 3:00 PM.
Entry Fee:
$15 online until 3/28.
$20 online until 4/4.
$10 off for Caveman Chess members.
Online entries only, no entries onsite.
Byes: One ½-point bye available for any round, committed by the end of round 1. No byes may be added or rescinded after round 1.
ENT: Register online at Caveman Chess Registration

4 round Swiss. Game in 25 minutes with 5 sec delay. Boards, sets, clocks and scoresheets will be provided.

Time Control: G/30;+5 (Game in 30 minutes with a 5-second increment at each move.)
Games will be US Chess regular & quick-rated (so called dual-rated).
Players will be split into groups of four (quads) based on their ratings, from the highest-rated to the lowest-rated.
In case the last quad is not four players, they will play a mini-3 round Swiss tournament with 5-7 players or they may play double round robin.
Monthly supplemental OTB regular rating will be used. The Chief TD has discretion to use a player's USCF online rating (ONL) or live rating for pairing purposes in extreme cases where fairness will be preserved by doing so
Minor roster shifts to avoid family member pairings may be possible
No byes are available
Forfeit time is 30 minutes
WHEN
April 4th , 2026 (Saturday) @ 2:00 PM
Please arrive at the venue at least 10 minutes before the start time.
WHERE
​Holiday Inn Express & Suites Gilbert near Mesa Gateway Airport
5530 S Power Road, Gilbert, AZ 85295, USA
Intersection: Power Rd & E Ray Rd
APPROXIMATE HOURS
2:00pm – 5:30pm
Might end early based on the quad.
REGISTRATION
Registration Link https://pci.jotform.com/form/260105957774161
Entry List
https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1EIrAhiFxQymJxGy_XrWVWuUx3uERRfYlq1JYQOw0cM0/
Entry Fee:
$25 on or before March 30th (Monday)
$30 through April 3rd (Friday)
$35 on April 4th (Saturday) until 12:00 PM (noon)
Refunds are available only for cancellations made on or before Friday, April 3rd , and will incur a $5 administrative fee.
Registrations may also be transferred to a future tournament if requested on or before Friday, April 3rd .
No refunds for no-shows.
For cancellations, refunds or transfers, email [email protected] . Refunds will be processed after April 4th .
PRIZES
For each quad,
- Trophy for 1st place.
- Trophy for 2nd place.
- Participation medals for all other players.
Special prizes:
- Trophy for best parent-kid pair (cumulative score and cumulative tiebreak score)
- Trophy for best siblings pair (cumulative score and cumulative tiebreak score)
REQUIREMENTS
Players must have current US Chess Federation membership. Expiration date of their US Chess membership must be later than the last day of the tournament.
Not sure if you have a membership? Need to check the expiration date of your membership? Visit: https://ratings.uschess.org/

Round 2: ASAP

Event Overview
Sponsored by the Leon County Division of Tourism/Visit Tallahassee and Challenger Learning Center (CLC) , the Tallahassee Young Knights (TYK) Chess Club is organizing a USCF-rated chess tournament in April 2026 at CLC, located in the heart of downtown Tallahassee. The main event will be a four-round Quick tournament, along with a six-round Blitz side event. More details can be found at our CLC website and event page .

Date: April 5th (Sunday), 2026
Location: Challenger Learning Center, 200 S Duval St, Tallahassee, FL 32301

Prizes: $80 + trophy 1st, $60 2nd, $40 1st U1400, $40 1st U800
Notes: Active USCF membership is required. You are strongly encouraged to bring your own chess sets and clocks (a limited number will be provided by the organizer).

WWW.SCSCHOLASTIC.COM

April 11, 2026

Registration Details
Open to all SC K-12 Girls (Girls are permitted and encouraged to play in both State Championship on March 21, 2026 as well as Girls' Championship on April 11, 2026)
Online Registration Only. $30 by April 4, 2026, $40 thereafter. Registration closes at 8:30 a.m. the morning of the tournament.
All equipment provided. No check-in required: players not reporting to their first round game before their time expires will be withdrawn from the tournament. Please contact Click here to show mail address if there are any issues with your registration.
Pairings and standings available in real time online, see "Pairings & Standings" in www.scscholastic.com menu.
Active USCF membership required. Memberships can be purchased/renewed at uschess.org/join-us-chess .
Register Now
Format
The Girls' Championship tournament is organized as a single-section (K-12) tournament, 5-Round Swiss G/30;d5.
Schedule
Round 1: 10:00 a.m.
Round 2: 11:20 a.m.
Round 3: 1:30 p.m.
Round 4: 2:50 p.m.
Round 5: 4:10 p.m.
Awards: 5:40 p.m.
Prizes
Top 8 receive trophies. Superlative awards to youngest participant, best debut, and biggest upset.
The SC Chess Association awards the first place finisher an invitation and a stipend to compete as the South Carolina representative to Haring National Tournament of Girls State Champions . The WIM Ruth Haring National Tournament of Girls State Champions is an annual invitational event run by US Chess that has determined the Haring National Champion since 2013 . A total of $18,700 in prizes will be awarded, including $5,800 in scholarship and cash prizes to the champion. The champion will also qualify for the U.S. Girls Junior Championship and either the World Youth Championship or the World Cadet Championships .
The second place finisher in the SC Girls' Scholastic Championship is named the South Carolina Representative to the Susan Polgar Invitational Tournament in St. Louis, MO, and given a stipend for attendance.
This "Hannah 'Tori' Whatley GRIT Award," started by the Whatley family in 2015, honors a young South Carolina female chess player chosen to compete at the Susan Polgar Girls Invitational. Named after Tori Whatley, the first South Carolinian girl to attend in 2008 as a 6th grader, it celebrates her tenacity. She competed six times, a rare feat, and was known for upsetting higher-rated players, like in her debut when she drew a player 518 points above her and beat Virginia’s champion. In 2012, she placed 22nd. Tori joined Webster University’s SPICE program in 2015, the only North American female on the team until 2018. After earning a studio art degree, she worked briefly at the World Chess Hall of Fame and now studies nuclear engineering at Florida International University.
Sponsored by Tori and her dad David, a former scholastic chess coordinator, the award reflects their love for chess and aims to inspire others to pursue their passions.

4/11 - Quad chess tournament G40; d5
Saint Petersburg Chess Club
Saturday, April 11, 2026
Event Overview
There will be no “Byes” or withdrawals allowed. Please complete all your Quad games.
WHAT IS THE QUAD CHESS TOURNAMENT? After all the players have entered, they’re ordered from highest rating to lowest. Unrated players are placed at the low end. The top four players are placed into their own section (a “quad”), then the next four highest in another section, and so on down the list.If two family members are in the same quad, I can move one of them quad up or down.The players in each quad play a round robin, one game against each of the players in their section, for a total of three games each. If there is not an even multiple of four players, the lowest section (usually) will have the few extra players and play a three round Swiss tournament rather than a round robin. The quad format is popular in one day events, and results in players of the most similar playing strengths being paired together for all three rounds. Each group of four chess players is called a Quad.If two family members are at the same Quad,I can move one of them to another Quad.
ADVANTAGES OF QUAD TOURNAMENTS: The advantage of Quad Tournaments, and why players enjoy them so much, is that players of the same strength and experience are able to compete against each other. In addition, the less experienced players are able to win the same "First Place" prizes as their more experienced, stronger counterparts in Quad I and II. You have opportunity your rating to go up faster!!!

REGISTRATION: 10:00-10:45 a.m. If you want to make sure you can play, you need to Pay ahead of time here - https://www.chessregister.com/ .

$35 if paid on Saturday.
USCF membership is required. Please check your USCF ID and renew it if it has expired. If you need me to do it on site add $5 to your bill.

TIME CONTROL: G40; d5
PRIZES: $65 for first place at each Quad or 1st place very big trophy (if two players tied for 1st place $33 each or 1st place big trophy each)
Trophies for 1st to 3rd place for last section!
IMPORTANT NOTICE: Due to space limitation to secure your spot Pay online ahead of time! BRING YOUR CHESS CLOCK!!!

CKQ Saturday Piscataway Rapids
Chess Kings & Queens Academy
Saturday, April 11, 2026
Event Overview
CKQ Saturday Piscataway Rapids
Start time: Players should arrive no later than 4:15 p.m. The first game begins promptly at 4:30. Latecomers risk their clock running when they arrive.
End time: The Under 600 section typically ends by 8:30 p.m., the Under 1200 section more like 9:00. The tournament could go a bit longer if players use all their time.
Players: Most players at this event will be children (ages 6-16), but adults are welcome to play. Beginners are welcome, but at a minimum players should know how to legally move chess pieces, recognize when they’re in check, and how to perform basic checkmates (ex; king and queen vs. king).
Structure / time controls: 4-SS, G30 +5. (Each player will play four games. Each player receives 30 minutes per game, plus another five seconds per move.)
Sections: Under 600 and Under 1200 rating sections. The Under 1200 section requires at least 500 rating to enter. Lower-rated and unrated players may enter with the tournament director's permission.
Requirements: A USCF membership is required to play in the tournament. Contact the tournament director if you need assistance creating or renewing a membership.
Equipment: Players do not need to bring any equipment. Players are recommended to eat before arriving, or at least bring a snack.
Registration: The registration fee is $30. Online registration closes at 5pm on the day of the event.
Byes: If you can’t attend the entire tournament, a half-point bye (limit one) is available for any round. Byes must be requested before the tournaments starts. If you are going to take first-round bye please contact the tournament director at least one hour before the tournament starts.
Prizes: Top three winners in each section receive a trophy or a medal.
For more information: Contact tournament director Stephen Lorimor ( [email protected] , phone/text: 908-286-0720).

Pozez Jewish Community Center of Northern Virginia
Saturday, April 11, 2026
Event Overview
Register at chessacademy.com/tournaments !
This tournament is for scholastic players in grades K-12 with and without prior tournament experience. We recommend that players in their first tournament choose the Unrated option, where they will be grouped by age and play 3 or 4 games.
Players who've previously done well in an Unrated section or have previous rated tournament experience should choose the Rated option, where they'll be placed in a group of 4 players according to their age and rating. Each participant then plays one game against each of the other three players in their group. At the end of the third game, the winner of each group receives a trophy.
This event should typically finish in 1-2 hours, but can potentially take as long as 3 hours for the most advanced players (although that is rare).
Everyone will use a clock! We'll go over how to use clocks on-site, and you can watch this short video to see how they work. Unrated section players will play a game in 10 minutes with a 5 second delay, and Rated games are 25 minutes with a 5 second delay for each player.
Players can play in the morning at 10am, the afternoon at 1pm, or both!
All sections are non-elimination, and all players participate in all rounds
If you're playing in the Rated sections and have a US Chess ID# and membership, please include it. If you don't have one, we will purchase it for you ($24 value!). If you're not sure what your ID# is you can look it up here
Please arrive 15 minutes before games start. Players who arrive after that may not be placed in quads.
Prices increase by $10 at noon the Tuesday before the tournament.

Game 40 Challenge
Phoenix Chess Academy
Saturday, April 11, 2026
Event Overview
4 round Swiss. Time control: Game in 40 minutes with 5 sec delay. Boards, sets, clocks and scoresheets will be provided.
Registration: Go to www.phoenixchessacademy.com. USCF membership is required. New or renewing USCF members are welcome. Highest rating will be used for Swiss pairings and prize purposes.
Sections: Open, Under 1700, Under 1200 & Under 700. No playing up allowed for Open and U1700. Players Under 700 can play in the U1200 Section. Sections will be combined in case a section has less than 4 players registered.
Schedule: Round 1- 9:00 AM, Round 2- 10:30 AM, Round 3- 12:00 PM, Round 4- 1:30 PM. Awards Ceremony will start right after last game is over. Half point Byes are available in all 4 rounds and (Max 2) and must be requested before round 2. Requesting a zero-point Bye late in the tournament is considered the same as withdrawing.
Contact: Liulia Cardona at [email protected] or (602) 402-4985
Prizes: Trophies for top three in each section.
Entry Fee: $30.00 by Wednesday; $35 by Friday; $40 same day. Refund Policy: Full refund will be issued to players who withdraw at least an hour before the first round. In cases where a registered player does not show up for the tournament without prior notice, they will not be eligible for a refund.
A player will automatically forfeit the game if going in the bathroom with a cellphone.
Address: 18440 N. 7th Street Suite 8.
Phoenix , AZ 85022
United States

Reserve: 1st: $50 + Trophy
2nd, Top U1600, Top 65 and Over: Trophy
Novice: 1st: $50 + Trophy

Shippensburg Spring Open 2026
Ceddia Union Building, Room 119
Saturday, April 11, 2026
Event Overview
$485 GUARANTEED PRIZE FUND
Open Section:
1st Place: $140, 2nd Place: $100
Top U1750: $75
U1350 Section:
1st: $80, 2nd: $50
Top U1100: $40
Special Prizes:
Top Unrated: Free Entry to 1-day Central PA or Frederick, MD tournament (top unrated scorer in either section)
Top K-12 Player: Trophy (The scholastic scorer in either section)
Format: 4SS, G/40;+5 (4-round Swiss, Game in 40 minutes with a 5-second bonus per move).
CLOCKS AND SETS PROVIDED. ( Triple-weighted )
This event is part of the 2026 Shippensburg Chess Grand Prix ( Click here to find out more )!
Prizes, time control, and sections are subject to change until Feb. 3rd depending on feedback from the Jan. 31st Shippensburg Winter Open tournament.
Schedule:
Round 1 : 10:30am (tournament starts promptly. We recommend players arrive by 10:15am)
Round 2 : 12:15pm
Lunch Break: 2:00pm (Chick-Fil-A and convenience store across the street)
Round 3: 2:30pm
Round 4: 4:15pm
Prizes given out by 6pm (ASAP)
ENTRY FEE:
Online Registration Page: https://chessnut.club/e/shippensburg-spring-open-2026
U1350 Section Entry Fees (Open to players rated below 1350 and unrated players): Early Bird Discount Entry: $15 if registered by Tuesday, April. 7th
Regular Entry: $20 if registered by 9:30am before the tournament starts
Same-Day Entry: $25 if registering on-site, the day of the tournament. (please arrive before 10:00am if registering the day of)
FOR NEW PLAYERS: Unrated player entry fee is $5 Entry fee is $5 for new players as long as they register by 9:30am the day of). Same-day entries are $25.
Open Section Entry Fees (Open to all, including unrated players): Early Bird Discount Entry: $20 if registered by Tuesday, April. 7th
Regular Entry: $25 if registered by 9:30am before the tournament starts
Same-Day Entry: $30 if registering on-site, the day of the tournament. (please arrive before 10:00am if registering the day of)
FOR NEW PLAYERS: Unrated player entry fee is $5 Entry fee is $5 for new players as long as they register by 9:30am the day of). Same-day entries are $25.
Can't pay electronically but want to register early? You may send checks/cash in the mail. Email tournament director Nathan Zeigler at [email protected] for address. Electronic payment is preferred for advanced registration.
Players may also choose to Paypal [email protected] (friends & family option) or Venmo @nathzeig the entry fee. Please email all the entry information (USCF ID, Name, Section, etc.) to [email protected] if registering this way
Requesting a 1/2-point bye? Email tournament director at [email protected] to put in the request.
UNRATED (New Player) POLICY:
Unrated players are not eligible for the 1st place prize in the U1350 section. The only prize unrated players are eligible for in the U1350 section is the 2nd place prize. Unrated players in the Open section are eligible for the 1st place prize and the 2nd place prize, but not the U1750 prize.
Location Info:
408 Lancaster Dr, Shippensburg, PA 17257
Room 119 in the Ceddia Union Building in Shippensburg University
Free parking: Park in the C-7 parking lot (link to parking map: https://www.ship.edu/globalassets/visit/parkingmap.pdf ) C-7 is the lot opposing Luhrs Performing Arts Center. That will provide a good landmark.
New to Shippensburg?
Click this link to view more info: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1slLL0W9Mz0_qVg_mswh83nYQ0CMvGsSOPRXx62VYVPo/edit?usp=sharing
USCF Membership:
ALL players are required to have a USCF membership to play in the event. Find the rates here: https://new.uschess.org/join-us-chess Don't want to pay for an annual membership? Adults may opt to pay $20 for a 2-month USCF membership as opposed to paying the annual membership.
Questions? Email the tournament director at [email protected] . If you want, we can process your membership for you if you email us about it and you will receive a $3 discount.

Sept. 21, 2024: https://www.uschess.org/msa/XtblMain.php?202409213942-15132283

State Championship Event
San Diego Chess Club
Saturday, April 11, 2026
- Sunday, April 12, 2026
Event Overview
4 Rd Swiss, 4 Sections; Time control is G/100 +30 second increment
1. Open Section: 50 years or older, and rated1800 or better:
1st $600, 2nd $400, 3rd $200, 4th $100

1st $500, 2nd $400, 3rd $200, 4th $100

online at www.scchess.com . SCCF membership is required for all So. Cal.
residents ($25). Onsite Registration: 8:30 to 9:45 AM on Saturday.

events.name: 2026 April Tournament
events.sourceText:
2026 April Tournament
Houston Chess Studio
Sunday, April 12, 2026
Event Overview
Organizer
Azeri Chess Academy LLC ( USCF Affiliate ID A9567106 )
Tournament Director
International Grandmaster and Local TD Ulvi Bajarani ( USCF ID 17112757 )
Tournament Purpose
This tournament is part of the Azeri Chess Academy Houston Circuit 2026.
Date & Time
Round 1 starts on April 12, 2026, at 10:00 AM .
Venue
Houston Chess Studio, 250 Patton Street Suite H Houston, Texas 77009.
Time Control
G/30, d10 (Each player gets 30 minutes with a 10-second delay per move).
Format
6-round Swiss system.
Pairings will be generated using ChessRoster SwissSys 11.75 (subject to updates to more recent versions).
Ratings
This tournament is USCF-rated , and the official April 2026 USCF ratings will be used.
Byes
Up to two (2) half-point byes is allowed and must be declared during registration.
No additional byes are permitted except for 0-point byes .
A 1-point bye is awarded to a player who is left without an opponent when the number of players is odd in a given round.
Entry Fee
$60 – Until March 15, 2026, or for the first 10 players, whichever comes first.
$80 – Until April 1, 2026, or for the next 20 players, whichever comes first.
$100 – Until April 12, 2026 at 12:00 AM (midnight), or until all spots are filled.
Cancellation & Refund Policy
A 50% refund will be granted if a player requests cancellation by April 8, 2026, at 12:00 AM (midnight) .
No refunds will be issued after this deadline.
Withdrawal Policy
Players must notify an arbiter before the start of a round if they intend to withdraw.
Failure to notify an arbiter may affect eligibility for future tournaments organized by Azeri Chess Academy LLC.
Number of Entries
Maximum of 64 participants.
Eligibility
Open to all players with active USCF membership .
Players must ensure their USCF membership is active before the start of Round 1.
Onsite check-ins may be available for players needing USCF membership renewal. They must pay the required renewal fee plus an additional $10 processing fee.
Failure to renew an expired membership before the tournament will result in exclusion without a refund .
Tournament Schedule (Estimated Round Start Times)
1st Round – 10:00 AM
2nd Round – 11:25 AM
30-minute break
3rd Round – 1:20 PM
4th Round – 2:45 PM
5th Round – 4:05 PM
6th Round – 5:25 PM
Closing Ceremony – 6:45 PM
Prize Fund
Prize distribution is based on the final number of players in the tournament:
< 10 players
1st: $300 + plaque
Total prize fund: $300
10–15 players
1st: $400 + plaque
2nd: $100
Total prize fund: $500
16–20 players
1st: $500 + plaque
2nd: $250
Total prize fund: $750
21–25 players
1st: $500 + plaque
2nd: $250
3rd: $150
Total prize fund: $900
26–30 players
1st: $500 + plaque
2nd: $250
3rd: $150
Best U1600: $150
Best U1200: $150
Total prize fund: $1,200
31–35 players
1st: $500 + plaque
2nd: $250
3rd: $150
Best U1600: $150
Best U1200: $150
Best U800: $150
Total prize fund: $1,350
36–40 players
1st: $550 + plaque
2nd: $350
3rd: $150
Best U1600: $150
Best U1400: $150
Best U1200: $150
Best U1000: $150
Best U800: $150
Total prize fund: $1,800
41–45 players
1st: $590 + plaque
2nd: $350
3rd: $210
Best U1600: $200
Best U1400: $200
Best U1200: $150

Best U800: $150
Total prize fund: $2,000
46–50 players

2nd: $410

Best U800: $200

> 50 players

Best U800: $300
Total prize fund: $2,800
If rating prizes are offered, unrated players are eligible only for prizes in the lowest rating group . This does not affect their eligibility for the overall (main) prizes.
Prizes are equally shared in case of a tie .
Payments will be sent via Zelle/PayPal before April 19, 2026. Prize-winners must contact the organizer immediately after the final round to confirm their preferred payment method. Additionally, the prize winners are required to participate in the prize ceremony following the tournament. Failure to complete these actions will result in disqualification from receiving the prize.
Tiebreaks
Tiebreaks will be determined using ChessRoster SwissSys , applying standard USCF tiebreak methods :
Solkoff
Modified Median
Cumulative
If players are tied for 1st place and all tiebreaks are equal , a coin toss will determine the winner.
Anti-Cheating Measures & Electronic Devices Policy
All players are subject to electronic device scanning (“wanding”) .
No electronic devices (phones, smartwatches, etc.) are allowed unless explicitly permitted by the arbiter for medical reasons .
A designated storage box will be provided for electronic devices.
Photography & Video Recording
By registering, players consent to being photographed and recorded by the Tournament Director and their associates for promotional purposes.
Equipment & Notation Rules
Chess sets, clocks, scoresheets, and pens will be provided by the organizer.
Notation is mandatory unless a player has less than 5 minutes remaining on their clock.
Players may keep a yellow scoresheet copy and a pen . However, players are encouraged to bring an extra pen , as available pens may be limited .
Parking & Nearby Restaurants:
Free parking is available near the venue.
3 restaurants in the same strip center as venue: The Red Hot Noodle (Asian), Subway , and Patron Pizza . Several others are within walking distance.

Scholastic Quads (Groups of 4 based on rating)
Hampton Inn and Suites Dulles
22700 Holiday Park Drive
April 12 at 3:30 pm
***This is a side event for the Dulles International Scholastic Championship. To register or find out more information about the quads, visit the main Dulles International registration page: https://caissachess.net/online-registration/index/8465
Additional info
At 3:30 pm on April 12, in addition to the Dulles International Scholastic happening earlier, we also have a scholastic quads tournament. Players may choose to play in just the championship at 10 am, play only the quads at 3:30 pm, or play both events. Players who play in both events will receive a discounted entry into the quads. If playing both events, the quads will only be $20, regardless of registration date. Otherwise the entry fee for the quads is $30 by 3/26, $35 by 4/3, $40 by 4/11, $45 on 4/12.
A quad is a four-person round robin section in which all participants play each other once (three rounds). Our quads are open to all scholastic players in grades K-12, and each quad will be divided based on rating rather than grade. The advantage of quads is that players get the chance to compete against opponents with close USCF ratings. The tournament director has discretion when determining quad seeding (for example, the TD may use a player's unpublished rating). Depending on the exact number of registrations, the bottom section may have five, six, or seven players, in which case that section will be paired as a Swiss tournament.
To register or find out more information about the quads, visit the main Dulles International registration page: https://caissachess.net/online-registration/index/8465

events.name: SCHOLASTIC SUNDAY by Indy Chess
events.sourceText:
SCHOLASTIC SUNDAY by Indy Chess
St. Monica Catholic School Gym (Door 15)
Sunday, April 12, 2026
Event Overview
REGISTER FOR THIS TOURNAMENT HERE: https://www.indychess.org/events
Kids who have learned how the pieces move and some basic strategy are welcome to enter the world of rated chess tournaments! All school-aged kids from kindergarten to 12th grade are welcome. Walk-ins are discouraged, as we would appreciate all registering online in advance. The chess playing room is a silent atmosphere to enable maximum concentration.
For the "rated" tournament, all players MUST be members of the US Chess Federation ($24/year). Before registering for the rated event, become a member of USCF here (you will need to write down your child's USCF ID#). However, being a member of Indy Chess--our local club--at $50/year/student or $75/year/family is optional. If interested, you can do that here to get a $5 discount on this event and every other one you attend this year with us, including Weekly Tuesdays, and support the growth of chess in Indy!
[If a beginner and wanting to play in the "casual" tournament (unrated, does not require USCF membership), that is explained far below.]
Here are the details:
Check-in on site: 1:45-2:00pm, entering the door up a few exterior stairs/ramp (not the street-level door). Games start right after a player meeting at 2:15pm.
4ss: Four rounds in a "Swiss" system. A Swiss tournament--the most common chess form--means every player plays every round, with future rounds pairing those who won and those who lost. Up to two 1/2-point byes can be requested by emailing [email protected] or telling the tournament director at the event which rounds you would like byes. Note: Premiere section is 3 rounds.
G/25+5: Games are 25 minutes on each players clock, plus 5 seconds added to a player's time when they hit the clock every move.
USCF-rated: All players must be members of the US Chess Federation and provide a member ID# in online registration. This will give each child a "rating" in chess that will follow them with each tournament they play. Ratings are in blitz, quick, and regular play, and the 25+5 time control affects their regular and their quick rating.
Entry fee is $20/kid, or $15 for members of Indy Chess.
Kids rated under 1000 are divided into three sections so kids play only those in their age group (e.g., 3rd Grade & Under, 6th Grade & Under, and 12th Grade & Under). Want your child to "play up?" Just email Mike at [email protected] . Notation is optional but encouraged in these sections.
There is one "Premiere" section for kids rated 1000 or above (published rating from the 1st of the month). Notation is required in the premiere sections. The Premiere section is three rounds, and may be split by rating at TD discretion to achieve less than eight players per section.
Casual Tournament:
Alongside the rated tournament, kids can instead register for a casual tournament (i.e., unrated) which will begin at the same time. The games will be optionally clocked, notation is not required, and the tournament director will determine section splits based on turnout. It will be a Swiss tournament (i.e., all players play all rounds, unless someone gets a bye due to an odd number). There will be four rounds. There are trophies for the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd place winners!
Other details:
Children under 12 years old must have an adult present and responsible for them, unless the parent/guardian has the permission of the tournament director.
Concessions are typically available for sale by St. Monica, including hot food (less likely in summer months).
An outside playground is available.
Parents may watch chess silently from the bleachers in the gym, or sit at tables in the cafeteria. There is a guest WiFi network with password August27.
The site is wheelchair accessible.
Parking is free in the school lot (Door 15 is located near the southeast side of the building), but is sometimes full right at 1:45p due to a church function. Parking on a nearby street for overflow is available.
Chess sets, clocks, and notation sheets are provided for up to 60 kids. If the child has played in a tournament or two prior, it is helpful if they bring a regulation set and/or clock to ensure there are enough.
Trophies are provided to the top five finishers in each of the three lower sections. In the premiere section, a $50 Amazon gift card goes to the winner (decided by 5+0 blitz playoff if need be, Black/White randomly chosen). Biggest upset earns a medal (unrated does not qualify).
Players who notate at least one game get to pick a prize from the bin at the end of the tournament! Learn how to notate chess moves here (YouTube link).
Questions? Email Mike at [email protected] . We hope to see you there!

Bill Wright Saint Louis Open 2026
Grand Prix
Saint Louis Chess Club
Friday, April 17, 2026
- Sunday, April 19, 2026
Event Overview
Name: Bill Wright Saint Louis Open 2026
Location: Saint Louis Chess Club - 4663 Maryland Avenue, St. Louis MO 63108
Dates: Friday, April 17th - Sunday, April 19th, 2026
Event Overview
- Event Information
5-round Three-day Swiss Open
Held at the Saint Louis Chess Club
Rounds: 1st Round - Friday 6:30 PM; 2nd Round - Saturday 10:00 AM; 3rd Round - Saturday 3:00 PM; 4th Round - Sunday 10:00 AM; 5th Round - Sunday 3:00 PM
Time Control: G/90 + 30 second increment from move one
Sections: Premiere (Open); Reserve (U2000)
- Prize Information
$7,500 Unconditionally Guaranteed!!
Premiere Section - Open (US Chess Rated) - 1st - $1750; 2nd - $800; 3rd - $650; 4th - $500; U2200 - 1st - $575; 2nd - $350
Reserve Section - U2000 (US Chess Rated) - 1st - $750; 2nd - $550; 3rd - $425; 4th - $300; U1600 - 1st - $275; 2nd - $200; U1200 - 1st $175; 2nd - Tournament Entry Voucher*; Top Unrated - Tournament Entry Voucher*
Overall Winner will be declared 2026 Saint Louis Champion.
*Tournament Entry Voucher entitles the player to one free entry into another open tournament at the Saint Louis Chess Club in 2026.
Entry Information
Entry Fee: $100
Must be registered by Friday, 4/17/2026 @4:00 Central Time
No on-site registration, register online as space is limited
Free entry for GMs and IMs
Other Notes
Two 1/2 points byes available; must be declared before the start of Round 1.
USCF ratings will be used for prize purposes in all sections
TD has discretion to appoint ratings
Hotel Rate available at Chase Park Plaza and AC Hotel (Ask for Chess Club Rate)
Register Now! https://register.stlchess.club/bill-wright-saint-louis-open-2026

events.name: 2025-26 CalChess Super States: K-3 & K-8 Championship and K-12 Sections
events.sourceText:
2025-26 CalChess Super States: K-3 & K-8 Championship and K-12 Sections
Sonesta Silicon Valley Event Center
Saturday, April 18, 2026
- Sunday, April 19, 2026
Event Overview
Compete in the 2025-26 CalChess Super States K-3 & K-8 Championship and other K-12 sections, where scholastic players enjoy exciting games at a state-level championship! It's the perfect opportunity to gain experience and earn trophies.
Register here
You must log in or sign up before you can register.
Online registration closes at 12:00 a.m. the day of the tournament.
Onsite registration is subject to availability ($44 additional fee incurred).
Late fees applied starting April 12 or when reaching capacity.
Sections
Players will need to register based on their 2025-26 school grade and their April Supplement Rating (i.e., rating as of Mar. 19) into one of the following sections: K-12 Rookie (unr.)
K-12 Beginner (100-399)
K-3 Jr. Varsity (400-799)
4-12 Intermediate (400-799)
K-12 Intermediate (400-799)
4-12 Advanced (800-1199)
K-12 Advanced (800-1199)
K-8 Jr. Varsity (800-1199)
K-3 Champ (800+)
K-8 Champ (1200+)
9-12 Advanced (1200+)
Play-up rule
A player may pay to play up one higher section, double play up is NOT allowed.
Players must be within 300 points of the rating cutoff to play up.
(Note: The rating used to determine if a player may play up is their April USChess Published Supplement Rating)
Schedule
K-12 Rookie & K-12 Beginner : Time Control: 5x G/25 d5
Two schedules available: Saturday OR Sunday
Round Times: Sat, Apr. 18 - 9:00 a.m., 10:40 a.m., 12:20 p.m., 2:00 p.m., 3:40 p.m.
OR
Sun, Apr. 19 - 9:00 a.m., 10:40 a.m., 12:20 p.m., 2:00 p.m., 3:40 p.m.
K-3 Jr. Varsity , 4-12 Intermediate & K-12 Advanced : Time Control: 5x G/25 d5
Round Times: Sat, Apr. 18 - 9:00 a.m., 10:40 a.m., 12:20 p.m., 2:00 p.m., 3:40 p.m.
K-3 Champ , K-12 Intermediate & 4-12 Advanced : Time Control: 5x G/25 d5
Round Times: Sun, Apr. 19 - 9:00 a.m., 10:40 a.m., 12:20 p.m., 2:00 p.m., 3:40 p.m.
K-8 Jr. Varsity , K-8 Champ & 9-12 Advanced : Time Control: 6x G/65 d5
Round Times: Sat, Apr. 18 - 9:00 a.m., 12:00 p.m., 2:50 p.m.
Sun, Apr. 19 - 9:00 a.m., 12:00 p.m., 2:50 p.m.
½-point bye is available for ONE (1) round, except for the last round (Byes must be requested at least 30 min before that round's start).
0-point byes are available for any round.
If you request more than one bye, we will give you a ½-point for the latest round possible except for the last round (0-point byes for all other rounds).
Awards
Personal Trophies to all players with a winning record. One trophy per player.
Trophy size vary based on standings.
Medals to all other players.
Team Trophies to all of the following with two or more players in all sections combined: Clubs
Schools
A player who withdraws during the tournament is not eligible for awards.
Fees
Entry fee: K-8 Jr. Varsity, K-8 Champ and 9-12 Advanced: $113
All other sections: $79
Play up fee: +$29
Discount for BayAreaChess Membership Subscribers ( More info ).
Late fees, starting: Apr. 12: +$11
Apr. 14: +$22
Apr. 16: +$33
Onsite fee: +$44
BayAreaChess Membership discounts are NOT redeemable for late and onsite fees.
Withdrawals
Withdrawals are eligible for a partial refund, subject to the following deductions: until Apr. 11, 4% processing fee.
from Apr. 12 to Mar. 13, $11 withdrawal fee + 4% processing fee.
from Apr. 14 to Mar. 15, $22 withdrawal fee + 4% processing fee.
from Apr. 16 onward, NO REFUND will be issued.
Only withdrawals made before or on Apr. 15 are eligible for refund.
Change requests
After registration, changes can be requested at bayareachess.com/changeform and are subject to the following fees: until Apr. 16, $7 change fee.
on Apr. 17, $15 change fee.
The following requests are exempt from the change fee: playing up to a higher section.
requesting byes.
updating club and/or school.
Other requirements
USCF membership must be active.
More info available here .

2026 Maryland State Scholastic Championships
State Championship Event
Hammond High School
Saturday, April 18, 2026
- Sunday, April 19, 2026
Event Overview
Register at chessacademy.com/tournaments !
The official Maryland State Scholastic Championship tournament and Denker, Barber, Rockefeller, and Ashley Qualifiers!
With special guest IM Danny Rensch, who will be doing a lecture and book signing of his memoir Dark Squares at 11am on Saturday
This is a US Chess rated Swiss style tournament. There are ten different sections for players depending on their age and skill. Sections include K-1 U-400, PS U-600, ES U-800, MS U-1000, HS U-1200, K-1 Champ, PS Champ (550+), ES Champ (750+), MS Champ (950+), and HS Champ (1150+). Participants play only against opponents in their own section. Under sections for elementary school, K-1 Champ, and PS Champ will play all their games on Saturday. Under sections for middle and high school will play all their games on Sunday. ES Champ, MS Champ, and HS Champ will play their games on Saturday and Sunday.
Championship sections are only open to students who live in or attend school in MD, under sections are open to participants from any state.
All sections are non-elimination, and all players participate in all five rounds.
We provide FREE US Chess Federation memberships for all participants, a $24 value!
For players using chess clocks, the time control is G/25 with a 5-second time delay. For ES, MS, and HS championship sections, the time control is G/75 d5.
Trophies to the top players and teams in each section.
Prices increase $10 at noon on Tuesday, 3/31 and $10 at noon on Tuesday, 4/14.
Questions? Please let us know at Click here to show mail address !

4/18 - ST. PETERSBURG EXTRA QUAD CHESS TOURNAMENT G60; d5.
Saint Petersburg Chess Club
Saturday, April 18, 2026
Event Overview
There will be no “Byes” or withdrawals allowed. Please complete all your Quad games.
WHAT IS THE QUAD CHESS TOURNAMENT? After all the players have entered, they’re ordered from highest rating to lowest. Unrated players are placed at the low end. The top four players are placed into their own section (a “quad”), then the next four highest in another section, and so on down the list. The players in each quad play a round robin, one game against each of the players in their section, for a total of three games each. If there is not an even multiple of four players, the lowest section (usually) will have the few extra players and play a three round Swiss tournament rather than a round robin. The quad format is popular in one day events, and results in players of the most similar playing strengths being paired together for all three rounds. A Quad Tournament consists of the top four ranked players (#s 1-4) on the Chess Ladder playing each other, then the second top four ranked players (#s 5-8) playing each other, then the third top four ranked players (#s 9-12) playing each other, and so forth. Each group of four chess players is called a Quad.If two family members are at the same Quad,I can move one of them to another Quad.
ADVANTAGES OF QUAD TOURNAMENTS: The advantage of Quad Tournaments, and why players enjoy them so much, is that players of the same strength and experience are able to compete against each other. In addition, the less experienced players are able to win the same "First Place" prizes as their more experienced, stronger counterparts in Quad I and II. You have opportunity your rating to go up faster!!!
LOCATION : Saint Petersburg Chess Club 540 4th Avenue North Saint Petersburg, FL 33701 (it is located in between Mirror Lake and the Coliseum, next to the Sunshine Center.)
REGISTRATION : 10:00-10:45 a.m. If you want to make sure you can play, you need to Pay ahead of time here - https://home.chessregister.com/
ENTRY FEE:
$25 if paid by Wednesday (3 days before the tournament)
$30 afterward
$35 if paid on Saturday
USCF membership is required. Please check your USCF ID and renew it if it has expired. If you need me to do it on site add $5 to your bill.
ROUNDS: Three Rounds, First starts at approx. 11:00 a.m.
TIME CONTROL: G60; d5
PRIZES : $65 for first place at each Quad or very big trophies for 1st place (if two players tied for 1st place $33 each, or chess trophies for 1st place for both of them)
Trophies for 1st to 3rd place for the last section!
IMPORTANT NOTICE : Due to space limitation to secure your spot Pay online ahead of time! BRING YOUR CHESS CLOCK!!!
Visit our website- https://saintpetersburgchessclub.com/ for more information about chess at Saint Petersbug.
Join our Facebook groups Saint Petersburg Chess Tournaments - https://www.facebook.com/groups/385692191510406/
