CKQ Saturday Piscataway Rapids
Chess Kings & Queens Academy
Saturday, April 18, 2026
Event Overview
CKQ Saturday Piscataway Rapids
Start time: Players should arrive no later than 4:15 p.m. The first game begins promptly at 4:30. Latecomers risk their clock running when they arrive.
End time: The Under 600 section typically ends by 8:30 p.m., the Under 1200 section more like 9:00. The tournament could go a bit longer if players use all their time.
Players: Most players at this event will be children (ages 6-16), but adults are welcome to play. Beginners are welcome, but at a minimum players should know how to legally move chess pieces, recognize when they’re in check, and how to perform basic checkmates (ex; king and queen vs. king).
Structure / time controls: 4-SS, G30 +5. (Each player will play four games. Each player receives 30 minutes per game, plus another five seconds per move.)
Sections: Under 600 and Under 1200 rating sections. The Under 1200 section requires at least 500 rating to enter. Lower-rated and unrated players may enter with the tournament director's permission.
Requirements: A USCF membership is required to play in the tournament. Contact the tournament director if you need assistance creating or renewing a membership.
Equipment: Players do not need to bring any equipment. Players are recommended to eat before arriving, or at least bring a snack.
Registration: The registration fee is $30. Online registration closes at 5pm on the day of the event.
Byes: If you can’t attend the entire tournament, a half-point bye (limit one) is available for any round. Byes must be requested before the tournaments starts. If you are going to take first-round bye please contact the tournament director at least one hour before the tournament starts.
Prizes: Top three winners in each section receive a trophy or a medal.
For more information: Contact tournament director Stephen Lorimor ( [email protected] , phone/text: 908-286-0720).

events.sourceText:
ICA FIDE Championship
Grand Prix
Community Church of Glen Rock Education Building
Saturday, April 18, 2026
- Sunday, April 19, 2026
Event Overview
This is a two-day dual FIDE and USCF-rated tournament.
Registration Fee: $120. Early bird! Register by April 11, 11:59 pm for just $100.
Free entry to GMs, IMs, and 2400+ FIDE rated players. Email Click here to show mail address for a coupon for free entry.
For full refund, canceled registrations must be requested by e-mail by 11:59 pm the night before the tournament.
Format: 4 round Swiss-System (two rounds per day). G110 d10. Pairings based on FIDE ratings.
Minimum rating: A monthly published rating of 1600 USCF or 1500 FIDE
All players must have a valid FIDE ID. Players may request a USA-flagged FIDE ID at this URL: https://tinyurl.com/nebafd36 . Players wishing a non-USA flagged FIDE ID must contact the relevant country’s chess federation.
Schedule: Saturday 11:00 am, 3:30 pm. Sunday 1:00 pm, 5:30 pm.
Prizes: Prize distribution will follow standard USCF rules.
1st - $500
2nd - $360
3rd - $240
Under 2200 (FIDE) - $180
Under 2000 (FIDE) - $180
Under 1800 (FIDE) - $180
Under age 13 - $180
Over age 55 - $180
Byes: Two half-point byes available for any round. Half-point byes must be requested before the start of round two. Byes must be requested 15 minutes before the start of each round.
Online registration: Closes at 10:00 am on the first day of the tournament
Online registration link: https://ica.jumbula.com/ICATournaments2026/ICAFIDEChampionshipApril18April19
On-site registration is open from 10:00 am to 10:30 on the day of the tournament.
Equipment: All participants must bring clocks.
Norms: FIDE norms are not available at this event.
Late arrivals: Late arrivals will be handled as per USCF rules
Parents and caregivers: There is waiting space for parents and caregivers where they can keep an eye on young players.
Parking: Please enter via parking lot entrance on Hamilton Avenue. After parking, please enter through the door that has an “International Chess Academy” sign then proceed to the second floor.
By train: Glen Rock has two NJ Transit stations within easy walking distance of ICA: Glen Rock - Main Line and Glen Rock - Boro Hall.
By bus: Take 164, 164B, 164E, or 175B to Rock Road at Central Avenue. All stop directly in front of ICA.
Address: 354 Rock Road
Glen Rock , NJ 07452
United States

PA Senior Championship - Irwin Qualifier
State Championship Event
Tri-Bridges Chess Club
Saturday, April 18, 2026
- Sunday, April 19, 2026
Event Overview
This event is the official Pennsylvania Senior Open. You must be 50 or older to play as of 8/3/25 (when the Irwin tournament starts all participants must be 50 or over.) You may be from any state. However, to represent Pennsylvania in the Irwin Championship at the U. S. Open, you must be a citizen of Pennsylvania.
One section – G/90 d5. Round Times: Saturday – 10 – 1:30 – 5; Sunday 9:30 – 1
Prizes: Irwin representative for top Pennsylvanian; 1st Overall – $200, 2nd Overall – $100; Top Under 2000 – $90; Top Under 1800 – $80; Top Under 1600 – $70; Top Under 1400 – $60; Top Under 1200 – $50; Top Under 1000 – $50;
Entry Fee: $30
Please note that there are stairs to both playing areas. If this is a problem, I can arrange to use a room on the main floor (there are still two steps to get into the building), but it would be helpful to know beforehand. Coffee/tea/water is available. Fast food/sit-down restaurants/convenience stores are within a few minutes’ commute. Two or three hotels are about 5 minutes away, and many are within about 20 minutes. There will also be a small selection of chess literature for sale.
One half-point bye allowed; must declare by the start of round 2.
When signing up, click blue registration button, fill out form, don’t worry if there is no grade, etc. (we do many kid events, but you can just ignore those blanks), click submit, and then reload page to see if you want to double check that you have signed up.
Please note that we have moved into April as the first weekend in March is the State Scholastic and the Ira Lee Riddle State Championship.
You may register on site between 8:30 and 9:30. The entry fee for registering on site is $50.

Phoenix Saturday Action
Phoenix Chess Academy
Saturday, April 18, 2026
Event Overview
4 round Swiss. Time control: Game in 25 minutes with 5 sec delay. Boards, sets, clocks and scoresheets will be provided.
Registration: Go to www.phoenixchessacademy.com. USCF membership is required. New or renewing USCF members are welcome. Highest rating will be used for Swiss pairings and prize purposes.
Sections: Open, Under 1700 & Under 1200 (No playing up allowed). Sections will be combined in case a section has less than 4 players registered.
Schedule: Round 1- 9:00 AM, Round 2- 10:05 AM, Round 3- 11:10 AM, Round 4- 12:15 PM. Awards Ceremony will start right after last game is over. Half point Byes are available in all 4 rounds and (Max 2) and must be requested before round 2. Requesting a zero-point bye late in the tournament is considered the same as withdrawing.
Entry Fee: $25.00 by 04/15; $30 by 04/17; $35 same day. Full refund will be issued to players who withdraw at least an hour before the first round. In cases where a registered player does not show up for the tournament without prior notice, they will not be eligible for a refund.
Prizes: Trophies for top three in each section.
A player will automatically forfeit the game if going in the bathroom with a cellphone.

Columbia Chess Club
6169 St. Andrews Rd.
Columbia, SC 29212
Register
Registration
Standard registration is $40 until the day before the tournament. $50 late registration the day before/morning of. Registration online only, registration limited to first 74 players.
Entry for titled players (National Master and above) is free, standard entry fee deducted from prizes. If you are a titled player, simply use the "Titled Player" option at checkout.
Considering Tunnelvision as your first chess tournament? Great! We've put together a guide to help first-time players .
Register Now
Pre-Registered Players
Format
4 Round Swiss. Time control is G45/inc.5 (45 minutes starting time with a 5-second increment ), which will be USCF dual-rated under both Quick and Classical. All equipment provided. USCF Rules Apply, active USCF Membership required. Tournament has three sections: Championship (1600+), Under 1600, and Under 1000. Players may register for a higher section if they are within 100 USCF rating points of the cutoff.
If you need to renew or obtain a USCF membership, please visit https://new.uschess.org/join-us-chess.
Live Standings/Pairings/Boards
The top board of each section will be live streamed to the DGT LiveCloud along with real-time updates to Lichess.org and Chess.com. A live video stream of the top Championship board will also be available on the club's Twitch page. See this site's "Live" menu for links.
Live standings (including current pre-registration information) and pairings are also available below.
Live Standings
Prizes
$1000 Prize Fund Guaranteed.
Championship (1600+)
$400 Fund. 1st: $200; 2nd: $130; 3rd: $70
Under 1600
$300 Fund: 1st: $150; 2nd: $100; 3rd: $50
Under 1000
$300 Fund: 1st: $150; 2nd: $100; 3rd: $50
Schedule
Round 1: 10:30 a.m.
Round 2: 12:50 p.m.
Round 3: 2:40 p.m.
Round 4: 4:30 p.m.
Byes
A single half-point bye is available any round, including the final round. The half-point bye may be requested as a part of the advance entry or on site before the tournament starts. Thereafter the only bye available is a zero-point bye. The chief tournament director shall have the ability to grant a half-point bye for any round on unusual circumstances.

Email [email protected] or call/text James Brandmair at 803.569.0938.
Parking
The Columbia Chess Club is located in a shopping center with ample parking.

The Columbia Chess Club offers on-site concessions, including drinks and snacks. By the Fire Pizza and Zorba's Restaurant are located in the same shopping center and will be open during the tournament. Many other restaurants are available close by!

2026 Tulane Classic
Tulane University
Friday, April 24, 2026
- Sunday, April 26, 2026
Event Overview
The Tulane Chess Club and Downriver Chess invite you to a two-day classical event with $2,100 in prizes!
Venue: The Qatar Ballroom, on the second floor of the Lavin-Bernick Center at Tulane University. 29 McAlister Drive, New Orleans, LA.
Tournament details: Five round, two-section, swiss system, G/60;i30, USCF rated tournament. Top section FIDE-rated.
Sections: Two, open and U1500.
Prize fund: $2,100 in prizes. Total prize fund b/60 with 50% guaranteed.
Class prizes: Class prizes to be determined by official April USCF rating. Unrated players are eligible for class and section prizes in the open section.
Prize Structure:
Open section: 1st $600, 2nd $300
U2000 class: 1st $300, 2nd $150
U1500 section: 1st $300, 2nd $150
U1200 class: 1st $200, 2nd $100
Date: April 24-26, 2026. Estimated round schedule,
Friday 7:00 PM Blitz side event
Saturday 10:00 AM, 2:00 PM, 5:30 PM
Sunday 10:00 AM, 2:00 PM
Blitz side event: $25 entry, 60% returned as prize money. 7 PM Friday evening. USCF-rated. Six rounds of G/5;d2. Register by clicking here . Walk in registration allowed.
Eligibility: $60 early entry fee if purchased one week prior. $70 standard entry fee if purchased two days prior. $80 late and same-day entry fee. Capacity limited to the first 120 players, please pre-register to guarantee your spot. Current USCF membership required. Free FIDE membership available to all players in top section with valid USCF membership.
Ratings: If a player does not have a regular rating, the highest of their quick and blitz will be used. 100 elo added to provisional ratings. Unrated players should report to the tournament directors so they may attempt to assign a rating for pairing and prize purposes. Unrated players may play in the open section or the U1500 section, but will only be eligible for the open section place prizes unless the tournament directors have been able to assign a rating. For unrated USCF players with established foreign ratings, the most current USCF conversion will be used (with preference toward their FIDE rating, if available). Games including FIDE rated players 2400 or above are not FIDE rated due to time control and format.
Byes: Two half point byes are available upon request. No bye requests shall be made after round three other than for emergency situations.
Parking: Parking permits are not required in most parking zones on Tulane University campus during the weekend. For ease, we recommend using the Diboll Garage. Diboll Garage is a short walk from the Lavin-Bernick Center and has plenty of space available for our attendees. Consult the annotated parking map here .
Hotel info: We recommend the St Charles Inn - Superior Hotel. We do not have a group rate, however.
Late players: Any player arriving at the chessboard more than 30 minutes late from the actual starting time of the round will lose their game (xref USCF 13D and FIDE 6.7.1). If both players arrive late elapsed time will be split between the players (xref USCF 16K and FIDE 6.7.2).
Prize payouts: Players have 10 days after the conclusion of the tournament to claim their prize. We will email you twice. Please check your email if you believe you are prize eligible.
Contact: Email Click here to show mail address with all questions.
Refunds: Players who withdraw 60 minutes before round one are eligible for a refund of their entry fee, minus any applicable payment-processor fees (typically 5-7%).
Tulane students: Please contact the Tulane Chess Club for discounted entry.
Visit: www.downriverchess.com for all other upcoming tournaments!

2026 TEXAS QUICK CHESS STATE CHAMPIONSHIP
State Championship Event
THE HOUSTON CHESS STUDIO
Saturday, April 25, 2026
Event Overview
2026 TEXAS QUICK CHESS STATE CHAMPIONSHIP
A TCA GRAND PRIX EVENT!
Registration: https://www.kingregistration.com/event/2026QuickChessChamp
9 rounds of G/15 (no delay no increment) on Saturday April 25th. One section. USCF rated for Quick Chess only. This tournament will not affect your regular rating. Keeping score (notation) is not required in Quick Chess!
QUALIFICATIONS : All chess players, regardless of residence, are welcome as long as they meet the membership requirements. You must have an unexpired USCF and Texas Chess Association membership in good standing on the day of the tournament . Please note, however, that while residents of other states may participate, and win cash prizes, state champion titles are for Texas residents only .
BYES : Every player is entitled to a single half-point bye if requested before the beginning of round 1. After that time, all requested byes will be for zero points. All last round byes are zero point byes.
SECTIONS: Just one open section. The April Rating Supplement will be used for pairings and for determination of the Class State Championship certificates.
SCHEDULE : Round 1 at 10am, others ASAP, one hour lunch break from about noon to 1. Last round should end about 4 or 4:30.
CAPACITY: Limited to 72, so register early, it might sell out. It is a State Championship event after all.
ENTRY FEES : $45 by April 4th, $55 by April 22nd, $65 thereafter. Poison Pawn members use your $10 off coupon. GM's & IMs enter free, entry fee deducted from any prize won.
CANCELLATION : You may cancel up to 24 hours before the beginning of round 1 and get a refund of what you paid minus $15, or you may apply the entire amount towards a future entry fee.
PRIZES : Overall 1st place - the title of "2026 Texas Quick Chess State Champion", a trophy, and $250 guaranteed . Overall 2nd place $175, and overall 3rd place $100. 2nd & 3rd place based on 25 paid entries. All 3 cash prizes increased proportionally with more than 25 entries. (last year's prize fund was $380/$270/$160 with 49 entries). All cash prizes paid via PayPal. In case of a tie for first place the trophy will be awarded using standard USCF tiebreakers: Modified Median, Solkoff, Cumulative, Cumulative Opponent's score. HOWEVER, the others who tie for first will get certificates designating them "2025 Texas Quick Chess State Co-Champion".
ALSO, CLASS STATE CHAMPIONSHIP CERTIFICATES AWARDED TO TOP SCORE IN CLASS A (1999-1800), CLASS B (1799-1600), C (1599-1400), D (1399-1200), & E (1199 & lower). No tie breaks , if 2 or more tie for top score in a class they will each get a certificate declaring them the "2026 Texas Quick Chess State Co-Champion" of that Class!
CLOCKS, SETS & BOARDS: Please bring your own if you can, there might be enough equipment at The Studio but depending on the turnout there might not be, and Poison Pawns club members get first dibs on those. Know how to set your clock to G/15!!
HOTEL INFO : Holiday Inn Express , 3401 N. Main St., is less than a mile from The Studio. Phone 832-834-6197 and ask for The Houston Chess Studio discount, or if booking online use code ALDR9. Also within a mile is the Heights House Hotel , an America’s Best Value , and a Luxury Inn . Google them for info.
WHERE: THE HOUSTON CHESS STUDIO , is dedicated to providing a quality, high tech, chess playing experience for players of all levels, and their parents. Centrally and conveniently located at 250 Patton St., Suite H, Houston TX 77009. Just inside North Loop 610 and just 2 blocks off North I-45. There are 3 restaurants in the same strip center as The Studio: The Red Hot Noodle (Asian), Subway, and Patron Pizza. Several others are within walking distance. Plenty of FREE parking.
SCANNING: All players are subject to being scanned (“wanded”) in order to help prevent cheating.
UPCOMING EVENTS: https://www.kingregistration.com/affiliate/poisonpawns

events.name: Arizona Golden Cup 🏆
events.sourceText:
Arizona Golden Cup 🏆
Phoenix Chess Academy
Saturday, April 25, 2026
Event Overview
Arizona's Premier Year - Long USCF Chess Series.
Earn Points. Win Gold. Become a Champion. 🏆
A year-long USCF-rated chess series. Players earn Golden Points at each monthly event. Final standings after December determine the Arizona Golden Cup Champion, 2nd and 3rd Place in each section. Players may enter the series at any time during the year. Tournament is open to everyone. USCF membership is required.
4 Round Swiss G/30; d5 USCF-rated tournament series with cumulative points.
Sections: Open (1800 +). Under 1800. Under 1200. No playing up allowed. Official rating will be used for sections and prizes. Half point Byes available in all 4 rounds (Max 2) and must be requested before round 2. If a player moves to a higher section during the year, points earned in the previous section do not transfer. The player begins earning Golden Cup points in the new section.
Schedule: Round 1: 9:00 AM. Round 2: 10:15 AM. Round 3: 11:30 AM. Round 4: 12:45 PM. Ceremony will follow right after last game is over.
Entry Fee: $35.00 by Wednesday, $40.00 by Friday, $45.00 Same Day. Refund Policy: Full refund if canceling up to 1 hour before the event. No refund after that.
Awards: Top 3 Trophy in each section, Best U1400 and Best U800 in each monthly event.
At the end of the series-After December event: Champion Trophy (in each section) + 7 Months of Free entry for 2027 series. 2nd Place Trophy (in each section) + 5 Months of Free entry for 2027 series. 3rd Place Trophy (in each section) + 3 Months of Free entry for 2027 series. Players are eligible to win only one Arizona Golden Cup prize, awarded in the highest scoring section in which they competed.
Golden Points System:
Finish Points
1st Place 20
2nd Place 16
3rd Place 13
4th Place 10
5–6 8
7–10 5
Participation 3
Bonus Points:
+3 points — Perfect score (4/4).
+2 points (only in December) — Played Most consecutive months.
Monthly Event Tie-Handling (Point Splitting): When two or more players are tied for placement in a monthly Arizona Golden Cup event, Golden points are split evenly among the tied positions.
Tie-Breaks (Year-End):
1. Most 1st-place finishes.
2. Head-to-head results.
3. Most tournaments played.
4. Best December result.
TD decisions are final.

CKQ Saturday Piscataway Rapids
Chess Kings & Queens Academy
Saturday, April 25, 2026
Event Overview
CKQ Saturday Piscataway Rapids
Start time: Players should arrive no later than 4:15 p.m. The first game begins promptly at 4:30. Latecomers risk their clock running when they arrive.
End time: The Under 600 section typically ends by 8:30 p.m., the Under 1200 section more like 9:00. The tournament could go a bit longer if players use all their time.
Players: Most players at this event will be children (ages 6-16), but adults are welcome to play. Beginners are welcome, but at a minimum players should know how to legally move chess pieces, recognize when they’re in check, and how to perform basic checkmates (ex; king and queen vs. king).
Structure / time controls: 4-SS, G30 +5. (Each player will play four games. Each player receives 30 minutes per game, plus another five seconds per move.)
Sections: Under 600 and Under 1200 rating sections. The Under 1200 section requires at least 500 rating to enter. Lower-rated and unrated players may enter with the tournament director's permission.
Requirements: A USCF membership is required to play in the tournament. Contact the tournament director if you need assistance creating or renewing a membership.
Equipment: Players do not need to bring any equipment. Players are recommended to eat before arriving, or at least bring a snack.
Registration: The registration fee is $30. Online registration closes at 5pm on the day of the event.
Byes: If you can’t attend the entire tournament, a half-point bye (limit one) is available for any round. Byes must be requested before the tournaments starts. If you are going to take first-round bye please contact the tournament director at least one hour before the tournament starts.
Prizes: Top three winners in each section receive a trophy or a medal.
For more information: Contact tournament director Stephen Lorimor ( [email protected] , phone/text: 908-286-0720).

events.name: Eureka College Open
events.sourceText:
Eureka College Open
Cerf Center - Eureka College
Saturday, April 25, 2026
Event Overview
Event Overview
Saturday April 25, 2026
Cerf Center
S Burgess St.
Eureka, IL 61530
US Chess Membership is Required for Open and U1401 sections. All US Chess Rules will be followed. Notation is required in all rated sections. Players 8 years old or younger (or their parents) can ask the tournament director before Round 1 for an exemption, if they are still learning to write in general.
Players and spectators younger than high school age (~14) must be accompanied by an adult. The accompanying adult must be present at the tournament site. Disruptive and/or destructive behavior will result in dismissal from the tournament and site. Players are responsible for the behavior of anyone accompanying them to the tournament.
Three Sections:
Open - Open to all players. Active US Chess membership required.
U1401 - Players must have a published USCF Regular Rating below 1401. Unrated players may play in this section, however they are only eligible for place prizes. Active US Chess membership required.
Non-rated - Geared towards players who would like to try out tournament chess before committing to a US Chess membership. Notation not required for this section. US Chess membership not required.
Check your rating here: https://ratings.uschess.org/
USCF Quick, Blitz, or any FIDE/foreign ratings may be used for section eligibility purposes for players without a regular rating.
Format:
Open and U1401 Sections
4 Rounds SS; G/40+10 (Clocks will be set with 40 minutes per player, and a 10 second increment that adds back after each move)
Non-rated Section
4 Rounds SS; G/20+5 (Clocks will be set with 20 minutes per player, and a 5 second increment that adds back after each move)
Entry Fees:
Entry Fees will be paid onsite with cash only.
General Entry Fee for Open and U1401 Sections: $30
Players with a US Chess Regular Rating 1800 or higher (using published or most recent live rating): $15
Players with a US Chess Regular Rating 2200 or higher (using published or most recent live rating): Free
General Entry Fee for Non-rated Section: $10
*Eureka College Students, Staff, and Faculty will receive free entry to any section.
**If a live rating is used for a discounted entry fee, that rating will be used for prize and pairing purposes.
Pre-registration link: https://forms.gle/EcjG5QydNEm448so6
Prizes
Prizes for Open and U1401 sections are based on 30 paid entries in rated sections.
Open
1st - $150
2nd - $90
Top U2001/Unrated - $60
Top U1701/Unrated - $50
U1401
1st - $100
2nd - $60
Top U1201 - $40
Top U900 - $35
USCF Quick, Blitz, or any FIDE/foreign ratings may be used for prize eligibility purposes for players without a regular rating. Unrated players playing in the U1401 section are only eligible for place prizes (i.e. 1st-2nd). Unrated players are eligible for all prizes in the Open section.
Non-rated
1st - $40
2nd - $20
3rd - $10
Schedule:
Onsite Registration and Check-In: 9:00am-9:45am
Open and U1401 Sections
Round 1: 10:00am
Round 2: 11:45am
Lunch Break
Round 3: 2:00pm
Round 4: 3:45pm
Estimated end: 5:30pm
Non-Rated Section
*Rounds will start ASAP, generally 15 minutes after the conclusion of the previous round
Round 1: 10:00am
Round 2: 15 minutes after the end of Round 1
Round 3: 15 minutes after the end of Round 2
Round 4: 15 minutes after the end of Round 3
Estimated end: 1:30pm
Players arriving after registration will receive one half-point bye and will be paired in subsequent rounds. Half-point byes may be requested for any round during registration only.
Boards and pieces will be provided. Please bring clocks (clocks will be provided for the Non-rated section).
Board 1 in the Open Section may be streamed via Facebook Live or Youtube.
Please contact tournament organizer if you have any questions.

Eureka , IL 61530
United States

events.sourceText:
MVP Chess K-12 Quads (FREE for US Chess Members)
Mount Vernon Rec Center
Sunday, April 26, 2026
Event Overview
Date: Sunday, April 26, 2026 at 12:45 PM
Venue: 2017 Belle View Blvd. Alexandria, VA 22307. The rec center has recently been renovated and features state-of-the-art facilities including a gym, two skating rinks, an indoor pool, and a rock-climbing wall.
Organizer: MVP Chess is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization based in Alexandria, Virginia. Our mission is to make chess accessible for everyone and develop growth-minded players. For questions, please email [email protected] .
Register Now: MVP Chess K-12 Quads | April 2026 - Organized by MVP Chess | Chess Nut
Entry & Donations
This tournament is FREE for all US Chess members in grades K–12.
An active US Chess membership is required — you can join or renew here .
The event is limited to 32 players, so please register in advance to secure your spot and help us plan pairings and sections.
We welcome voluntary donations to help cover the cost of room rental, awards, and other tournament-related expenses.
All contributions are tax-deductible and may be made online or onsite at the event.
Format
3-round quad (final section may be a small Swiss)
Time control: G/25; d5 (25 minutes per player, 5-second delay)
Rated by US Chess
Awards
🏆 Trophies for each quad winner
🎖️ Medals for all other participants
📺 Game Analysis Feature: Select games will be analyzed on the MVP Chess YouTube channel. To be considered, players should submit their scoresheets at the end of the event.
Schedule
Check-in: 12:45 PM
Round 1: 1:00 PM
Rounds begin as soon as prior games finish
Expected finish: no later than 4:00 PM
Rules & Expectations
US Chess rules apply
Notation optional
Chess sets and clocks provided
Parents/guardians should stay on-site during the event
Please show respect for opponents, staff, and the venue
Media Policy
MVP Chess may take photos or short video clips for educational and promotional purposes.
Names will not be published without consent. If you prefer not to be photographed, simply let us or the photographer know.

events.name: Super Sunday FIDE Tournament
events.sourceText:
Super Sunday FIDE Tournament
Chess Kings & Queens Academy
Sunday, April 26, 2026
Event Overview
Note: This is a dual USCF - FIDE section of a larger USCF tournament (Super Sunday). Please read the information carefully. For the other sections and more events, please check our other listing.
Structure
- 3 rounds Swiss-Style. G75 +15. Accelerated pairings at the director's discretion.
- One half-point bye is available for any round, but must be requested before tournament start. All other requested byes are zero points.
- Clocks, boards, and weighed plastic pieces are provided. Players may use their own equipment with the agreement of their opponent.
- FIDE notice: Rules for late arrival will match standard USCF 60 minute rule.
Schedule
- Round times: 10:00 am / 1:30pm / 5:00 pm
USCF
- A current USCF membership is required to play.
- Players MUST have at least 1) 1700 USCF rating (live or current published), or 2) 1600 FIDE rating
FIDE
- A valid FIDE ID is required to play. Most players with a valid USCF membership may request a USA-flagged FIDE ID at this URL. Note that it may take several days to process. https://tinyurl.com/3zcjwmex
- There is no minimum FIDE rating for this event. There is a maximum rating of 2399.
- FIDE norms are not available at this event.
Registration
- Registration fee: $45
- Online registration only. Registration closes at 9:00 a.m. on the day of the event. On-site registrations are discouraged but may be accepted at the TD's discretion.
- Registration link: https://chesskq.com/tournament
- Free entry for all players rated 2200 or higher. ($45 will be deducted from the player's prize winnings.) E-mail name, USCF ID, and FIDE ID to Stephen Lorimor at [email protected] to sign up.
- This event has no age restrictions.
- Players signing up for a section they are not eligible to join will be automatically shifted to the appropriate section.
- Players ineligible to participate in any section of this event, or withdrawing before 9:00 AM on the day of the tournament, will receive a credit for a future class or tournament.
Prizes
Prizes are paid out via Zelle or PayPal. Check-by-mail available for anyone without these options.
- 1st place: $200
- 2nd place: $100
- Top U1800 (FIDE): $60
@45 players (across all three sections) - we serve doughnuts and coffee. Everyone wins!
@50 players - we add a Top Junior (under age 12) award to each section
@55 players - we add a Top Senior (age 55+) award to each section
@60 players - we increase 2nd place and "top under __ rating" prizes for all sections by $15
@65 players - we increase 1st place prizes for all sections by $20.
Additional information
- The tournament director for this event is Stephen Lorimor. Bye requests and other issues may be e-mailed to [email protected] , or by voice/text to 908-286-0720. Note that he may not notice or respond to e-mails, texts, or calls after 9:00 am the day of the event.
- The venue is located within walking distance of multiple restaurants and fast food businesses. No food is allowed at the playing tables, but a waiting room with tables is available.

Speedy - because the time control is G/5;d0 (each player gets 5 minutes to make all their moves.)
Quads - because we divide the players in groups of four based on ratings or skill level.
Players play two games against each of the three other players in their quad.
We hold a Speedy Quads tournament every fourth Monday each month. Speedy Quads has a FREE entry (but we do accept donations to cover the rating fees). There are no prizes. The games are blitz-rated and do not affect regular or quick ratings.
Time Control is G/5;d0; and we play double-round quads.
Register on site only - please arrive before 7:30pm. US Chess members will play rated quads. Non-members will play in an unrated small Swiss blitz tournament.

The Charlotte Spring Open is a classical event with a $6,000 guaranteed prize fund - $5,500 in the main event plus a FREE $500 Blitz tournament! All sections are US Chess and FIDE rated. El Dorado 750 Regular Swiss
El Dorado Train Depot, West Room
Saturday, May 2, 2026
Event Overview
05/02/2026
Train Depot, West Room
430 N Main St El Dorado, KS 67042
Tournament:
Format: 4-round Swiss (no eliminations).
Time Control: g/45; d5.
Registration: 8:30 - 9:15. Rounds: 9:30 - 12:00 - 1:45 - 3:30.
Players who register in advance do not need to arrive early.
One 1/2-point bye may be requested at any time before round 2 pairings. No changes to requested byes allowed after round 2 pairings.
Registration And Fees:
Players 18 and under may register as Scholastic at a discount if they wish to do so.
Scholastic players will not be eligible for cash prizes.
All games will be rated by the United States Chess Federation. (Regular and Quick)
All players must be members of the United States Chess Federation.
KCA membership not required.
Normal Entry Fee : $35 by 04/28 at midnight or $45 after or on-site.
Scholastic Entry Fee : $10 by 04/28 at midnight or $20 after or on-site.
On-site registration is cash-only.
Players that wish to change their section may do so only during registration before round 1.
Sections:
There will be 4 sections available to register in, but all scholastic sections will be merged into their non-scholastic counterpart for a total of 2 sections:
Open (Anyone)
Amateur (U1400)
TD reserves the right to merge sections or move select players up or down a section if deemed necessary for pairings.
TD also reserves rights to use accelerate pairings if deemed necessary.
Sections will be based on supplemental ratings from April.
Prizes:
$750 Prize Fund (b/35 Normal entries, 50% guaranteed):
Biggest upset: $135 (see Fine Print below) *
Open :
1st: $225
2nd: $145
Amateur :
1st: $145
2nd: $100
Equipment:
Players must bring their own board, pieces and clocks. There are very few clocks for the TD to loan.
TD may be too busy to assist players in setting their clocks. It is advised that players set their own clocks before the event. Most modern clocks have a g/45;d5 preset.
Nearby Amenities:
Coffee: Great coffee shop (Dilly Deli) within a short walk
Food: Mexican restaurant within a short walk, Casey's, Taco Bell, Wendy's, and Arby's within a short drive. We have a refrigerator to keep food and drinks in, and a microwave to cook it.
Parking: Free, on-site.
Contact:
Feel free to reach out with any questions you might have.
Email: [email protected]
Phone (Text only): (316) 350-7354‬
Fine Print
* Unrated players do not qualify for biggest upset. Score calculation for this prize is higherRating-lowerRating for wins, and that same amount divided by two for draws. Player with the highest score wins the prize. All games in all sections will be considered for the single biggest upset for the overall tournament. Winner of biggest upset may also qualify and win a place prize in their section.

Key Rules, Procedures, Cheating & Etiquette:
Scoresheets: Notation of moves in Open and Reserve sections is required. Players must record moves in algebraic notation, typically writing the move after executing it on the board.
Contacting the TD: Stop the clock and immediately call the Tournament Director for any rule violation, illegal move, or dispute.
Touch-Move Rule: If you touch one of your pieces, you must move it if it has a legal move. If you touch an opponent's piece, you must capture it if possible.
One-Hand Rule: Use only one hand to move a piece and press the clock.
Clock use: Make your move then press the clock to stop your time until it is your turn again. Running out of time before checkmate means you lose the game automatically.
Illegal Moves: If you make one, your opponent stops the clock, shows the TD the illegal move, and you get a time penalty (2 minutes extra time will be added to your opponent).
Castling: Touch the King first, then the Rook, using one hand.
"J'adoube" (I adjust): Say this before touching a piece to adjust it, not to move it.
Pawn Promotion: The pawn is considered "touched" when it reaches the promotion square and must be promoted immediately to the piece you place on that square.
No Outside Help: No computers, phones (strict penalties), books, or talking to others about the game during play.
Communication: Only talk to your opponent or the TD. Be courteous. Be courteous of the players and their ongoing games around you. Whisper if talking must happen.
Cell Phones: Keep them off and away; penalties are severe.
Disputes: Handle calmly; argue with the TD, not your opponent.
USCF Board Regulations & Features:
Square Size: 2.25 inches is standard, though 2 to 2.5 inches is permissible.
Overall Size: 20" x 20" or 22" x 22" (approx. 50-55 cm).
Material: Usually flexible vinyl, often featuring algebraic notation on all sides.
Proportion Requirement: The King's base diameter should occupy roughly 75% to 80% of the square size.
Where to Find More rules: The full rules are in the US Chess Federation's website under Official Rules of Chess section.

events.name: SCHOLASTIC SUNDAY by Indy Chess
events.sourceText:
SCHOLASTIC SUNDAY by Indy Chess
St. Monica Catholic School Gym (Door 15)
Sunday, May 3, 2026
Event Overview
REGISTER FOR THIS TOURNAMENT HERE: https://www.indychess.org/events
Kids who have learned how the pieces move and some basic strategy are welcome to enter the world of rated chess tournaments! All school-aged kids from kindergarten to 12th grade are welcome. Walk-ins are discouraged, as we would appreciate all registering online in advance. The chess playing room is a silent atmosphere to enable maximum concentration.
For the "rated" tournament, all players MUST be members of the US Chess Federation ($24/year). Before registering for the rated event, become a member of USCF here (you will need to write down your child's USCF ID#). However, being a member of Indy Chess--our local club--at $50/year/student or $75/year/family is optional. If interested, you can do that here to get a $5 discount on this event and every other one you attend this year with us, including Weekly Tuesdays, and support the growth of chess in Indy!
[If a beginner and wanting to play in the "casual" tournament (unrated, does not require USCF membership), that is explained far below.]
Here are the details:
Check-in on site: 1:45-2:00pm, entering the door up a few exterior stairs/ramp (not the street-level door). Games start right after a player meeting at 2:15pm.
4ss: Four rounds in a "Swiss" system. A Swiss tournament--the most common chess form--means every player plays every round, with future rounds pairing those who won and those who lost. Up to two 1/2-point byes can be requested by emailing [email protected] or telling the tournament director at the event which rounds you would like byes. Note: Premiere section is 3 rounds.
G/25+5: Games are 25 minutes on each players clock, plus 5 seconds added to a player's time when they hit the clock every move.
USCF-rated: All players must be members of the US Chess Federation and provide a member ID# in online registration. This will give each child a "rating" in chess that will follow them with each tournament they play. Ratings are in blitz, quick, and regular play, and the 25+5 time control affects their regular and their quick rating.
Entry fee is $20/kid, or $15 for members of Indy Chess.
Kids rated under 1000 are divided into three sections so kids play only those in their age group (e.g., 3rd Grade & Under, 6th Grade & Under, and 12th Grade & Under). Want your child to "play up?" Just email Mike at [email protected] . Notation is optional but encouraged in these sections.
There is one "Premiere" section for kids rated 1000 or above (published rating from the 1st of the month). Notation is required in the premiere sections. The Premiere section is three rounds, and may be split by rating at TD discretion to achieve less than eight players per section.
Casual Tournament:
Alongside the rated tournament, kids can instead register for a casual tournament (i.e., unrated) which will begin at the same time. The games will be optionally clocked, notation is not required, and the tournament director will determine section splits based on turnout. It will be a Swiss tournament (i.e., all players play all rounds, unless someone gets a bye due to an odd number). There will be four rounds. There are trophies for the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd place winners!
Other details:
Children under 12 years old must have an adult present and responsible for them, unless the parent/guardian has the permission of the tournament director.
Concessions are typically available for sale by St. Monica, including hot food (less likely in summer months).
An outside playground is available.
Parents may watch chess silently from the bleachers in the gym, or sit at tables in the cafeteria. There is a guest WiFi network with password August27.
The site is wheelchair accessible.
Parking is free in the school lot (Door 15 is located near the southeast side of the building), but is sometimes full right at 1:45p due to a church function. Parking on a nearby street for overflow is available.
Chess sets, clocks, and notation sheets are provided for up to 60 kids. If the child has played in a tournament or two prior, it is helpful if they bring a regulation set and/or clock to ensure there are enough.
Trophies are provided to the top five finishers in each of the three lower sections. In the premiere section, a $50 Amazon gift card goes to the winner (decided by 5+0 blitz playoff if need be, Black/White randomly chosen). Biggest upset earns a medal (unrated does not qualify).
Players who notate at least one game get to pick a prize from the bin at the end of the tournament! Learn how to notate chess moves here (YouTube link).
Questions? Email Mike at [email protected] . We hope to see you there!

We aim to create a pleasant environment for playing chess. Below are the answers we received at a previous tournament to the question of what do we do better than other tournaments.
Tournament Features
We pair rounds as early as possible and start rounds on time You have time to get ready and don't have to waste your time waiting for the round to start Players like the way we run our events Survey results from a previous Maryland Open
30 second increment time control in the top six sections → No more clock smashing scrambles at the end of the game.
Score-based prizes → See the advantages below.
Additional 1st place prizes to clear first when there is no 5-0 player in the section, added to your score prize → More prize money
>Sets and boards, and clocks provided in ALL sections → All you need to do is show up.
Minimum ratings to play in the top six sections → Less mismatch games.
Free Sunday morning Continental breakfast → Relax, have some coffee and a danish before you start your game.
Texting or emailing of pairings to your cell phone available → No rush at the pairing chart before the round
$149/ per night room rate → Relax and stay at the tournament hotel. $5 EF discount if staying at hotel Reserve a room
Hotel next to DC Metro stop → Take the Metro directly to the tournament.
Shorter time controls in lower sections → Less waiting around between rounds.
Prizes
This tournament will pay prizes based solely on your final score. All the prizes are guaranteed. If the total pay out in the Open section is less than $1500, extra money will be added to the pay out of the top score group to bring the total to $1500.
Advantages over place-based scoring
Less Waiting
Your score determines your prize. Once you finish your last game, you can receive a check.
Less Uncertainty
Your prize does not get lowered if others tie with you. For example, if there are two 5-0 players, both receive the full amount for 5-0.
Less short draws
The total payout is always higher when games are decisive.

5/9 - Quad chess tournament G40; d5
Saint Petersburg Chess Club
Saturday, May 9, 2026
Event Overview
There will be no “Byes” or withdrawals allowed. Please complete all your Quad games.
WHAT IS THE QUAD CHESS TOURNAMENT? After all the players have entered, they’re ordered from highest rating to lowest. Unrated players are placed at the low end. The top four players are placed into their own section (a “quad”), then the next four highest in another section, and so on down the list.If two family members are in the same quad, I can move one of them quad up or down.The players in each quad play a round robin, one game against each of the players in their section, for a total of three games each. If there is not an even multiple of four players, the lowest section (usually) will have the few extra players and play a three round Swiss tournament rather than a round robin. The quad format is popular in one day events, and results in players of the most similar playing strengths being paired together for all three rounds. Each group of four chess players is called a Quad.If two family members are at the same Quad,I can move one of them to another Quad.
ADVANTAGES OF QUAD TOURNAMENTS: The advantage of Quad Tournaments, and why players enjoy them so much, is that players of the same strength and experience are able to compete against each other. In addition, the less experienced players are able to win the same "First Place" prizes as their more experienced, stronger counterparts in Quad I and II. You have opportunity your rating to go up faster!!!

Arizona's Premier Year - Long USCF Chess Series.

A year-long USCF-rated chess series. Players earn Golden Points at each monthly event. Final standings after December determine the Arizona Golden Cup Champion, 2nd and 3rd Place in each section. Finish Points

Compete in as many or as few Chess League events, earning points throughout the year. The top 12 players from each section will be invited to the Chess League round-robin tournament at the conclusion of the regular season to determine the Chess League Champion!
Season Pass and Multi-month registration discounts available.

Evanston Tri-Level May
Levy Activity Center
Saturday, May 9, 2026
Event Overview
4SS G/40, delay 5. USCF Dual Rated
Open to players who are EITHER age 14 and older OR whose US Chess Current Published Regular Rating for the month of the tournament is 900 or higher.
US Chess Membership is required.
Three Sections
Section Gold: 1700 and over (1600 - 1699 may play up to Gold)
Section Silver: 1200-1699 (1100 - 1199 may play up to Silver)
Section Bronze: U1200 and unrated
Sections may be combined at TD discretion. IMPORTANT: We use the US Chess Current Published Regular rating for the month of the tournament to place players in sections. We don’t make exceptions.
Junior players: Junior players (under fourteen years) rated 900+ are welcome. Must be accompanied by an adult throughout the event. We do not accept junior players rated under 900.
Four rounds. Digital clocks are required and will be set to G/40, delay 5. You may take one half-point bye in round 1, 2 or 3.
Prizes: Your prize is an excellent playing experience at a reasonable cost. We've been running these since 2007 and people like playing here.
Entry fee is $20. Please pre-register and pay here when registration opens. Online registration closes when the tournament is full; we don’t have a wait list; we reopen registration if spaces become available.
On-Site Entries: Check evanstonchess.org the morning of the tournament. If space is available on-site entries are $20 cash on an as-available basis starting at 9:00 a.m.
Master and Expert Entries: First two Masters or Experts who sign up get free entry. If your USCF or FIDE regular rating is 2000 or higher, email your name and USCF ID to [email protected] by 5 p.m. the Tuesday before the tournament to pre-register.
Schedule:
Check-in and On-site Registration from 9:00 to 9:30 AM.
Players must check in on the posted registration list by 9:30 am; players who don’t check in receive a half-point bye for the first round or will be paired with another late arrival.
First Round 9:50 am, last round over roughly 5:00 pm.
Bring your lunch! We will have a brief lunch break with no time to go out for food. On-site we have vending machine snacks, coffee and soft drinks.
Other information: Sets supplied. Bring digital delay clocks. Wheelchair accessible. No Smoking. Limit 50 players.
Address: 300 Dodge Ave
Evanston , IL 60202
United States

Montgomery County Chess Tournament 5/9/26
Bender JCC of Greater Washington
Saturday, May 9, 2026
Event Overview
Register at chessacademy.com/tournaments !
This tournament is for scholastic players in grades K-12 with and without prior tournament experience. We recommend that players in their first tournament choose the Unrated option, where they will be grouped by age and play 3 or 4 games.
Players who've previously done well in an Unrated section or have previous rated tournament experience should choose the Rated option, where they'll be placed in a group of 4 players according to their age and rating. Each participant then plays one game against each of the other three players in their group. At the end of the third game, the winner of each group receives a trophy.
This event should typically finish in 1-2 hours, but can potentially take as long as 3 hours for the most advanced players (although that is rare).
Everyone will use a clock! We'll go over how to use clocks on-site, and you can watch this short video to see how they work. Unrated section players will play a game in 10 minutes with a 5 second delay, and Rated games are 25 minutes with a 5 second delay for each player.
Players can play in the morning at 10am, the afternoon at 1pm, or both!
All sections are non-elimination, and all players participate in all rounds
If you're playing in the Rated sections and have a US Chess ID# and membership, please include it. If you don't have one, we will purchase it for you ($24 value!). If you're not sure what your ID# is you can look it up here
Please arrive 15 minutes before games start. Players who arrive after that may not be placed in quads.
Prices increase by $10 at noon the Tuesday before the tournament.
Questions? Please let us know at Click here to show mail address !

St Martin's Episcopal School
Saturday, May 9, 2026
Event Overview
Strategic Thoughts NOLA, Crescent City Chess, and Downriver Chess Present:
CLICK HERE TO REGISTER!
THE NEW ORLEANS YOUTH CHESS 2025-2026 SEASON
Venue: St Martin's Episcopal School, 225 Green Acres Rd, Metairie
Format: Four round swiss format, G/25;d5 tournament. Five sections: K-2; K-4; K-6; K-8, K-12
Prizes: Individual and team trophies in each section
Registration: 8:45AM-9:15AM; Anyone not registered by 9:15AM will be given a first round bye
Check in: Check in is not necessary if your name is on the "entry list" tab of the King Registration page and there are no problems listed
Round times: 10AM, 11:15AM, 12:30PM, and 1:45PM
Entry fee: $30 if received by midnight one week before the event date (Saturday night). $35 if received by midnight two days before (Thursday night). $40 day before or same day (Friday-Saturday).
USCF requirement: Current USCF membership required, join here. If your membership does not have an expiration date, it is not yet current.
Eligibility: All K-12 students are welcome. You do not need to be part of a school or chess team to compete.
Discount codes: Use code FAMILY for a $5 discount when registering multiple siblings of the same family. Use code LUNCH for a $10 discount if student or family receives free or reduced lunch benefits.
Contact: email Click here to show mail address .
Byes: Two half-point byes available upon request. All byes must be requested before round 3, with exceptions made for emergency situations. All bye requests final after beginning of round 1.
Teams: Teams are comprised of the top four players per school per grade section. Minimum two players to qualify as a team. Team totals are calculated using cumulative score of each player.
Late arrivals: Games are forfeited 30 minutes after the round start time if a player has not arrived.
Refunds: Players who withdraw 30 minutes before round one are eligible for a refund of their entry fee, minus any applicable payment-processor fees (typically 5-7%).
Calendar: Full season calendar here .

events.name: West Texas '26 May Open
events.sourceText:
West Texas '26 May Open
Mad Hatter's House of Games
Saturday, May 9, 2026
Event Overview
PURPOSE: Our goal is to expand rated chess opportunities in our community to benefit and encourage both new and experienced players.
MONTHLY SPECIAL PROMOTIONS & ANNOUNCEMENTS:
Always FREE registration for players with current USCF rating over 2000! Entry fee deducted from winnings.
SPECIAL AWARD: TBA!
2025-2026 SEASON SPECIAL PROJECTS, CONTESTS & SPECIAL RECOGNITIONS:
2025-2026 Brilliancy Award - The player with the most brilliant move this season will receive an award at the May Open!
2025-2026 Texas Chess Association Region I Recognition Program (Details are to be determined) - Awards will be presented at the May Open!
DATE: Saturday, May 9, 2026
LOCATION: Mad Hatter's House of Games; 1507 Texas Ave., Lubbock, TX 79401
START TIME: Round 1 begins at 11 AM (Players registered in advance online arrive to pay and check-in before 10:45; Players registering onsite arrive before 10:30am)
END TIME: Most sections will finish at approximately 5:30 PM. The Novice Sections will finish at approximately 4:30 PM if players use full time allowed, but usually end earlier. Section awards will be presented shortly after all players in a section have completed their final round. Lower sections typically wrap up earlier than higher sections.
COST: FREE REGISTRATION for players with current USCF rating over 2000 (entry fee deducted from winnings); $16/player for Early (Online at https://forms.gle/FpBLjQYmqnBAkN6F9 ) or $21/player for Late (On-site) registration. Payment options include PayPal at the time of online registration or cash on-site at the door. ***There is a $1 cash payment discount, bringing cash payments down to $15 for early registration or $20 for onsite registration.***
REGISTRATION DEADLINES: Early (Online at https://forms.gle/FpBLjQYmqnBAkN6F9 ) pre-registrations are due by 6 PM Friday, May 8, 2026. Late (On-site) registrations must be done between 10:00 and 10:30 AM on Saturday, May 9, 2026.
TOURNAMENT DETAILS:
Tournament Director: Robert Moore, Region I Director – Texas Chess Association
USCF Rated Event: Current USCF membership required - PLEASE update your membership prior to tournament day. Contact us if you need help registering or renewing your USCF membership.
Schedule: This is a swiss style tournament; See below for number of rounds and time controls for each section. Pairings will be posted 5 minutes after the last game in the previous round ends, and the new round will begin 10 minutes after the previous round is complete. This effectively adds a 10-minute break for players who are the last to finish a round. Round 1 begins promptly at 11 AM.
Equipment: Chess sets and notation supplies will be provided. Some chess clocks will be available, but please bring your own clock if you have one .
Five sections as follows:
Open Championship - Must be rated above 1300. If fewer than 8 players are above 1300, highest rated players below 1300 will be used to ensure at least 8 players in the section; 4 Rounds, G/40;d5
Reserve A (U1300) - Rating between 950 and 1300 and unrated players; 4 Rounds, G/40;d5
Reserve B (U1000) - Rating between 750 and 1000 and unrated players; 4 Rounds, G/40;d5
Novice A (U800) - Rating between 350 and 800 and unrated scholastic players; 5 Rounds, G/25;d5
Novice B (U400) - Rating under 400 and unrated players 5th grade or below; 5 Rounds, G/25;d5
EXCEPTIONS FOR PROVISIONALLY RATED PLAYERS : Adult players with provisional ratings below 750 may choose to play up into a Reserve section, but they may also register for the novice section that matches their provisional rating. Scholastic players with provisional ratings may be placed in an appropriate section by the tournament director.
NOTE ABOUT PLAYERS' SECTION PLACEMENT: At the TD's discretion, sections may be added, deleted, or combined. A player near the rating cut-off may be moved to maintain an even number of players in as many sections as possible. Also, at the TD's discretion, section rating ranges may be revised onsite based on natural breaks in rating distributions, which could increase the number of players in the Open Championship section to more than 8.
RATING DETERMINATION: USCF ratings as of May 4 will be used to determine section eligibility for this event.
Prizes:
Cash prizes for Open Championship and Reserve Sections: Cash prize guarantees are based on 50 registered players .
The total guaranteed prize fund for 50 players is $350.
The available cash prize fund will be increased or decreased based on registration variance from 50 players. At 100 players, the prize fund will grow to $1000!
If there are fewer than 50 players, prizes may be given for fewer than 3 places in each section.
Ties will follow USCF rules for splitting cash prizes.
Trophies & medals for Novice sections:
Trophies will be awarded to the top three finishers in each Novice section.
Medals will be awarded to players who tie for third but do not receive a trophy.
Standard tie breaks will be used.
PHOTOGRAPHY: Photos may be taken during the tournament and awards ceremony. These images may be shared with Texas Chess Association, news outlets, or other interested groups or individuals. Images may be used for promotion of subsequent chess events.
CONTACT: Completing the registration form linked below should generate an email to the address used to complete the form. Prior to the tournament, another email communication will be sent with a link to check tournament registration details.
If you have any questions please email us:
Robert Moore - [email protected] ; 334-233-4373
Amy Jones - [email protected] ; 806-787-3568

events.sourceText:
2026 Memorial Tournament by Azeri Chess Academy LLC
Houston Chess Studio
Sunday, May 10, 2026
Event Overview
Organizer
Azeri Chess Academy LLC ( USCF Affiliate ID A9567106 )
Tournament Director
International Grandmaster and Local TD Ulvi Bajarani ( USCF ID 17112757 )
Tournament Purpose
This tournament is part of the Azeri Chess Academy Houston Circuit 2026 and is dedicated to Memorial Day (May 25, 2026)
Date & Time
Round 1 starts on May 10, 2026, at 10:00 AM .
Venue
Houston Chess Studio, 250 Patton Street Suite H Houston, Texas 77009.
Time Control
G/30, d10 (Each player gets 30 minutes with a 10-second delay per move).
Format
6-round Swiss system.
Pairings will be generated using ChessRoster SwissSys 11.75 (subject to updates to more recent versions).
Ratings
This tournament is USCF-rated , and the official May 2026 USCF ratings will be used.
Byes
Up to two (2) half-point byes is allowed and must be declared during registration.
No additional byes are permitted except for 0-point byes .
A 1-point bye is awarded to a player who is left without an opponent when the number of players is odd in a given round.
Entry Fee
$60 – Until April 10, 2026, or for the first 10 players, whichever comes first.
$80 – Until May 1, 2026, or for the next 20 players, whichever comes first.
$100 – Until May 10, 2026 at 12:00 AM (midnight), or until all spots are filled.
Cancellation & Refund Policy
A 50% refund will be granted if a player requests cancellation by May 6, 2026, at 12:00 AM (midnight) .
No refunds will be issued after this deadline.
Withdrawal Policy
Players must notify an arbiter before the start of a round if they intend to withdraw.
Failure to notify an arbiter may affect eligibility for future tournaments organized by Azeri Chess Academy LLC.
Number of Entries
Maximum of 64 participants.
Eligibility
Open to all players with active USCF membership .
Players must ensure their USCF membership is active before the start of Round 1.
Onsite check-ins may be available for players needing USCF membership renewal. They must pay the required renewal fee plus an additional $10 processing fee.
Failure to renew an expired membership before the tournament will result in exclusion without a refund .

30-minute break

If rating prizes are offered, unrated players are eligible only for prizes in the lowest rating group . This does not affect their eligibility for the overall (main) prizes.
Prizes are equally shared in case of a tie .
Payments will be sent via Zelle/PayPal before May 17, 2026. Prize-winners must contact the organizer immediately after the final round to confirm their preferred payment method. Additionally, the prize winners are required to participate in the prize ceremony following the tournament. Failure to complete these actions will result in disqualification from receiving the prize.
Tiebreaks
Tiebreaks will be determined using ChessRoster SwissSys , applying standard USCF tiebreak methods :
Solkoff
Modified Median
Cumulative
If players are tied for 1st place and all tiebreaks are equal , a coin toss will determine the winner.
Anti-Cheating Measures & Electronic Devices Policy
All players are subject to electronic device scanning (“wanding”) .
No electronic devices (phones, smartwatches, etc.) are allowed unless explicitly permitted by the arbiter for medical reasons .
A designated storage box will be provided for electronic devices.
Photography & Video Recording
By registering, players consent to being photographed and recorded by the Tournament Director and their associates for promotional purposes.
Equipment & Notation Rules
Chess sets, clocks, scoresheets, and pens will be provided by the organizer.
Notation is mandatory unless a player has less than 5 minutes remaining on their clock.
Players may keep a yellow scoresheet copy and a pen . However, players are encouraged to bring an extra pen , as available pens may be limited .
Parking & Nearby Restaurants:

3 restaurants in the same strip center as venue: The Red Hot Noodle (Asian), Subway , and Patron Pizza . Several others are within walking distance.

Fairfax Chess Tournament 5/16/26
Pozez Jewish Community Center of Northern Virginia
Saturday, May 16, 2026
Event Overview
Register at chessacademy.com/tournaments !
This tournament is for scholastic players in grades K-12 with and without prior tournament experience. We recommend that players in their first tournament choose the Unrated option, where they will be grouped by age and play 3 or 4 games.
Players who've previously done well in an Unrated section or have previous rated tournament experience should choose the Rated option, where they'll be placed in a group of 4 players according to their age and rating. Each participant then plays one game against each of the other three players in their group. At the end of the third game, the winner of each group receives a trophy.
This event should typically finish in 1-2 hours, but can potentially take as long as 3 hours for the most advanced players (although that is rare).
Everyone will use a clock! We'll go over how to use clocks on-site, and you can watch this short video to see how they work. Unrated section players will play a game in 10 minutes with a 5 second delay, and Rated games are 25 minutes with a 5 second delay for each player.
Players can play in the morning at 10am, the afternoon at 1pm, or both!
All sections are non-elimination, and all players participate in all rounds
If you're playing in the Rated sections and have a US Chess ID# and membership, please include it. If you don't have one, we will purchase it for you ($24 value!). If you're not sure what your ID# is you can look it up here
Please arrive 15 minutes before games start. Players who arrive after that may not be placed in quads.
Prices increase by $10 at noon the Tuesday before the tournament.

Tunnelvision XLIV
Columbia Chess Club
Saturday, May 16, 2026
Event Overview
The Columbia Chess Club Presents Columbia Tunnelvision XLIV
May 16, 2026
$1000 Guaranteed
10:30 a.m. 4-Round G/45;inc.5
Columbia Chess Club
6169 St. Andrews Rd.
Columbia, SC 29212
Register
Registration
Standard registration is $40 until the day before the tournament. $50 late registration the day before/morning of. Registration online only, registration limited to first 74 players.
Entry for titled players (National Master and above) is free, standard entry fee deducted from prizes. If you are a titled player, simply use the "Titled Player" option at checkout.
Considering Tunnelvision as your first chess tournament? Great! We've put together a guide to help first-time players .
Register Now
Pre-Registered Players
Format
4 Round Swiss. Time control is G45/inc.5 (45 minutes starting time with a 5-second increment ), which will be USCF dual-rated under both Quick and Classical. All equipment provided. USCF Rules Apply, active USCF Membership required. Tournament has three sections: Championship (1600+), Under 1600, and Under 1000. Players may register for a higher section if they are within 100 USCF rating points of the cutoff.
If you need to renew or obtain a USCF membership, please visit https://new.uschess.org/join-us-chess.
Live Standings/Pairings/Boards
The top board of each section will be live streamed to the DGT LiveCloud along with real-time updates to Lichess.org and Chess.com. A live video stream of the top Championship board will also be available on the club's Twitch page. See this site's "Live" menu for links.
Live standings (including current pre-registration information) and pairings are also available below.

Round 1: 10:30 a.m.
Round 2: 12:50 p.m.
Round 3: 2:40 p.m.
Round 4: 4:30 p.m.
Byes
A single half-point bye is available any round, including the final round. The half-point bye may be requested as a part of the advance entry or on site before the tournament starts. Thereafter the only bye available is a zero-point bye. The chief tournament director shall have the ability to grant a half-point bye for any round on unusual circumstances.

The Columbia Chess Club offers on-site concessions, including drinks and snacks. By the Fire Pizza and Zorba's Restaurant are located in the same shopping center and will be open during the tournament. Many other restaurants are available close by!

5/23 - ST. PETERSBURG EXTRA QUAD CHESS TOURNAMENT G60; d5.
Saint Petersburg Chess Club
Saturday, May 23, 2026
Event Overview
There will be no “Byes” or withdrawals allowed. Please complete all your Quad games.
WHAT IS THE QUAD CHESS TOURNAMENT? After all the players have entered, they’re ordered from highest rating to lowest. Unrated players are placed at the low end. The top four players are placed into their own section (a “quad”), then the next four highest in another section, and so on down the list. The players in each quad play a round robin, one game against each of the players in their section, for a total of three games each. If there is not an even multiple of four players, the lowest section (usually) will have the few extra players and play a three round Swiss tournament rather than a round robin. The quad format is popular in one day events, and results in players of the most similar playing strengths being paired together for all three rounds. A Quad Tournament consists of the top four ranked players (#s 1-4) on the Chess Ladder playing each other, then the second top four ranked players (#s 5-8) playing each other, then the third top four ranked players (#s 9-12) playing each other, and so forth. Each group of four chess players is called a Quad.If two family members are at the same Quad,I can move one of them to another Quad.
ADVANTAGES OF QUAD TOURNAMENTS: The advantage of Quad Tournaments, and why players enjoy them so much, is that players of the same strength and experience are able to compete against each other. In addition, the less experienced players are able to win the same "First Place" prizes as their more experienced, stronger counterparts in Quad I and II. You have opportunity your rating to go up faster!!!
LOCATION : Saint Petersburg Chess Club 540 4th Avenue North Saint Petersburg, FL 33701 (it is located in between Mirror Lake and the Coliseum, next to the Sunshine Center.)
REGISTRATION : 10:00-10:45 a.m. If you want to make sure you can play, you need to Pay ahead of time here - https://home.chessregister.com/
ENTRY FEE:
$25 if paid by Wednesday (3 days before the tournament)
$30 afterward
$35 if paid on Saturday
USCF membership is required. Please check your USCF ID and renew it if it has expired. If you need me to do it on site add $5 to your bill.
ROUNDS: Three Rounds, First starts at approx. 11:00 a.m.
TIME CONTROL: G60; d5
PRIZES : $65 for first place at each Quad or very big trophies for 1st place (if two players tied for 1st place $33 each, or chess trophies for 1st place for both of them)
Trophies for 1st to 3rd place for the last section!
IMPORTANT NOTICE : Due to space limitation to secure your spot Pay online ahead of time! BRING YOUR CHESS CLOCK!!!
Visit our website- https://saintpetersburgchessclub.com/ for more information about chess at Saint Petersburg.
Join our Facebook groups Saint Petersburg Chess Tournaments - https://www.facebook.com/groups/385692191510406/
For more information you can call (727) 776-5583, or send me email to Click here to show mail address

Baltimore County Chess Tournament 5/23/26
Jewish Community Center of Greater Baltimore
Saturday, May 23, 2026
Event Overview
Register at chessacademy.com/tournaments !
This tournament is for scholastic players in grades K-12 with and without prior tournament experience. We recommend that players in their first tournament choose the Unrated option, where they will be grouped by age and play 3 or 4 games.
Players who've previously done well in an Unrated section or have previous rated tournament experience should choose the Rated option, where they'll be placed in a group of 4 players according to their age and rating. Each participant then plays one game against each of the other three players in their group. At the end of the third game, the winner of each group receives a trophy.
This event should typically finish in 1-2 hours, but can potentially take as long as 3 hours for the most advanced players (although that is rare).
Everyone will use a clock! We'll go over how to use clocks on-site, and you can watch this short video to see how they work. Unrated section players will play a game in 10 minutes with a 5 second delay, and Rated games are 25 minutes with a 5 second delay for each player.
Players can play in the morning at 10am, the afternoon at 1pm, or both!
All sections are non-elimination, and all players participate in all rounds
If you're playing in the Rated sections and have a US Chess ID# and membership, please include it. If you don't have one, we will purchase it for you ($24 value!). If you're not sure what your ID# is you can look it up here
Please arrive 15 minutes before games start. Players who arrive after that may not be placed in quads.
Prices increase by $10 at noon the Tuesday before the tournament.
Questions? Please let us know at Click here to show mail address !

J. Gilligan's Bar and Grill

Event Overview
Speedy - because the time control is G/5;d0 (each player gets 5 minutes to make all their moves.)
Quads - because we divide the players in groups of four based on ratings or skill level.
Players play two games against each of the three other players in their quad.
We hold a Speedy Quads tournament every fourth Monday each month. Speedy Quads has a FREE entry (but we do accept donations to cover the rating fees). There are no prizes. The games are blitz-rated and do not affect regular or quick ratings.
Time Control is G/5;d0; and we play double-round quads.
Register on site only - please arrive before 7:30pm. US Chess members will play rated quads. Non-members will play in an unrated small Swiss blitz tournament.

events.name: 2026 VIRGINIA SENIOR & ADULTS OPEN
events.sourceText:
2026 VIRGINIA SENIOR & ADULTS OPEN
State Championship Event
Country Inn & Suites by Radisson
Friday, May 29, 2026
- Sunday, May 31, 2026
Event Overview
2026 Virginia Senior & Adults Open
AND ADULTS-ONLY BLITZ!!
at the Country Inn & Suites by Radisson
10358 Patriot Hwy, Fredericksburg, VA
Friday - Sunday, May 29 – 31, 2026
Organized by the Virginia Chess Federation
WHAT : The 2026 Virginia Senior and Adults Open Chess Championship, with Saturday night Adults-only Blitz.
WHEN : Friday through Sunday, May 29th – 31st, 2026. Round 1 is at 7 PM on Friday , May 29th.
WHERE : Country Inn & Suites by Radisson, 10358 Patriot Hwy, Fredericksburg, VA
- Hotel rate is $99 per night, plus taxes if reserved by Wednesday, May 27th, 2026. Follow the hotel reservation instructions on the Virginia Chess Federation home page, www.vachess.org .
MAIN TOURNAMENT FORMAT : The main event consists of two sections of play using the Swiss System for pairings:
- Senior Section : Rated by FIDE and US Chess , observing FIDE Rules. Top Virginia player in this section is eligible to represent Virginia at the 2026 John T. Irwin National Tournament of State Senior Champions to be held in Grand Rapids, MI, during the annual U.S. Open Chess Championships. Players must be at least 50 years old as of August 1, 2026 . We use this date because that is the start date of the Irwin Invitational Tournament.
- Under 50 Section : US Chess rated , US Chess rules. For players who are 21 to 49 years old as of August 1, 2026.
- 5 rounds , Swiss System. This is not an elimination event!
- The Time Control for all 5 rounds is Game-90 with 30 seconds of increment for each move. This time control requires all players to take chess notation for the entire game.
- There is a 1-hour “no show/forfeit” rul e in effect. A player who is more than 60 minutes late for the announced start time of any round shall be forfeited for that round.
ADULTS-ONLY BLITZ : Four (4) Double-rounds at a time control of Game 5, Delay 2. Play is in two Sections: Open and Under 1500 . All games will be US Chess rated.
PLAYER ELIGIBILITY :
- Residency Requirements : There are no Virginia residency requirements. This tournament is open to all players who are at least 21 years old as of August 1, 2026 ; no exceptions.
- All players must be current members of the US Chess Federation. Virginia-based players must be current members of the Virginia Chess Federation (VCF). You can join US Chess and/or Virginia Chess at www.vachess.org by selecting the appropriate membership option on our Home Page.
OPTIONAL BYE REQUESTS :
- One half-point Bye is allowed for any round in the Main Tournament (no Bye requests for Blitz). Must be declared by speaking directly with the Chief Arbiter/TD before onsite registration closes at 6:15 pm on Friday May 29th.
- Byes requests and changes for Rounds 2 through 5 must be declared at least ONE HOUR before the start of Round 2. Changes after this deadline will be listed as zero-point byes.
TOURNAMENT SCHEDULE : Both sections follow the same schedule and time controls.
- Friday , May 29th: Round 1 at 7 PM. Pairings will be posted at 6:30 PM.
- Saturday , May 30th: Round 2 at 11 AM, Round 3 at 4 PM. Senior and Adult Blitz will be played on Saturday evening at 9 PM (US Chess rated, Game 5, delay 2, enter online or onsite and see the separate TLA for the Blitz event).
- Sunday , May 31st: Round 4 at 11 AM, Round 5 at 4 PM
- Pairings for Rounds 2-5 will be posted ONE HOUR before the start of the next round. “Tentative Pairings” for the Saturday morning and Sunday morning rounds (Rounds 2 and 4) will be posted the evening prior, but these tentative pairings will be subject to change.
PRIZES : GUARANTEED $4,500 prize fund based on 80 paid players . 1st to 3rd place prize amounts are guaranteed in both sections.
- Senior Section :
+ 1st to 3rd Places: $650, $450, $300. Plaque to the Champion and the Top Virginia player.
+ Top Under 2200: $200 + Plaque
+ Top Under 1800: $165 + Plaque
+ Top Under 1400 / Unrated: $145 + Plaque
+ Top Super Senior (Age 65+): $130 + Plaque
- Under 50 Section :
+ 1st to 3rd Places: $650, $450, $300. Plaque for 1st Place.
+ Top Under 2000: $200 + Trophy
+ Top Under 1700: $165 + Trophy
+ Top Under 1400: $145 + Trophy
+ Top Under 1000: $130 + Trophy
+ Top Unrated: $100 + Trophy
- Both Sections:
+ $75 for the Top Upsets in Rounds 1-2 and Rounds 3-5.
+ An unrated player winning a place prize is limited to $300.
REGISTRATION AND ENTRY FEES :
- Main Tournament ONLINE Entry: Click here to register now!
+ $75 online or US mail by Sunday May 17th.
+ $95 from Monday May 18th through Sunday May 24th. Note that Saturday, May 23rd is the last day to use the US Mail entry option.
+ $105 starting Monday May 25th and at the tournament site. Cash, checks, credit cards, PayPal, Apple Pay accepted onsite.
- Main Tournament ONSITE Entry: Friday, May 29th from 3-6:15 PM. Registration also will be open on Saturday from 8-10 AM for players who want to enter the tournament for Round 2.
- Optional Adults-only Blitz : $25 in advance, $30 onsite at the tournament. We will pay 90% of the Blitz entry fees we receive by section. (For example, if we have 15 entries in the Blitz Open Section, the minimum prize pool will have $338 in cash awards for that section.)
- Entry by US Mail:
+ Send to Mike Hoffpauir, ATTN: VA Sr./U50 Open, 405 Hounds Chase, Yorktown, VA 23693.
+ Print and send us the “mail-in entry form” accessible through the VA Chess Federation ( www.vachess.org ) or include the following information with your mail-in entry: Section, US Chess ID, Bye Requests, mailing address, email address, and phone number. Also be sure to let us know whether you are playing Blitz and provide your Blitz Section! Make your check payable to “VCF” or “VA Chess Federation.”
+ Your Entry is post-marked by Saturday, May 23rd and includes a check written for the proper amount of your entry fees.
+ Do not send any US Mail entries after May 23rd.
- NOTE: We will retain $10 from entries who withdraw before the start of Round 1.
RE-ENTRY : $35 . A player who had a disappointing Round 1 can “re-enter” the tournament for Round 2 and receive a Half-point Bye to replace their Round 1 score. The Round 1 game counts for rating points, but the Round 1 loss is replaced with a Half-point Bye. Re-entry also means that any other half-point bye the player requested for a later round will become 0-point byes unless that player decides to play in that round at the time of re-entering the tournament.
PAIRINGS :
- The Chief Arbiter/TD will use ratings from the US Chess May 2026 Rating Supplement for pairings and prize awards. The May ’26 Rating Supplement is published by US Chess on or about April 19, 2026. Pairings will be made using the higher of each player’s Over-the-Board (OTB) and Online Regular (slow) ratings from the May Rating Supplement unless the Online rating is “stale” compared to the OTB rating.
- Players without a US Chess rating but who have a rating in another system recognized by US Chess (e.g., FIDE, Canada, many foreign countries) will be paired according to the Chief Arbiter/TD’s conversion of their foreign rating. The Chief Arbiter/TD is the final authority for ratings used for each player.
- “Unrated” players are not unrated if they acquire a US Chess or FIDE rating by Thursday, May 28th.
TOURNAMENT EQUIPMENT :
- Chessboards, pieces, and chess clocks will be provided for all games. You may use your own.
- Use of Electronic Scoresheets is not allowed in the Senior Section unless the player has the approval of the Chief Arbiter.
- Health protocols: Masks are optional, but we will have some on hand for anyone who desires to wear one. We also will have ample hand sanitizer and sanitizing wipes.
QUESTIONS? Mike Hoffpauir, VCF, [email protected] , 757-846-4805 (text)

10358 Patriot Highway
Fredericksburg, VA 22408
